Intelligence Brief / N° 127 · HOT · F1

Fluidstack

AI Infrastructure · GPU Cloud / Data-Centre Builder · New York (founded in Oxford, 2017) · Private (~$18B reported; $1.5B round, Sep 2026)

Fluidstack, the Oxford-born AI-infrastructure builder now constructing Anthropic's $50B US data-centre programme, has reportedly closed a $1.5B round led by Jane Street at an $18B valuation (Forbes, 3 Sep 2026), more than doubling the $7.5B mark it set only in July.

76
Opportunity / 100
Timing window
HOT
Series
F1
Recommended team
Atlassian Williams Racing
Action horizon
6-10 WKS

The case

Forbes reported on 3 September that Fluidstack raised $1.5B led by Jane Street at an $18B valuation; Crunchbase News puts total funding just over $2.6B. The company has not announced the round. It closed a ~$750M round at ~$7.5B in July after Bloomberg-sourced talks in April, so the price has more than doubled in two months. The business behind it is real: Anthropic's $50B US infrastructure programme, announced 12 Nov 2025, starts with Fluidstack-built data centres in Texas and New York, with sites coming online through 2026.

The grid has already priced this archetype: CoreWeave became Aston Martin Aramco's Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in May 2025, and Core Scientific sits on Cadillac's first roster. Jane Street is the common thread, having committed billions of compute spend to CoreWeave and Crusoe before backing Fluidstack outright. Fluidstack is the one of the three with no seat, and its anchor customer's brand, Claude, already races on a Williams.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Forbes reported on 3 September that Fluidstack has raised $1.5B led by Jane Street at an $18B valuation; Crunchbase News puts total funding at just over $2.6B. The company has not announced the round itself, so this is reported, not confirmed, and the brief says so.
Price doubled in two months
In April Bloomberg reported Jane Street in talks at an $18B target; Fluidstack instead closed a ~$750M round at ~$7.5B in July. Two months later the $18B print landed. A company re-priced that fast has a story to tell to enterprise buyers, bankers and the public markets, and a budget to tell it with.
The Anthropic build-out
Anthropic's $50B US infrastructure programme, announced 12 November 2025, starts with Fluidstack-built data centres in Texas and New York, with sites coming online through 2026. Each site that goes live is a milestone the partnership can be timed to.
Calendar window
The United States GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026; teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.

Why Atlassian Williams Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, VAST Data for the data platform, Keeper for identity security, Airia and Brillio on the technology side, and Claude as Official Thinking Partner. No cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner: Official AI Compute Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The warm path
Fluidstack builds Anthropic's data centres; Anthropic's Claude has been on the Williams car since the February livery reveal, working with the team's engineers and strategists. The introduction can run through a partner Williams already trusts, and the activation can pair the model with the compute beneath it.
A team that will use the product
Williams' revival is data-led. Elastic GPU capacity for surrogate models, simulation and analytics is consumed in the factory, not just displayed on the car, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
Story and market fit
Oxford-founded, now New York-headquartered: a British origin story for a British team and a US identity for the Austin and Las Vegas rounds where Fluidstack's customers and investors sit.

Audi F1 TeamHewlett Packard Enterprise on the roster in the last 12 months; lane crowded.
TGR Haas F1 Team · Racing BullsOpen but not chosen: neither carries the Anthropic tie that gives Williams a warm path.

Value To Atlassian Williams Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Compute for the work outside the aerodynamic-testing restrictions: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-the-loop and race-strategy simulation, telemetry and video analytics between sessions. Fluidstack supplies it on demand; the team gets capacity it could not fund inside the cost cap.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to CIOs, CFOs and hyperscalers brings a guest list of enterprise buyers, investors and bankers to Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Williams' B2B partners want in the suite.
Content and ecosystem
The model and the compute on one car: co-produced engineering content with the Claude programme, a factory reference customer for Fluidstack's enterprise sales, and a data-centre-to-pit-wall story the team can tell on camera.
What the team gives back
Official AI Compute Partner designation, engine-cover or sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, driver and engineering access for Fluidstack's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Compute Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the Anthropic build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $4-7M a year, part-payable in compute credits. Scope: engine-cover or sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, US-race hospitality, engineering content with the Claude programme.

The askA 25-minute call with Gary Wu before the United States GP to confirm the round on the record, agree an Austin announcement window, and size an Official AI Compute Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Gary Wu
Co-Founder & CEO, Fluidstack · verified
Wu co-founded Fluidstack in Oxford in 2017 and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: César Maklary, Co-Founder and President (commercial), and Rob Perdue, COO since February 2025. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Claude connection.
“Gary, Claude already races on the Williams; you build Anthropic's compute. CoreWeave took its seat at Aston Martin in the year of its listing, and the compute lane at Williams is open. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A reported $1.5B round at $18B, a $50B Anthropic build-out on Fluidstack sites, and Claude already on the Williams put Fluidstack at peak brand-investment authority with a warm path in. The compute lane at Williams is open and two US races remain inside the window.

Crusoe

AI Infrastructure · GPU Cloud / Datacentre Builder · Denver, Colorado · Private (~$30B reported; $3B+ Series F, Sep 2026)

Crusoe, the energy-first AI-infrastructure builder behind OpenAI's 1.2 GW Abilene campus, has reportedly closed a $3B+ Series F at a ~$30B valuation (Bloomberg, 3 Sep 2026), nearly tripling its October 2025 mark, days after a reported ~$13B five-year Jane Street cloud contract.

The case

Crusoe's reported $3B+ Series F at roughly $30B post-money, co-led by Atreides Management and Valor Equity Partners with Mubadala Capital participating, nearly triples the $10B+ valuation set by its $1.375B Series E in October 2025. The company builds and powers gigawatt-scale AI data centres - the first phase of the 1.2 GW Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas is live for Oracle and OpenAI - and sells GPU cloud to OpenAI, Microsoft and Meta. Bloomberg also reports a ~$13B, five-year AI-cloud contract with Jane Street, its highest-profile cloud customer yet.

The grid has already proved this archetype buys F1: CoreWeave signed with Aston Martin Aramco in May 2025 as Official AI Cloud Computing Partner, and Core Scientific joined Cadillac for 2026. Crusoe's closest rival is on the grid and Crusoe is not, and no team carries a brand that owns both halves of the AI build-out, the power and the compute.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Bloomberg reported on 3 September that Crusoe closed more than $3B of Series F capital at roughly $30B post-money, co-led by Atreides Management and Valor Equity Partners with Mubadala Capital participating. That is close to three times the valuation set by its $1.375B Series E in October 2025, and it lands in the same week as a reported ~$13B, five-year AI-cloud contract with Jane Street.
Budget authority
A raise of this size resets the brand and marketing budget for the next 12 to 18 months. With OpenAI, Microsoft, Meta and now Jane Street already on the customer list, the next buyers Crusoe has to reach are enterprise CIOs, CFOs and the capital-markets audience ahead of a probable listing. That is the audience a Formula 1 partnership puts in the room.
Calendar window
The US GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two remaining home-market races of 2026. A partnership agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027; teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter.
Competitive clock
CoreWeave, Crusoe's closest listed rival, has held the Official AI Cloud Computing Partner slot at Aston Martin Aramco since May 2025, and Core Scientific joined Cadillac for 2026. Fluidstack raised a reported $1.5B at an $18B valuation this week and is the next name likely to shop for a grid position. The open cloud-compute lanes will not stay open through 2027.

The open lane
Haas carries no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner. Its technology roster is Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner, Mphasis for digital services and RUCKUS Networks for networking, which leaves Official AI Cloud Compute Partner a clean, ownable category at a team-partner price rather than a title price.
Audience and market fit
Haas is the American privateer in a US-owned sport; Crusoe is a Denver company whose growth story (Abilene, Wyoming, Jane Street) is American. Austin and Las Vegas are US rounds still to come in 2026, and the team's guest lists at those events are the enterprise and capital-markets buyers Crusoe is selling to.
A team that will use the product
Haas is the grid's lean privateer, so it has the most to gain from elastic GPU capacity for simulation, strategy and analytics work. The partnership would be consumed in the factory, not just displayed on the car, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
Precedent and price
CoreWeave's Aston Martin deal proves a neocloud buys Formula 1. The Haas lane comes at a team-partner entry tier, an estimated $5-8M a year and part-payable in compute credits, with sidepod placement and naming of the team's compute environment. The precedent removes the category doubt; the price makes it an easy first commitment.

Octopus Energy Group

Energy Retail & Technology · Renewable Supply, EV Charging, Grid Flexibility · London · Private ($9B, May 2024)

Octopus Energy, Britain's largest household supplier with £13.7bn of revenue and 10 million customers, closed its majority investment in US grid-flexibility company Uplight on 1 September, eight months after selling a $1B stake in Kraken at $8.65B. The most EV-native energy brand has never been on an electric racing car.

The case

On 1 September Octopus Energy Group completed its majority investment in Uplight, which manages 8.5 GW of flexible load for more than 85 US utilities; Schneider Electric stays as minority partner and Nick Chaset runs Uplight alongside Octopus Energy US. It caps a year of capital re-shaping: $850M of the $1B Kraken stake sale (December 2025, $8.65B valuation) went to Octopus, on top of a $9B valuation set by Generation Investment Management and CPP Investments in May 2024. The year to 30 April 2025 brought £13.7bn of revenue, up 10%, and 10 million customers.

The brand is built on electric cars. Electroverse reaches more than 1 million public chargers in over 40 countries, Ford integrated it into its own charging network in September 2025, and more than half of Britain's 653,000 smart EV-tariff customers are with Octopus. It already knows long-term sport: Arsenal's official energy partner since October 2016. What it lacks is a stage where the product is the sport itself.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Octopus Energy Group completed its majority investment in Uplight on 1 September 2026. Uplight stays an independent company, Schneider Electric remains a minority partner, and Nick Chaset becomes Uplight's CEO alongside his role running Octopus Energy US. The stated targets are $1 billion of customer savings and more than doubling flexible capacity to 20 GW over five years.
A year of capital re-shaping
In December 2025 Octopus sold a $1B stake in Kraken at an $8.65B valuation, with $850M of the proceeds going to the group, and set a mid-2026 target for full separation. The group itself was valued at $9B in May 2024 when Generation Investment Management and CPP Investments increased their stakes. A company that has just re-cut its own identity needs a new way to explain itself to customers and investors.
The numbers underneath
In the year to 30 April 2025 Octopus recorded £13.7bn of revenue, up 10%, and grew to 10 million customers, including 7.6m UK homes. It reported a £255m net loss after one-off items, which is why the brief sizes the entry at partner level and includes an in-kind supply component.
Calendar window
Formula E's Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December 2026 and reaches London on 29-30 May 2027. A partnership agreed in the fourth quarter is announced at the season launch and activated in full at the home race.

Why Jaguar Tcs Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Jaguar TCS Racing carries TCS as title and technology partner, Castrol and the Jaguar powertrain. There is no energy retailer, EV-charging or home-energy brand on the roster, so Official Energy Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
Jaguar's relaunch
The road brand is relaunching electric-only in 2026 with its first new car sold from Bond Street, the first of three new electric Jaguars. Every buyer needs a home tariff and a public charging network; Octopus sells both, and Ford has already shown that an OEM will integrate Electroverse into its own charging offer.
Two British electrification stories
Britain's largest household supplier and Britain's electric racing team, with a home race in London. The partnership reads as a national story rather than a badge.
A team that uses its partners
The TCS partnership runs across the team's operations rather than sitting on the car. Octopus's supply, charging and flexibility products fit the same pattern.

An Intelligent Octopus Go plus Electroverse bundle offered to buyers of the new electric Jaguars in the UK, on the model Ford adopted in September 2025, giving the team's parent a customer proposition and Octopus a premium acquisition channel.

A consumer brand with 10 million customers brings a mass audience to the London E-Prix and a hospitality guest list of fleet, utility and government buyers. The Arsenal partnership shows Octopus activates for a decade, not a season.

A $9B energy brand whose product is electric driving, fresh from the Uplight close and the Kraken proceeds, with a proven ten-year sports partnership and no presence in electric racing. Jaguar TCS Racing's energy lane is open and the London E-Prix is its home stage.

Fervo Energy

Clean Firm Power · Enhanced Geothermal · Houston, Texas · Nasdaq: FRVO (IPO 13 May 2026 at $27)

Fervo Energy, the Houston enhanced-geothermal developer that listed on Nasdaq in May in clean energy's largest-ever IPO, signed a 396 MW, 15-year power purchase agreement with Google on 1 September, the biggest enhanced-geothermal deal yet, weeks before its first Cape Station power flows in Utah.

Opportunity / 100
Timing window
HOT
Series
FE
Recommended team

Action horizon
8-14 WKS

The case

Fervo sold 70,000,000 shares at $27 on 13 May 2026, above the marketed range; with the greenshoe the 10-Q puts the raise at 80,500,000 shares and roughly $2.2B gross, and Fortune reported the stock opened about 35% higher, above a $10B value. It is still pre-revenue: Q2 revenue was $113,000 against a $55.9M net loss. What it has is power under contract: a 396 MW, 15-year PPA with Google Energy announced 1 September, expandable to nearly 1 GW by June 2030, and Cape Station Phase I in Utah targeting first power in Q4 2026 on the way to 1.1 GW by 2030.

Formula E is the electrification stage: ABB holds the championship title and Google Cloud, Fervo's anchor customer's sister brand, is a championship partner. On the grid the only power-generation name is Envision Group, which owns Envision Racing; the oil majors sit with DS Penske (TotalEnergies) and the Lola Yamaha ABT team (Shell). No team carries a clean firm-power brand, and the one American team, Andretti, has no energy partner at all.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 1 September Fervo announced a 396 MW, 15-year power purchase agreement with Google Energy for the Cape Station GeoCluster in Utah, signed on 26 August, with an option for Google to take nearly 1 GW by June 2030. It is the largest enhanced-geothermal contract yet, and it arrived less than four months after the company's Nasdaq listing.
From developer to producer
Cape Station Phase I (100 MW) is in commissioning: GeoBlock 1 first power is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, with GeoBlocks 2 and 3 following in early 2027 and Phase II (400 MW) by 2028. A company that has spent nine years drilling becomes a power producer this quarter, which is the moment a brand story is worth paying for.
Budget authority
The IPO raised roughly $2.2B gross (80.5 million shares at $27, greenshoe included). Fervo is still pre-revenue, with Q2 revenue of $113,000 and a $55.9M net loss, so any sponsorship has to be sized as a marketing line, not a vanity line, and pointed at the audiences a newly public company must reach: utilities, hyperscalers, policymakers and public-market investors.
Calendar window
Season 13 opens with a Jeddah double-header on 18-19 December 2026 and Formula E races in Texas for the first time on 6 February 2027 at the Circuit of The Americas, with Miami a fortnight later. Teams close their GEN4 partner rosters in the fourth quarter; a deal agreed before Jeddah can be launched at COTA in front of a home-state audience.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E carries TWG AI as primary partner and Official Artificial Intelligence Partner, plus Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo. There is no energy, power or sustainability partner, so Official Clean Power Partner is an ownable category at a team-partner price on the one team where a Texas company has a home race.
A roster being redrawn
Porsche's powertrain supply ends after Season 12 and Andretti moves to Nissan powertrains for 2026-27 under the GEN4 regulations. A new technical partner, a new car and a fresh livery mean the team is deciding its partner line-up now, which is exactly when a first-time sponsor gets a fair hearing.
Audience and market fit
Andretti is the only American team in the championship, owned by TWG Global, and Formula E's US swing in February 2027 (Austin, then Miami) is the team's home ground. Fervo's buyers and investors are American utilities, hyperscalers and funds; COTA is a two-hour drive from Fervo's Houston headquarters.
Teams ruled out
Envision Racing is owned by Envision Group, a renewables and battery group that would not share the energy lane with a rival generator. DS Penske carries TotalEnergies and Lola Yamaha ABT carries Shell. Jaguar TCS, Nissan, Porsche, Mahindra, Cupra Kiro and Citroën are European or Asian works teams whose partner rosters and audiences give a Houston company no home stage.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

What this is not (Mode B)
Fervo generates electricity for grids and data centres; it does not supply anything a race team consumes. There is no operational workstream, and the OPS FIT score of 10/20 reflects that honestly. The value is brand, audience and content, and each of those has a concrete mechanism below.
Brand and narrative for the team
Official Clean Power Partner gives Andretti a GEN4-era sustainability story that is about firm, round-the-clock power rather than offsets: the car races on electricity, the partner makes it. That is a narrative the team can carry on camera and into the championship's own sustainability programme without inventing anything.
Commercial lift for the team
A newly listed company brings a guest list the team's existing B2B partners want in the suite: utility executives, hyperscaler energy buyers (Google is Fervo's anchor customer and Google Cloud is a championship partner), infrastructure investors and bankers. Hospitality at Austin and Miami turns two US rounds into Fervo's investor and customer days.
Content and what the team gives back
Co-produced content pairing Fervo's drilling engineers with Andretti's race engineers: heat to electrons at Cape Station, braking to charge on a GEN4 car. In return the team provides rear-wing and sidepod placement, the partner designation, COTA and Miami hospitality, driver and engineering access for Fervo's customer and IR channels, and a Google co-activation.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Clean Power Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27-2028/29), spanning Cape Station Phase I and the 2028 Google GeoCluster. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a season at team-partner tier. Scope: rear-wing and sidepod placement, COTA and Miami hospitality, joint content, and a Google co-activation given Google Cloud's championship role.

Opening angle

Lead with the Texas debut.
“Tim, Formula E races in Texas for the first time on 6 February, your first Cape Station power flows this quarter, and the clean-power lane at the only American team is open. 25 minutes before Jeddah to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A May IPO of roughly $2.2B, a 396 MW Google contract signed in August and first Cape Station power due this quarter put Fervo at its brand-building peak as Formula E arrives in Texas. Andretti, the only American team, carries no energy partner and is redrawing its GEN4 livery now.

review.reason: contradicted: The prospect as recorded does not exist. 'Omterra' is the new corporate brand of Siemens Energy ITSELF (and Siemens Gamesa), announced 14 Jul 2026 because the Siemens brand licence from the 2020 spin-off is time-limited; rebranding rolls out in stages from later in 2026. The carve-out is a different thing: on 25 Aug 2026 Siemens Energy's supervisory board approved the legal and operational separation of its Transformation of Industry business area (steam turbines, compressors, electrolysers; ~17,000 employees; ~EUR 5.7B revenue in fiscal 2025; Q3 FY26 revenue EUR 1.5B at 14.3% margin), with options ranging from external investors to a capital-markets transaction and Siemens Energy retaining a significant minority stake; Bloomberg-reported value above EUR 10B; CVC, EQT, Bain, Brookfield and KKR reported as interested. That unit has NO announced name, NO announced chief executive or leadership team of its own, NO brand and NO decided structure (IPO or private-equity sale), so the verified named decision-maker and decision path the standard requires cannot exist yet; the only people to call today are Siemens Energy's board (CEO Christian Bruch) and Anne-Laure de Chammard, listed on Siemens Energy board profiles as Executive Vice President for Transformation of Industry — confirm she leads the carve-out before any contact. Two category hazards for whenever it does surface: on the Formula E side ABB, the championship's title partner, is a direct electrification and grid rival; on the F1 side Siemens AG (a separate company since 2020) is the FIA's Official Digital Twin Sponsor and a McLaren and Ferrari partner, an adjacency the desk must not conflate with the prospect. The Versigent archetype is right and the catalyst is real, so put it on the catalyst radar: re-surface when the carve-out has a name, a CEO and a transaction structure, at which point the born-big spin-off case (new brand from zero, EUR 5.7B revenue) is worth building properly, most likely for F1 given the ABB clash in Formula E.

N° 141 · 05 SEP 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 141 · HOT · FE

Hydrostor

Long-Duration Energy Storage · Advanced Compressed-Air Storage Developer & Operator · Toronto (US HQ Denver, Colorado) · Private ($230M equity, Aug 2026; valuation not stated)

Hydrostor, the Toronto developer of cavern-scale compressed-air storage backed by Goldman Sachs, CPP Investments and Canada Growth Fund, closed a $230M equity investment on 12 August to carry its 500 MW Willow Rock plant in California to financial close this year and its Australian Silver City project into construction.

The case

On 12 August Hydrostor closed a $230M equity investment: the conversion of the note committed by Canada Growth Fund, Goldman Sachs Alternatives and CPP Investments in February 2025, plus a strategic round from Baker Hughes, Realize Capital Partners and Hatch. The new-money share is not broken out. It follows US$55M from Export Development Canada in September 2025 and Baker Hughes' January agreement pairing equity with up to 1.4 GW of equipment orders. The money has a stated job: a 7 GW pipeline and Willow Rock, 500 MW in Kern County, to financial close this year.

This is the half-year in which a developer becomes a builder. Willow Rock holds a California licence granted on 19 December 2025 and a 25-year offtake with Central Coast Community Energy worth about $1B; Silver City in Broken Hill won grid-connection approval on 2 September and is due to start construction. Goderich in Ontario has run commercially since 2020. A company about to pour concrete in two countries needs a public identity it lacks.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Hydrostor closed a $230M equity investment on 12 August 2026. It includes the conversion of the previously announced note from Canada Growth Fund, Goldman Sachs Alternatives and CPP Investments and a strategic equity round from returning investor Baker Hughes and new investors Realize Capital Partners and Hatch. The company does not break out the new-money portion, and the brief says so.
The capital stack behind it
February 2025 brought $200M from the same three institutions ($150M convertible note plus a $50M development loan). Export Development Canada added US$55M in September 2025 for Silver City. In January 2026 Baker Hughes, an investor since 2019, paired an equity investment with up to 1.4 GW of equipment orders. Capital of this quality is what makes a multi-year partnership bankable even without a stated valuation.
Developer to builder
Willow Rock in Kern County, California (500 MW) holds a state licence granted on 19 December 2025, a 25-year offtake with Central Coast Community Energy worth about $1B, and a further 50 MW offtake signed with California Community Power in February 2026; financial close is targeted later in 2026. Silver City in Broken Hill (200 MW) won grid-connection approval on 2 September 2026 and is due to start construction. The first plant, Goderich in Ontario, has operated commercially since 2020.
Calendar window
Formula E's Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December 2026; the Austin E-Prix follows on 6 February and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027. A partnership agreed in the fourth quarter is announced at the season launch and activated in the United States within eight weeks.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E carries TWG AI as primary partner, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo, with Nissan powertrains from Season 13. There is no energy, storage, utility or grid brand on the roster, so Official Energy Storage Partner is a clean category at a partner price.
The American team for a US build-out
Hydrostor's US headquarters is in Denver and its flagship plant is in California. Andretti's Austin and Miami rounds land within weeks of Willow Rock's financial close, in front of the utilities, community-choice buyers and financiers Hydrostor sells to.
Why not the energy team
Envision Racing would be the natural fit, but its title partner Envision Group owns Envision AESC, a maker of grid-storage battery cells with a 60 GWh storage expansion under way. Hydrostor's compressed-air caverns compete with exactly that product.
Story fit
Formula E markets itself as the championship of electrification. Eight-hour storage that firms renewable power is the missing chapter in that story, and Andretti's content programme with TWG AI gives it a home.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Halo, honestly stated (Mode B)
There is no operational workstream: cavern-scale storage has nothing to do on a race car, and the brief does not pretend otherwise. The value is commercial and narrative.
Audience the team wants
Utilities, community-choice aggregators, regulators and project-finance investors are a B2B audience Andretti's hospitality has not yet hosted. Hydrostor brings them to Austin and Miami, and the team's other partners get to meet them.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced content on long-duration storage and grid reliability, a Willow Rock site activation with the team's US partners, and a technology narrative that complements TWG AI rather than competing with it.
What the team gives back
Official Energy Storage Partner designation, car and race-suit placement, Austin and Miami hospitality, driver access, and a platform for Hydrostor's first public brand campaign at the moment its plants become visible.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Energy Storage Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, spanning Willow Rock construction and the first Silver City operations. Estimated $1-2M a season at partner level. Scope: car and suit placement, Austin and Miami hospitality, co-produced content on long-duration storage, and a Willow Rock site activation.

The askA 25-minute call with Curtis VanWalleghem before the Jeddah opener on 18 December to confirm whether a brand budget exists alongside the project capital, and to size an Official Energy Storage Partner entry at Andretti Formula E for Seasons 13-15 timed to Willow Rock's financial close.

Primary decision-maker

Curtis VanWalleghem
Co-Founder & CEO, Hydrostor · verified
VanWalleghem launched Hydrostor in 2010 and fronts every raise, so a first brand partnership is his call. Path: Jon Norman, President; Jordan Cole, Chief Commercial Officer, ex-Brookfield; Beth Summers, Chief Financial Officer. No chief marketing officer is listed, which is itself the opening.

Opening angle

Lead with the construction moment.
“Curtis, Willow Rock closes and Silver City breaks ground in the same quarter Formula E launches Season 13; Andretti is the American team with an open energy lane and Austin and Miami in February. 25 minutes before Jeddah to see whether the timing works?”
Bottom line
A well-backed storage developer at the moment its first two utility-scale plants go to financial close and construction, with no brand, no CMO and no rival storage name on the Andretti roster. Partner-level, halo-honest, timed to the Season 13 launch and two US rounds in February.

Form Energy

Energy Storage · Iron-Air 100-Hour Batteries · Somerville, Massachusetts (factory in Weirton, West Virginia) · Private ($750M Series G, Aug 2026; $1.75B pre-money reported)

Form Energy, the Somerville iron-air battery maker building Google's 30 GWh, 100-hour system in Minnesota, closed a $750M Series G led by T. Rowe Price on 12 August 2026, taking total equity past $2B as its announced backlog jumped from roughly 20 GWh to 80 GWh.

The case

Form announced the $750M Series G on 12 August, led by T. Rowe Price, with Sequoia Capital, Janus Henderson, Franklin Templeton and PEAK6 new to the register. Total equity passes $2B; proceeds scale Form Factory 1 in Weirton, West Virginia. Axios reports the round priced at $1.75B pre-money, down from about $3B in October 2024. The order book explains the investors' patience: an announced backlog of 80 GWh, led by the 300 MW / 30 GWh Google and Xcel Energy system in Minnesota, and 12 GWh for Crusoe's AI data centres.

Weirton is the story a sponsor buys: a 550,000-square-foot battery plant on a former steel-mill site, around 400 people and a planned 500 MW a year by 2028, shipping 100-hour batteries to utilities and hyperscalers. Axios and TechCrunch report a listing being prepared for 2027. A down round is a reason to build the brand, not to hide: the next four quarters decide whether Form is priced as a manufacturer or a technology bet.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Form Energy announced a $750M Series G on 12 August 2026, led by T. Rowe Price, with Sequoia Capital, Janus Henderson, Franklin Templeton and PEAK6 joining existing investors including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Coatue, TPG Rise Climate and GE Vernova. Total equity raised now exceeds $2B. The proceeds scale Form Factory 1 in Weirton, West Virginia, and fund commercial deployments.
A down round, read honestly
Axios reports the round priced at $1.75B pre-money, down from about $3B in October 2024. That is a reason to build the brand rather than a reason to pass: the investors who took the lower price are the ones who want the company recognised as an industrial manufacturer before it lists. Axios and TechCrunch report a listing being prepared for 2027; the brief treats that as reported, not confirmed.
The order book
Announced backlog rose from roughly 20 GWh to 80 GWh. The anchor is the 300 MW / 30 GWh Google and Xcel Energy system at Pine Island, Minnesota, announced in February 2026 as the largest battery system by energy capacity yet announced, with TechCrunch reporting Google paid about $1B. Crusoe signed for 12 GWh at CERAWeek in March 2026 for its AI data centres. Deliveries from Weirton begin in 2027.
Calendar window
Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah double-header on 18-19 December 2026. The new Austin E-Prix at Circuit of The Americas on 6 February 2027 and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027 put an American brand in front of a US audience twice in a month, before any listing roadshow.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E's roster is TWG AI as primary and AI partner, Quest Global for engineering services, Crowe UK for audit and advisory, Reflo for sustainable sportswear and TWG Motorsports as owner, with Nissan powertrains from Season 13. The sponsor table shows no energy, storage or utility brand on the team: Official Energy Storage Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The American team
Andretti is run from Indianapolis, the only US-owned team on the Formula E grid, and its parent TWG Motorsports also operates the Cadillac Formula 1 team with General Motors. A company whose story is a West Virginia steel town rebuilt around batteries belongs on the American car.
Ecosystem overlap
Google Cloud is the championship's technology partner and Google is Form's anchor customer through the Pine Island system. Crusoe, Form's 12 GWh data-centre customer, is itself courting the grid. The paddock Form would join already contains the customers it sells to.
A story the team can tell
Formula E's on-track narrative is energy management. Form's product stores power for a hundred hours to carry a grid through days without wind or sun. The contrast, a forty-five-minute race against a four-day battery, is a content line the team can run all season without inventing a technical link that does not exist.

Honest MODE B halo
An iron-air battery is a grid asset; it will not sit in the garage or power the pit lane. The partnership's value is commercial and should be sold that way: an American storage brand on an American car in a championship built on electrification, in the year before a reported listing.
Commercial lift for the team
Form brings the guest list the team's other partners want to meet: utility executives, state regulators, hyperscaler energy buyers and the bankers around a 2027 listing. Hospitality at Austin and Miami, and a utility-customer programme through TWG Motorsports, turn those guests into pipeline for both sides.
Content and ecosystem
Factory-floor content from Weirton, driver visits to a steel-town plant, co-produced explainers on multi-day storage against race-day energy recovery, and joint activations with the championship's Google Cloud programme where Formula E allows.
What the team gives back
Official Energy Storage Partner designation, sidepod branding, Austin and Miami hospitality, driver and engineering access for Form's channels, and visibility to the capital-markets audience that follows the series.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Energy Storage Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27 to 2028/29), bridging the reported 2027 listing and the first Google and Crusoe deliveries. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year. Scope: sidepod branding, Austin and Miami hospitality, factory and grid content, driver visits to Weirton, and a utility-customer programme through TWG Motorsports.

Mateo Jaramillo
Co-Founder & CEO, Form Energy · verified
Jaramillo co-founded Form in 2017 after helping launch Tesla's Powerwall and fronts every raise. Path: Ted Wiley, Co-Founder, President and COO; Navneet Govil, CFO, formerly of SoftBank Investment Advisers; Wes Sloan, incoming COO from Panasonic Energy. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with Weirton and the listing.
“Mateo, you have 80 GWh of backlog, a steel-town factory and a listing to price. The American Formula E team races in Austin and Miami in February with an open energy lane. 25 minutes to see what a three-season seat costs?”
Bottom line
$750M closed on 12 August, an 80 GWh order book led by Google and Crusoe, a West Virginia factory and a reported 2027 listing: Form Energy needs a national brand within the year and has the story to carry one. Andretti's energy lane is open and two US E-Prix fall in February.

Base Power, the Austin company that installs grid-connected home batteries and sells the electricity behind them, closed a $1B Series D at a $13B post-money valuation on 3 August 2026, up from $4B last October, and launched Base Core, a 39.2 kWh battery built in its own Austin factory.

The case

Base Power announced on 3 August that it had raised a $1B Series D at a $13B post-money valuation, led by Ribbit, Addition, Valor Equity Partners and JPMorganChase's Strategic Investment Group, with Altimeter, Coatue and others alongside. It follows a $1B Series C led by Addition in October 2025 at $4B and a $200M Series B in April 2025; the company says it has raised more than $2.5B. The same release launched Base Core, a 39.2 kWh home battery in production at Base Factory 1 in Austin, with proceeds going to national expansion.

The model is the story: Base sells homeowners a cheap battery and cheap electricity, then dispatches thousands of batteries into the ERCOT market as a virtual power plant. Utilities now buy it wholesale, with CoServ signing for 100 MW across North Texas in March 2026, and Illinois opened on 24 June in ComEd territory. The all-electric championship arrives in Base's own city in February, with the money for a national launch already in the bank.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Base Power announced on 3 August 2026 a $1B Series D at a $13B post-money valuation, led by Ribbit, Addition, Valor Equity Partners and JPMorganChase's Strategic Investment Group. The company says it has raised more than $2.5B in total. This is company-announced, not press-reported: the release is on Business Wire and was covered the same day by TechCrunch.
Valuation tripled in ten months
The Series C of October 2025, $1B led by Addition, valued the company at $4B; the Series D puts it at $13B. A company re-priced that fast has a story to tell to homeowners, utilities and the public markets, and the release earmarks the money for taking Base Core to more homes and expanding nationally.
A product to launch
Base Core is a 39.2 kWh home battery designed and built at Base Factory 1 in Austin, available in Texas and Illinois. Sponsorship works hardest when there is a new product to put in front of people, and Base has one arriving state by state through the Season 13 calendar.
Calendar window
Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026. The Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027 is a race in Base's home city, and the Miami E-Prix follows on 20 February. Teams close their Season 13 partner rosters in the autumn, so a deal agreed in the next six to ten weeks can launch at the first US round.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E carries TWG AI as primary partner and Official AI Partner, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo, with Nissan supplying the GEN4 powertrain from Season 13. There is no energy, battery, storage or utility partner on the roster, and none at any other Formula E team: Official Energy Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The American team
Andretti is the American entry in an otherwise European and Asian grid, owned by TWG Motorsports. The Austin and Miami weekends are its home rounds as much as Base's, and an Austin company on an American car in Austin is the story local and national media will write.
A route to Formula 1
TWG Motorsports' parent, TWG Global, also fields the Cadillac F1 Team with General Motors. A Formula E entry that proves itself at the US rounds gives Base a relationship with the same owner when its footprint and budget justify Formula 1, without paying F1 prices for a two-state consumer brand today.
Audience fit
Formula E's partners are ABB, DHL, Julius Baer, Google Cloud and PIF: an electrification and sustainability audience. Base sells grid resilience to homeowners and dispatchable capacity to utilities such as CoServ, and its Head of Policy, Travis Kavulla, is a former state regulator; the series' hospitality is where those utility and policy conversations happen.

Base Core units powering the team's hospitality and fan zone at the Austin and Miami weekends, as a live demonstration of the product rather than a logo: the same battery that backs up a Texas home backing up the garage's guests.

Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to utilities, home builders and regulators brings a guest list of co-op executives, policy makers and investors to Austin and Miami, the audience a team's other B2B partners want in the suite.
What the team gives back
Official Energy Partner designation, livery and race-suit placement, naming of the home-race hospitality, Base Core demonstrations at the US rounds, driver and team content for the Texas and Illinois markets, and an introduction to the Cadillac F1 Team through TWG.

Entry as Official Energy Partner. THREE YEARS, Season 13 to Season 15, covering the national roll-out and a probable listing window. Zach Dell
Co-Founder & CEO, Base Power · verified
Dell co-founded Base in Austin in 2023 after Blackstone and Thrive Capital and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Justin Lopas, Co-Founder and COO (ex-SpaceX, Anduril), and Zina Bash, Chief Legal Officer since January 2026. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Lead with the home race.
“Zach, the Austin E-Prix is on 6 February and Andretti's roster has no energy partner. You just raised $1B to take Base national, and the all-electric series lands in your city first. 25 minutes to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $1B round at $13B, more than $2.5B raised, a factory-built product to launch nationally and a home race in Austin on 6 February 2027 put Base Power at peak brand-investment authority. Andretti's energy lane is open and both US rounds fall inside the window.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 130 · 05 SEP 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 130 · HOT · FE

Zenobē

Fleet Electrification · Electric Buses, Charging & Grid Storage · London (North American HQ Chicago) · Private (KKR / Infracapital; c.£980M financing, Jun 2026)

Zenobē, the London fleet-electrification and grid-battery operator owned by KKR and Infracapital, secured c.£980M of new financing on 15 June 2026 to put 1,200 more electric buses on UK and Irish roads, taking capital raised past £3.2B, then added a $400M Australasian platform and a German acquisition within six weeks.

The case

Zenobē announced on 15 June that 22 banks, NatWest, Lloyds, Santander and Aviva among them, had committed c.£980M to its UK and Ireland electric-fleet facility: £480M of long-dated term debt, a £400M capex line and £100M of ancillaries. Capital raised since 2017 now exceeds £3.2B. Nine days later it closed a $400M platform for zero-emission fleets in Australia and New Zealand, and on 27 July it bought Bavaria's sdp energie with a 1.75 GW German battery pipeline. KKR and Infracapital have been joint majority owners since a c.£870M equity round in September 2023.

This is a company that has already paid for motorsport in kind: its second-life bus-battery powerskids were Extreme E's official energy-storage supply from the series' first season to its final event in October 2025. With Extreme E gone, that budget line is orphaned. Zenobē now sells fleet electrification to bus operators in Britain, Europe, North America and Australasia, and the buyers it needs are transport authorities, fleet owners and the banks that fund them.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 15 June 2026 Zenobē announced c.£980M of new financing for its UK and Ireland electric-fleet facility, the facility's third round: £480M of new long-dated term commitments, a £400M capital-expenditure facility and £100M of ancillaries from 22 banks including NatWest, Lloyds, Santander and Aviva. It funds more than 1,200 new electric buses and their charging over three years and takes capital raised since 2017 past £3.2B.
Three financings in six weeks
Nine days after the UK round, Zenobē closed a $400M platform for zero-emission heavy-vehicle fleets across Australia and New Zealand, seeded with four operating depots. On 27 July it bought Bavaria's sdp energie and with it a 1.75 GW pipeline of transmission-connected battery projects in Germany. Combined with the €325M European facility, the company expects to support up to 5,000 electric buses by 2028. A company scaling on four continents at once is at the point where a global brand gets built.
A motorsport budget with nowhere to go
Zenobē was Extreme E's Official Energy Storage Supplier from the series' first season in 2021, powering remote paddocks with powerskids built from second-life bus batteries. Extreme E ran its farewell event in October 2025. The company has proved it will fund motorsport and has just lost the property it funded; Formula E is the obvious successor and the powerskid story transfers intact.
Calendar window
Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah double-header on 18-19 December 2026. The London E-Prix moves from ExCeL to Brands Hatch on 29-30 May 2027, a new home for the reigning champions' home race, about forty miles from Zenobē's London office and within reach of every UK bus operator it sells to.

Why Jaguar Tcs Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Jaguar TCS Racing's roster in the sponsor table is TCS as title partner and Castrol, with Jaguar as powertrain supplier and parent; the team's own partner page adds Wolfspeed, Reflo, OpenText, Dow and Chase. None is a fleet-electrification, charging or energy-storage brand. Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The champions
Jaguar TCS Racing won the 2025/26 Teams' World Championship at the London finale with Mitch Evans and António Félix da Costa, 17 points clear of Porsche, and is committed to the GEN4 era through 2030 under team principal Ian James. A partner joining for Season 13 joins the reigning champions in the first year of a new car.
British on British
Zenobē is London-headquartered and Britain's largest owner and operator of transmission-connected batteries; Jaguar TCS Racing is run from Kidlington, Oxfordshire. The Brands Hatch home race puts both in front of the transport authorities, bus operators and lenders that decide Zenobē's UK pipeline.
Fleet customers in common
Jaguar's parent sells vehicles to the same fleet buyers Zenobē electrifies. A joint proposition to fleet owners, vehicle plus depot plus charging plus finance, is a commercial programme the team's parent can carry beyond the racetrack.

Value To Jaguar Tcs Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Second-life battery powerskids for the team's garage and hospitality load at European rounds, subject to the championship's event-power rules, replacing generator diesel with a visible, on-camera story. Zenobē ran exactly this for five Extreme E seasons.
Depot and fleet electrification
Zenobē's fleet-as-a-service model, vehicles, chargers, batteries and finance, applied to the team's Kidlington base and support fleet, giving the champions a measured emissions reduction they can report and Zenobē a reference site.
Commercial lift for the team
Zenobē brings bus operators, transport authorities, city officials and the 22 banks behind its facility to Brands Hatch and Berlin; a guest list that overlaps with the public-sector and financial audience TCS and Chase already court.
What the team gives back
Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner designation, sidepod branding, Brands Hatch and Berlin hospitality, paddock-power content, and driver access for Zenobē's customer events in the UK, Europe, North America and Australasia.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27 to 2028/29), from the GEN4 debut through the first two Brands Hatch home races. Estimated £1-2M a year, part-payable in powerskid supply and depot electrification. Scope: sidepod branding, Brands Hatch and Berlin hospitality, paddock-power content, and a bus-operator guest programme.

The askA 25-minute call with Donald Weir before the Jeddah opener to confirm the financing and the Extreme E budget history on the record, agree a Brands Hatch announcement window, and size an Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner entry at Jaguar TCS Racing for Seasons 13-15.

Primary decision-maker

Donald Weir
Chief Executive Officer, Zenobē · verified
Weir joined Zenobē as CEO in 2025; a first Formula E partnership is his call. Path: Steven Meersman, Co-Founder and Director, EV Fleet; Tim Boothman, Chief Commercial Officer, Electric Fleet; Iain Wetherall, CFO, formerly CFO of Wizz Air. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with Extreme E and Brands Hatch.
“Donald, Zenobē powered Extreme E's paddock for five seasons and that series has gone. The reigning Formula E champions race at Brands Hatch next May with no fleet or storage partner on the car. 25 minutes to see what the seat costs?”
Bottom line
£980M closed in June, a $400M Australasian platform and a German acquisition inside six weeks, five seasons of paying for motorsport at Extreme E, and a home race at Brands Hatch in May: Zenobē has the budget, the habit and the stage. The fleet and storage lane at Jaguar TCS Racing is open.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 233 · 03 SEP 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 233 · HOT · FE

Oura Health

Consumer Health Technology · Smart Ring / Recovery Data · San Francisco (founded in Oulu, Finland) · Private (Nasdaq: OURA filed, 3 Sep 2026)

Oura filed a public Form S-1 with the SEC on 3 September for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker OURA, disclosing $1.4B of trailing-twelve-month revenue at $59M of net profit. The Official Wearable of Team USA holds no motorsport property.

The case

Oura filed its public S-1 on 3 September for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker OURA, led by Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Allen & Company and Jefferies. The filing shows $1.21B of revenue for the nine months to 30 June 2026, up 74% from $697.6M, five million paid members against 2.5 million a year earlier, and $1.4B of trailing-twelve-month revenue at $59M of net profit. TechCrunch reported on 24 August that the listing could value the company above $16B, against $11B at last October's Series E.

Human performance is already a priced category in motorsport: WHOOP has joined Scuderia Ferrari's roster and Eight Sleep has joined Aston Martin Aramco's. Oura has been buying elite sport at pace - Official Wearable of Team USA and the LA28 Games in February, of U.S. Soccer and its 27 national teams in April, and of the US Open on a five-year USTA agreement. Motorsport is the one arena it does not hold.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

The trigger
Oura Inc. filed a public Form S-1 with the SEC on 3 September 2026 for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker OURA. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Allen & Company and Jefferies lead the offering, with around a dozen further banks named. A confidential draft was submitted on 21 May 2026; this is the public step, and it is the reason the company is in front of every institutional investor in the country this month.
The numbers the filing put on the record
Revenue of $1.21B for the nine months to 30 June 2026, up 74% from $697.6M a year earlier. Trailing-twelve-month revenue of $1.4B at $59M of net profit. Five million paid members against 2.5 million a year earlier, and 3.6 million rings sold over twelve months. The nine-month loss attributable to common stockholders of $924.3M is an accounting artefact of a $985.0M deemed dividend to preferred holders, not trading performance.
The re-pricing
The Series E in October 2025 raised more than $900M at an $11B valuation, led by Fidelity with ICONIQ, Whale Rock and Atreides - double the $5B set at the Series D in December 2024. TechCrunch reported on 24 August that the listing could value Oura above $16B. That figure is reported, not confirmed, and no price range is set in the filing.
The calendar
Formula E opens Season 13 at the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026 and runs 21 races across 13 cities to July 2027. Teams close Season 13 partner rosters through the autumn. A deal agreed in the listing quarter can be announced after the bell and activated for the Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027 and the Miami E-Prix two weeks later.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

An empty category across a whole championship
The sponsor table shows no wearable, health-technology or recovery partner on any 2026 Formula E roster. On the Formula 1 grid the same lane is filling fast - WHOOP at Scuderia Ferrari, Eight Sleep at Aston Martin Aramco. Official Health Technology Partner is therefore available in Formula E as a clean, ownable designation rather than a contested one.
The American entry, for an American listing
Andretti Formula E is the US team on the grid, run under TWG Global with TWG AI as primary partner of the Formula E programme and Official Artificial Intelligence Partner of Andretti Global since 2026, alongside Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo. Season 13 gives it two home rounds, Austin and Miami, which is where a newly Nasdaq-listed consumer brand wants its hospitality.
It sits inside the portfolio Oura already owns
Oura is Official Wearable of Team USA and the LA28 Games and of U.S. Soccer's 27 national teams, and holds a five-year USTA agreement covering the US Open. A three-year Formula E term running to LA28 is the same audience and the same message, extended to the one arena the shelf is missing.
Why Formula E and not Formula 1
Three reasons, stated plainly. The Formula 1 human-performance lane is taken at the two teams that fit. Oura's own Formula 1 history sits at Red Bull Racing, which is not on its 2026 roster, so a return means re-opening a lapsed relationship or partnering a direct rival of it. And Formula E's price for a category-defining designation is a fraction of Formula 1's, which matters in the first budget cycle after a listing.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Season 13 is 21 races in 13 cities on four continents between December and July. The limiting factor for drivers, race engineers and travelling crew across that schedule is sleep debt and circadian disruption, not fitness. Oura Ring gives the team's performance staff readiness, sleep-stage, heart-rate-variability and body-temperature data per person per day - the same instrumentation Oura supplies to Team USA and supplied to Red Bull Racing's drivers and pit crew from 2020.
What the team can do with it
Travel and training plans built on measured recovery rather than assumption; a documented readiness protocol for a double-header weekend; an early-warning signal on illness in a travelling party of dozens. In a cost-capped, weight-sensitive series, a partner whose product is consumed by the people rather than the car is one the team can adopt without engineering trade-offs.
Commercial and content lift
Oura brings a five-million-member consumer base and a marketing organisation that has just spent a year activating Olympic, soccer and tennis properties. For Andretti that is retail reach, a co-branded content series on human performance in motorsport, and a partner whose brand is welcome in exactly the health-and-wellness territory Formula E's audience skews toward.
What the team gives back
Official Health Technology Partner designation, sidepod and race-suit placement, naming of the team's readiness programme, driver and engineer access for Oura's channels, and hospitality at the Austin E-Prix and the Miami E-Prix for Oura's retail partners and new public-market investors.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Health Technology Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, carrying through to the LA28 Games. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in product. Scope: sidepod and race-suit placement, naming of the team's readiness programme, US-round hospitality, performance content.

The askA 25-minute call with Doug Sweeny in the listing quarter to size an Official Health Technology Partner entry at Andretti Formula E against Season 13, agree an announcement window after the bell, and put a readiness pilot in front of the team's performance staff before the Austin E-Prix.

Primary decision-maker

Doug Sweeny
Chief Marketing Officer, Oura Health · verified
Sweeny owns the sports portfolio that bought Team USA, U.S. Soccer and the US Open; he came from Levi's, Nest and One Medical. Path: Tom Hale, chief executive since March 2022, who took Momentive public in 2018, and Sean Brecker, CFO. No president is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the listing, not the ring.
“Doug, you own Team USA, U.S. Soccer and the US Open, and nothing in motorsport. No Formula E team carries a wearable partner, and Andretti runs the Austin E-Prix and the Miami E-Prix before LA28. 25 minutes?”
Bottom line
A public S-1 on 3 September, $1.4B of trailing revenue and a reported listing above $16B put Oura at the point where a newly listed consumer brand writes its next marketing plan. It has bought Team USA, U.S. Soccer and the US Open and owns nothing in motorsport, and no Formula E team carries a wearable partner.

Risks & counters

A LIVE OFFERING
The S-1 is on file and pricing is weeks away; new multi-year commitments are hard to sign while an offering is in the market. Counter: Use the window to agree heads of terms for announcement after the bell - the filing is the reason to call now.
A FULL SPORTS SHELF, AND A LAPSED F1 DEAL
Team USA, LA28, U.S. Soccer and a five-year USTA agreement are already bought, and the 2020 Red Bull Racing partnership is not on Red Bull's 2026 roster. Counter: Pitch motorsport as the gap in the shelf, not a fifth of the same; the lapsed deal proves a top team deployed the product, and Formula E costs a fraction.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 234 · 25 AUG 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 234 · HOT · FE

Gatik

Autonomous Freight · Middle-Mile Driverless Trucking · Santa Clara, California · Private ($200M Series D, Aug 2026)

Gatik announced a $200M Series D on 25 August, co-led by the Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, on more than $600M of contracted driverless freight. A direct peer already runs on a Formula 1 car; no Formula E team carries an autonomy partner.

71
Opportunity / 100
Timing window
HOT
Series
FE
Recommended team
Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team
Action horizon
6-10 WKS

The case

Gatik announced $200M of Series D financing from Santa Clara on 25 August, co-led by the Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, with Millennium Management, ARK Invest and Intact Private Capital following. The company reports more than $600M of contracted revenue, 85,000 completed fully driverless orders and 99% on-time delivery, moving ambient, refrigerated and frozen goods between distribution centres and stores for Walmart, Kroger and PepsiCo. It is targeting more than 100 driverless trucks by the end of 2026.

Motorsport has priced this category once already. In November 2024 Zoox, Amazon's robotaxi business, became an Official Regional Partner of Atlassian Williams Racing in Formula 1's first autonomous-vehicle partnership, running on the car at that team's American races. It answers the obvious objection - that a safety-first autonomy company has no business in racing - because a direct peer made the argument first, and won it.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

The trigger
Gatik announced $200M of Series D financing on 25 August 2026 from its Santa Clara headquarters, co-led by the Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, with Millennium Management, ARK Invest and Intact Private Capital participating. Both Gatik's and QIA's own newsrooms carry it, so the round is company-confirmed rather than reported.
The business under the round
Gatik states more than $600M of contracted revenue, 85,000 completed fully driverless orders and 99% on-time delivery. Its network is the middle mile: ambient, refrigerated and frozen goods on high-frequency regional routes between distribution centres and stores for Walmart, Kroger and PepsiCo. These are the company's own figures from its release, not audited accounts.
The production clock
Isuzu put $30M into Gatik in 2024 and the two are jointly developing a chassis built for a Level 4 system, running on NVIDIA compute, targeting mass production from 2027. Gatik is aiming for more than 100 driverless trucks by the end of 2026 and thousands beyond that. A brand programme agreed now runs into that ramp rather than trailing it.
The calendar
Formula E teams close Season 13 rosters through the autumn. The season opens at the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026 and runs 21 races across 13 cities, with the Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027, the Miami E-Prix two weeks later and the Tokyo E-Prix closing on 24-25 July 2027.

Why Lola Yamaha Abt — the open lane, the audience, the platform

An empty category, and a proven one
The sponsor table shows no autonomy, ADAS or autonomous-vehicle partner on any 2026 Formula E roster. In Formula 1 the same category is already sold: Zoox has been an Official Regional Partner of Atlassian Williams Racing since November 2024, in what both parties called Formula 1's first autonomous-vehicle partnership. The archetype is proven and the Formula E version of it is unsold.
The thinnest technology roster on the grid
Lola Yamaha ABT's major partners are Castore, OMP and Shell - sportswear, race suits and lubricants - beside the Lola Cars, Yamaha and ABT Sportsline parents. There is no software, data, AI or technology partner. That means an autonomous-technology designation is available as a first rather than as an addition, and the partner sits beside a constructor brand rather than behind a car marque.
No manufacturer conflict
Gatik's chassis partner and investor is Isuzu, which is co-developing the Level 4 truck for 2027. That rules out the Formula E entries fronted by commercial-vehicle makers - Nissan, Mahindra, Citroen and Cupra Kiro through the Volkswagen Group - because Isuzu could reasonably object to its autonomy partner branding a rival manufacturer's works team. Lola is a constructor, ABT is an operator and Yamaha builds engines and components, so none of them competes with Isuzu.
Why Formula E and not Formula 1
Three reasons. The Formula 1 autonomy lane is held by a direct peer at Williams, so entering Formula 1 means either following Zoox or partnering a team that has already been passed over for it. Formula E races on city streets, which is where public and regulatory acceptance of driverless vehicles is actually contested. And a Formula E designation is affordable for a company whose $200M round is earmarked for fleet and safety validation, which a Formula 1 team-major position is not.

Value To Lola Yamaha Abt — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Mode B, stated honestly
There is no operational workstream here and the brief does not pretend otherwise. No Formula E team will deploy an autonomous middle-mile freight stack, and any claim that it would is a claim 1440 will not make. What follows is what the partnership actually delivers on both sides.
What the team gets
Its first technology partner and a designation it has never sold, at a moment when its commercial roster is three consumer-goods brands. A co-produced engineering content strand pairing Lola's constructor heritage and Yamaha's powertrain work with a driverless-freight story that reads as engineering rather than advertising. And a partner whose growth is contracted rather than speculative.
What Gatik gets
A category designation nobody else in autonomous freight holds. Hospitality at the Austin, Miami and Tokyo rounds for the retail and CPG buyers it sells to - Walmart, Kroger and PepsiCo all operate at scale in those markets - and for QIA, Koch, ARK and Millennium on the investor side. A recruiting channel into perception, controls and simulation engineering, where motorsport and autonomy hire from the same pool.
The commercial shape
Official Autonomous Technology Partner, three years across Seasons 13 to 15 so the term covers the Isuzu mass-production launch in 2027. Estimated at $1.5-3M a year - an estimate, not a quoted price. Scope: sidepod and halo placement, naming rights on the team's data and simulation programme, hospitality at the US and Tokyo rounds, and joint engineering content.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Autonomous Technology Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, running to the Isuzu mass-production launch. Estimated $1.5-3M a year. Scope: sidepod and halo placement, naming rights on the team's data and simulation programme, US and Tokyo hospitality, joint engineering content.

The askA 25-minute call with Gautam Narang inside the post-round budget cycle to test whether Gatik wants a visible brand at all, and if so to size an Official Autonomous Technology Partner entry at Lola Yamaha ABT against Season 13, with activation aimed at the Austin E-Prix and the Miami E-Prix.

Primary decision-maker

Gautam Narang
CEO & Co-Founder, Gatik · verified
Narang co-founded Gatik with Arjun Narang and Apeksha Kumavat and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Paul Dilaura, chief commercial officer, who owns commercial spend, and Patrick Archambault, chief financial officer. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with Zoox, not with the trucks.
“Gautam, Zoox took Formula 1's first autonomous-vehicle seat at Williams in 2024. No Formula E team has sold one yet and it costs a fraction of that. 25 minutes to look at the Lola Yamaha ABT numbers?”
Bottom line
A $200M Series D on 25 August, more than $600M of contracted revenue and a direct peer already running on a Formula 1 car put Gatik at the moment an autonomy brand decides whether to become visible. Formula E has never sold an autonomy seat, and the Lola Yamaha ABT roster carries no technology partner at all.

Risks & counters

OFF-BRAND RISK
A driverless-freight company's proposition is that its trucks are unexciting and safe. Racing says the opposite, and no autonomy peer but Zoox has bought motorsport. Counter: Zoox answered it in Formula 1. Buy the engineering story - perception, simulation, validation - and activate at the rounds where the customers already are.
THE MONEY IS SPOKEN FOR
The $200M was raised to put 100+ driverless trucks on the road by the end of 2026 and reach mass production with Isuzu in 2027, not to buy brand. Counter: Formula E prices the designation at a fraction of Formula 1, and a three-year term spreads it across the production ramp.

The case

Emerald AI raised a $150M oversubscribed Series A on 25 Aug 2026, valuing the grid-flexibility software company at $1.05B and lifting total capital raised past $220M. Energize Capital and DCVC co-led the round, joined by NVIDIA, Siemens, GE Vernova, RWE, Aramco Ventures and Samsung Ventures — twelve Fortune Global 500 companies now hold equity. The raise marks a BRAND RECKONING moment: Emerald moves from demonstration pilots to multi-megawatt, full data-center-scale commercial deployment, and needs a visibility platform to match its new enterprise-trust ambitions.

No F1 or Formula E grid-flexibility sponsor exists on either grid, leaving the energy-management category entirely open. As hyperscalers and utilities scrutinize Emerald's enterprise credentials, a global motorsport platform offers scale-validation no single-utility pilot can match. The slot that matches Emerald's grid-flex narrative architecturally is open at Nissan Formula E Team.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger

Open lane
Nissan Formula E Team carries no grid-flexibility or energy-management partner today, leaving a category lane open on an EV-native grid with no direct precedent among rival teams.

Formula E's urban, sustainability-literate fanbase and Nissan's global EV customer base overlap directly with the utility and hyperscaler executives Emerald is courting for its next contract cycle.

Nissan's factory operations, simulator facilities and race-weekend garage infrastructure give Emerald live surfaces to demonstrate real-time grid-flex software beyond a logo placement.

Emerald AI just banked $150M at a $1.05B valuation with zero motorsport visibility to match its ambition.

Databricks announced on 13 August that it had closed a $5B strategic round at a $190B valuation, led by Coatue, with Blackstone, MGX and T. Rowe Price accounts, and new money from Sixth Street Growth, Point72, Premji Invest and TPG. Its own release puts the revenue run-rate past $7B at more than 80% growth. Enterprise data brands already treat motorsport as a proven channel, and the Formula 1 grid is close to sold: Oracle at Oracle Red Bull Racing, SAP at Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team, Splunk at McLaren F1 Team, IBM at Scuderia Ferrari, VAST at Atlassian Williams Racing, CoreWeave at Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team. On the Formula E grid, six of the ten entries carry no data, AI or software partner at all.

The trigger
Databricks closed a $5B strategic funding round at a $190B valuation, announced on 13 August 2026. Coatue led, with Blackstone, MGX and accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates and T. Rowe Price Investment Management; new investors included Sixth Street Growth, BOND, Clearlake Capital, Point72, Premji Invest and TPG, with Andreessen Horowitz, Dragoneer, Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Thrive Capital following on. The company's own newsroom carries it, so this is company-confirmed rather than reported.
The business under the round
Databricks put its revenue run-rate past $7B with more than 80% year-on-year growth, and directed the capital at the Unity AI Gateway, Lakebase and Genie - the products for building and managing enterprise AI agents. These are the company's own figures from its own release, not audited accounts, and the brief attributes them that way.
A re-pricing, not a listing
The $190B mark is about 42% above the $134B Series L set six months earlier. Ali Ghodsi said in June 2026 that this is a poor year to go public, and no public or confidential S-1 had been filed as of mid-August, with a listing widely expected in 2027 or later. That matters commercially: there is no quiet period and no roadshow, so a multi-year brand commitment can be signed now rather than deferred.
The calendar
Formula E teams close Season 13 rosters through the autumn. Season 13 is the first season of the GEN4 regulations - the championship's largest technical reset - opening at the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026 and running 21 races across 13 cities, with the Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027, the Miami E-Prix two weeks later and the Tokyo E-Prix closing on 24-25 July 2027.

The Formula 1 lane is bought; the Formula E lane is not

Value To Nissan Formula E Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Formula E is decided by energy management: a fixed allocation per race, attack mode, regeneration and the slipstream, resolved by whoever models consumption and rivals' strategies best. A lakehouse unifying telemetry, energy, tyre, weather and timing data, with machine-learning models run between sessions and on the pit wall, is that lever. Unlike Formula 1 there is no aerodynamic-testing restriction shaping where a team may spend its effort, so the software lever is comparatively larger.
The GEN4 reset makes it worth more
Season 13 is the first season of GEN4. Every energy model, tyre model and strategy assumption a team holds is rebuilt from a smaller base of data. A partner that arrives at the start of that cycle is embedded in how the team learns the new car, which is a far stronger position than joining a settled formula, and it is why the timing rather than the money is the argument.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner selling to chief data officers and chief information officers brings a guest list of enterprise buyers to the Austin, Miami and Tokyo rounds, and a co-produced engineering content strand that gives the team technical credibility rather than another logo. For a works team whose commercial roster is thin outside the manufacturer, a category-defining technology partner is a signal to the rest of the market.
What the team gives back
Official Data and AI Partner designation, sidepod and halo placement, naming of the team's data environment, engineer and driver access for Databricks' channels, hospitality at the US and Tokyo rounds, and a joint programme with Nissan's own data organisation - the part of the deal that makes it defensible to a chief financial officer.

Entry as Official Data and AI Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, covering the GEN4 cycle. Estimated $3-6M a year, part-payable in platform credits. Scope: sidepod and halo placement, naming of the team's data environment, and a joint programme with Nissan's own data organisation.

The askA 25-minute call with Rick Schultz before Formula E teams close Season 13 rosters, to size an Official Data and AI Partner entry at Nissan Formula E Team across the GEN4 cycle, agree how the designation is scoped against the championship's own cloud partner, and put an energy-modelling proof of concept in front of the team's race engineers.

Rick Schultz
Chief Marketing Officer, Databricks · verified
Schultz has run Databricks' marketing since March 2017, after leading marketing at Alteryx through its listing; brand and sponsorship sit with him. Path: Ali Ghodsi, co-founder and chief executive since 2016, and Ion Stoica, co-founder and executive chair.

Opening angle

Lead with the grid map.
“Rick, Oracle, SAP, Splunk, IBM and VAST have each bought a Formula 1 team. Six of the ten Formula E entries have no data partner at all, and Nissan holds a drivers' title. 25 minutes before the rosters close?”
Bottom line
A $5B round closed at $190B on 13 August, a revenue run-rate past $7B growing more than 80% a year, and no listing to wait for. The Formula 1 data lane is bought at every team a brand this size would want, six of the ten Formula E entries carry no data partner, and the works team that holds a drivers' title has an open enterprise-software lane.

The case

Lovable confirmed on 12 August a $400M Series C at $13.3B, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, with Balderton, Kaszek, Tencent and Regent joining and Accel, CapitalG, DST and Salesforce Ventures returning. The price has doubled since the $330M Series B at $6.6B on 18 December 2025. The company says revenue run rate passed $500M in June and should reach about $600M by end-August; more than 60 million projects have been built on the platform and its apps draw over 900 million visits a month.

The money is earmarked for scale and for America: Stockholm stays headquarters while offices open in San Francisco, New York and Boston, with about 450 hires planned this year and a chief marketing officer already based in San Francisco. A brand whose customers are founders and business owners in 150 countries now needs a stage those customers watch. It has never bought sport; the first seat is the one that defines the category.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 12 August Lovable announced a $400M Series C at a $13.3B valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, and confirmed the same day by TechCrunch and Bloomberg. The company's own release is the primary source; the run-rate figures in it are company-stated and unaudited.
Price doubled in eight months
The Series B of 18 December 2025 raised $330M at $6.6B; the Series A in July 2025 was $200M at $1.8B. A company re-priced from $1.8B to $13.3B in thirteen months has a story to tell to founders, enterprise buyers and, in time, public-market investors, and a budget to tell it with.
The US build-out
Stockholm remains headquarters, but the round funds offices in San Francisco, New York and Boston and about 450 hires this year. The chief marketing officer is already based in San Francisco. A brand moving its marketing centre of gravity to America needs American reach; F1's US rounds are the most concentrated business audience in sport.
Calendar window
The Dutch and Italian GPs open the run-in after the summer break; the United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American stages left in 2026. Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 148 · 07 AUG 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 148 · HOT · F1

Firmus Technologies

AI Infrastructure · Liquid-Cooled NVIDIA AI Factories · Singapore (founded in Sydney, 2019); AI Factories in Tasmania · Private (>$10.5B post-money; ASX listing targeted Q4 2026)

Firmus, the Sydney-founded builder of liquid-cooled NVIDIA AI Factories on Tasmanian hydro power, announced a fully subscribed $2B strategic equity round on 7 August at a post-money valuation above $10.5B, backed by Coatue, NVIDIA, Blackstone and Jane Street, with an ASX listing targeted for the fourth quarter.

72
