The case

The round is company-announced: $2B of equity from Coatue, NVIDIA, funds managed by Blackstone and Jane Street, taking new equity raised in the past year past $3B and the valuation from $5.5B in April to more than $10.5B. Beneath it sits a $10B debt facility led by Blackstone and Coatue, signed in February, for Project Southgate: liquid-cooled AI Factories in Tasmania, 36,000 NVIDIA GPUs at the Launceston site, and a 170,000-GPU campus in Batam, Indonesia, from the first quarter of 2027, against which Firmus reports up to $30B of committed revenue over six years.

The identity moment is the listing. Firmus and its advisers are working towards an ASX float in the final quarter of 2026 (Wilson Asset Management, Capital Brief), which at the reported size would rank among the largest technology listings in Australian history. A company about to sell itself to Australian institutions and retail investors needs a brand beyond data-centre engineers, and the local precedent is set: Atlassian, Airwallex and Airtasker all bought Formula 1 for that reason.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 7 August Firmus announced full commitments for a $2B strategic equity round at a post-money valuation above $10.5B, with follow-on money from Coatue and NVIDIA, new investment from funds managed by Blackstone, and participation from Jane Street. It is a company release, confirmed by Bloomberg the same day, and takes new equity raised in the past year past $3B.
Price doubled in four months
In April Firmus raised $505M at a $5.5B valuation; four months later the post-money print is above $10.5B. Behind the equity sits a $10B debt facility led by Blackstone and Coatue, signed in February, described as one of the largest private debt financings in Australian history.
The listing
Firmus and its advisers are working towards an ASX float in the final quarter of 2026, after an earlier mid-year target slipped; Wilson Asset Management reports the company wants up to $30B of committed revenue in hand when it launches. A listing of the reported size would rank among the largest technology IPOs in Australian history, and the brand spend that accompanies it is decided in the months before, not after.
Calendar window
The Singapore GP in October is an hour from the Batam campus where Firmus will take delivery of up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs from the first quarter of 2027; the 2027 season then opens with the Australian GP in Melbourne, in front of the investors the offer is aimed at. A deal agreed before Singapore can be announced there and launched in full at home.

Why Atlassian Williams Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The Australian car
Atlassian, founded in Sydney, became Williams' title partner in 2025 in the largest deal in the team's history. Firmus was founded in Sydney six years ago and is about to ask Australian investors to value it above $10B. Two Sydney technology companies on one car is a story the ASX, the AFR and the Melbourne crowd will read without explanation.
The open lane
Per the sponsor table, Williams carries Atlassian, VAST for the data platform, Keeper for identity, Airia, Brillio and Claude as Official Thinking Partner, and no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner. Official AI Factory Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
A data-native roster
Williams' revival is data-led, and GPU capacity for surrogate models, simulation and analytics is consumed in the factory rather than merely shown on the car. That is what separates a technology partner from a logo, and it is what Firmus sells.
Precedent
Atlassian, Airwallex and Airtasker have each used a Formula 1 team to take an Australian technology brand global. Firmus would be the fourth, and the first whose product the team itself would run on.

Value To Atlassian Williams Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Compute for the work outside the aerodynamic-testing restrictions: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-the-loop and race-strategy simulation, telemetry and video analytics between sessions. Firmus supplies it on demand from liquid-cooled NVIDIA factories it says use 33% less energy and 99% less water than conventional builds, so the team gets capacity it could not fund inside the cost cap and a sustainability line it can defend.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner heading to a public listing brings Australian and Asian institutional investors, bankers and hyperscale customers to Singapore and Melbourne, an audience Williams' B2B partners want in the suite.
Content and ecosystem
A factory-to-pit-wall story: the compute behind the strategy models, filmed in Tasmania and Batam, with co-produced engineering content alongside the team's data partners.
What the team gives back
Official AI Factory Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at the Australian and Singapore rounds, driver and engineering access for Firmus' investor communications.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Factory Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the listing and the Batam ramp. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in compute. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at the Australian and Singapore rounds, joint engineering content.

The askA 25-minute call with Oliver Curtis, or with co-CEO Tim Rosenfield and Chair Grant Dempsey, before the Singapore GP to agree a Singapore announcement window and size an Official AI Factory Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster ahead of the listing.

Oliver Curtis
Co-Founder & Co-CEO, Firmus Technologies · verified
Curtis co-founded Firmus in Sydney in 2019, fronts every raise and holds a reported 19% stake. Path: Tim Rosenfield, Co-Founder and Co-CEO; Kirsty Godfrey-Billy, CFO, ex-Xero; Cameron Hanson, COO; Grant Dempsey, Chair. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Australian car.
“Oliver, Atlassian took Williams to market as the Australian team; you are taking Firmus to the ASX. The compute lane on that car is open and Singapore is an hour from Batam. 25 minutes before the Singapore GP to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A company-announced $2B round at more than $10.5B, a $10B debt stack and an ASX listing targeted for the fourth quarter put Firmus at peak brand-investment motive; Williams offers the grid's only Australian-titled car and an open compute lane. The case

The round is announced by the lead investor and the company: $250M at $2.1B, led by Mubadala, co-led by Woven Capital and Ion Pacific, with BlueCrest and Sona Capital new alongside BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton and Uber. Moove reports about $420M of annual recurring revenue from roughly 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries. Proceeds go to owning autonomous fleets outright and to 'Nests', robotics-first depots where robotaxis are charged, serviced and orchestrated, with the autonomous workforce growing from about 150 to about 500 by year-end.

The identity moment is the pivot from financing drivers in Lagos to owning the operating layer beneath robotaxis. Since Waymo contracted Moove for Phoenix and Miami in December 2024, every vehicle it runs there has been a Jaguar I-PACE; London, Waymo's first European city, is next, with Moove as fleet partner and service pending regulators. A company about to put its name on driverless Jaguars in three cities needs a brand its riders, regulators and partners recognise.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 5 August Mubadala and Moove announced a $250M Series C at a $2.1B valuation, led by Mubadala Investment Company and co-led by Woven Capital, Toyota's growth fund, and Ion Pacific, with BlueCrest and Sona Capital new alongside BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton, Uber and the Ontario Power Generation Pension Plan. Moove reports about $420M of annual recurring revenue from roughly 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries, built organically and through the acquisitions of Kovi in Brazil and Tokyo Taxi in Japan. The proceeds fund autonomous fleet ownership and 'Nests', robotics-first depots where robotaxis are charged, serviced and orchestrated, with the autonomous workforce growing from about 150 to about 500 by the end of 2026.
The London launch
Waymo named Moove its fleet partner for London in October 2025, its first European city, operating and maintaining all-electric Jaguar I-PACEs; testing is under way under a government-backed pilot and commercial service is pending regulatory approval. A brand launching driverless Jaguars in London wants to be known there before the cars arrive.

Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December and teams close rosters this autumn. The Miami E-Prix on 20 February and the London E-Prix double-header on 29-30 May 2027 are Moove's two Waymo cities; the Austin E-Prix on 6 February adds a third US stage.

Valar Atomics, the El Segundo nuclear start-up whose Ward 250 reactor went critical in Utah in June and powered an NVIDIA Blackwell chip on 1 July, announced a $1B Series B led by Sequoia on 3 August with a $200M credit facility; Bloomberg puts the valuation at $6B.

The case

The round is company-announced: $1B of Series B equity led by Sequoia, whose Shaun Maguire joins the board, with Atreides, Point72, Snowpoint and Valor Equity Partners participating, plus a $200M credit facility led by Erebor Bank with J.P. Morgan, Crescent Cove and Hercules Capital. Bloomberg and TechCrunch report a $6B valuation, about three times the prior round; the company has not disclosed it. The engineering is real: Ward 250 reached criticality on 18 June at the Utah San Rafael Energy Lab under the DOE Reactor Pilot Program, the first DOE-authorised reactor built outside a national laboratory.

The identity moment is public and presidential: on 1 July Ward 250 powered an NVIDIA Blackwell chip live on stage, the first US advanced reactor to run an AI chip, and the two companies announced a study for a 30 MW water-free AI facility in Utah. On 24 July Taylor stood in the Oval Office as one of four reactor CEOs the President honoured. A company selling firm power to hyperscalers needs a brand beyond the trade press.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 3 August Valar Atomics announced a $1B Series B led by Sequoia, with Shaun Maguire joining the board and Atreides, Point72, Snowpoint and Valor Equity Partners participating, alongside a $200M credit facility led by Erebor Bank with J.P. Morgan, Crescent Cove and Hercules Capital. Bloomberg and TechCrunch report a $6B valuation, about three times the roughly $2B of the prior round months earlier; the company itself did not disclose it, and the brief says so.
The reactor is real
Ward 250, a TRISO-fuelled high-temperature gas reactor flown to Utah by US Air Force cargo aircraft in February, reached criticality on 18 June at the Utah San Rafael Energy Lab in Emery County under the Department of Energy's Reactor Pilot Program, the first DOE-authorised reactor built outside a national laboratory and the second to go critical under the programme. The site had been empty nine months earlier.
The public moment
On 1 July Ward 250 powered an NVIDIA Blackwell chip live on stage and hosted a website, the first time a US advanced reactor has run an AI chip, and Valar and NVIDIA announced a joint study for a 30 MW water-free AI computing facility in Utah. On 24 July the President hosted Taylor and three other reactor CEOs in the Oval Office. The company is, for the first time, a brand the public has seen.
Calendar window
Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December and teams settle rosters this autumn. The Austin E-Prix on 6 February and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February 2027 are the two US rounds, in front of the utilities, hyperscalers, state governors and federal officials Valar sells to.

Andretti is the US entry in Formula E, and its two US home rounds fall within three weeks of each other in February. Valar's customers and regulators are American; the Oval Office is its most valuable photograph. No other Formula E team gives the story a home crowd.

Per the sponsor table, Andretti carries Porsche and, from Season 13, Nissan as powertrain partners, Andretti Global, TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo, and no energy, fuel or power partner. TWG AI is already on the Andretti car; Valar's first commercial customers are AI data centres, and its Utah facility study is with NVIDIA. Power and compute on one livery is a story the two partners can tell together.
Where the electricity comes from
Formula E is asked at every round where its power comes from. A partner whose product is clean firm electricity, on the American car, answers that question in a way a fuel or lubricant brand cannot.

OLIX Computing

AI Semiconductors · Optical Inference Silicon · London (registered St Albans; founded 2024) · Private ($3.3B; $312M Series B, Aug 2026)

OLIX, the London AI-chip company founded in 2024 by James Dacombe, announced a $312M Series B at a $3.3B valuation on 3 August, tripling the $1B mark set by its $220M Series A in February. Arm, Hudson River Trading and Reed Hastings joined; the UK's Sovereign AI fund invested.

The case

Fundomo led the round; Arm, Hudson River Trading and Reed Hastings joined, and existing backers Hummingbird, Plural, Creandum, Crane, Phoenix Court and Transition increased their commitments. Six months earlier Hummingbird had led a $220M Series A at just over $1B. OLIX builds specialised inference silicon connected by an optical network, with first systems due to customers in the second half of 2027. It is recruiting engineers across London, Bristol, Austin, Toronto and San Francisco, has hired former Wise CFO Matt Briers as CFO and put Stanford's Nick McKeown on the board.

The grid has already priced AI silicon: Groq became an Official Partner of McLaren in September 2025 with its inference chips on the car from Singapore, and Arm, now an OLIX investor, sits on Aston Martin Aramco's roster. OLIX is the British entrant without a seat. A company that must recruit against Nvidia and sell to hyperscalers before its first chip ships has a brand to build, and now the money to build it.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
OLIX announced a $312M Series B at a $3.3B valuation on 3 August 2026, led by Fundomo with Arm, Hudson River Trading and Reed Hastings. The company's own newsroom carries the round; Tech.eu, DCD and The Next Web report the same figures.
Tripled in six months
The $220M Series A in February 2026, led by Hummingbird, priced OLIX at just over $1B. Six months later the Series B priced it at $3.3B. A company re-rated that fast, before its first chip ships, is being valued on narrative, and narrative is what a sponsorship builds.
The 2027 launch
First AI systems are due to customers in the second half of 2027. A three-season partnership starting in 2027 puts the brand on the grid in the launch year, with an evaluation clause that turns the halo into a reference deployment once product exists.
Calendar window
Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin, where OLIX is recruiting, falls in late October; Las Vegas follows in November. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027.

The open lane
Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, VAST for the data platform, Keeper for identity security, Airia and Brillio on the technology side, and Claude as Official Thinking Partner. OLIX is the UK's sovereign-AI chip bet, with the government's Sovereign AI fund on the register. Williams at Grove is the British engineering revival on the grid. The two stories reinforce each other at Silverstone and in Westminster.
The same arc
Williams is rebuilding a technical base against far larger incumbents; OLIX is doing the same against Nvidia. That parallel gives the partnership a narrative the team can tell on camera without stretching.
Talent and the United States
OLIX is hiring in London, Bristol, Austin, Toronto and San Francisco. An F1 engineering brand is a recruitment asset in every one of those markets, and the Austin office gives the United States GP a home-market activation.

Horizon3.ai

Cybersecurity · Autonomous Penetration Testing · San Francisco (offices in Amsterdam, Australia, Singapore) · Private ($2B+; $250M Series E, Aug 2026)

Horizon3, the San Francisco security company whose NodeZero platform attacks customers' networks the way an adversary would, announced a $250M Series E at a valuation above $2B on 3 August, co-led by NightDragon and NEA, tripling the $650M price of its June 2025 Series D in little over a year.

The case

The oversubscribed round brought in Acrew, Blue Cloud Ventures, Demeter, Singapore's EDBI, PSG, SAIC and Sapphire, with Craft, Prosperity7, Qualcomm Ventures, Ridge and SignalFire returning. The company reports 120% year-on-year ARR growth and more than 7,000 organisations protected, four of them Fortune 10; TechCrunch puts ARR near $100M (reported). Founders Snehal Antani and Anthony Pillitiere met at Joint Special Operations Command; Antani was later CTO of Splunk. The money funds international expansion, with offices opened in Amsterdam in June, Australia and Singapore, and a partner network.

Cybersecurity is the most-sold technology category on the grid: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, Okta and Rubrik at McLaren, Cato Networks at Alpine, and Red Bull's 1Password. Every one sells defence. Horizon3 sells the attack, continuously, and its new CMO Andres Botero ran marketing at Rubrik in the period its McLaren partnership was being built. A category leader with no seat, and a marketer who has watched one taken.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Horizon3 announced a $250M Series E at a valuation above $2B on 3 August 2026, co-led by NightDragon and NEA, with seven new investors including Sapphire Ventures, PSG, SAIC and Singapore's EDBI. The company release and TechCrunch carry the same figures.
Tripled in a year
The June 2025 Series D, $100M led by NEA, valued the company at $650M (reported). Fourteen months later the price is above $2B, on 120% year-on-year ARR growth and more than 7,000 organisations protected, four of them Fortune 10. A brand re-rated that fast has a story to tell and the budget to tell it.
A marketing owner with a mandate
Andres Botero joined as Chief Marketing Officer on 7 January 2026 from Rubrik, where he was CMO through the April 2024 IPO. Rubrik's multi-year McLaren partnership was announced three weeks after his move; whether he built it is not confirmed, but he has seen the mechanics from the inside.
Calendar window
The United States GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026, with Mexico City and São Paulo between them; teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027.

Why Cadillac F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Cadillac's debut roster carries TWG AI as exclusive AI partner, Core Scientific for the data centre, IFS for enterprise software, plus Claro, Jim Beam, Tenneco and Tommy Hilfiger. No cybersecurity partner: Official Cybersecurity Partner is a clean category on a team that has said it wants fewer, bigger partners.
A greenfield estate
New factories in Fishers, Charlotte and Silverstone, a supplier base assembled in two years and a garage network rebuilt at every circuit. F1 teams have faced phishing, deepfake and telemetry-theft campaigns and a 2025 FIA systems loophole. A first-season estate is the one most in need of continuous attack testing.
An American story
Horizon3's founders met at Joint Special Operations Command and SAIC has joined the register. Cadillac is the GM-backed American flag-bearer with a commercial team hired from the Miami GP and Unilever to sell exactly that audience.
The buyer in the suite
Cadillac's hospitality reaches CISOs, CIOs and federal buyers at Austin and Las Vegas, the audience a $100M-ARR security company selling to Fortune 10 accounts wants in the room.

Value To Cadillac F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
NodeZero runs autonomous penetration tests continuously across the team's factory networks, trackside infrastructure, supplier integrations and partner environments, ranking findings by exploitability and re-testing after each fix. The team's security staff work from a live attacker's view rather than an annual audit.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to Fortune 10 CISOs and defence agencies brings a guest list of security and federal buyers to the US rounds, the audience Cadillac's B2B partners want alongside them.
Content and ecosystem
How a brand-new Formula 1 team defends itself: co-produced engineering content on continuous security validation, a reference customer for Horizon3's enterprise sales, and a story that fits a debutant building everything from scratch.
What the team gives back
Official Cybersecurity Partner designation, car and garage placement, naming of the security-validation programme, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, driver and engineering access for Horizon3's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Cybersecurity Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the international build-out. Estimated $4-6M a year, part-payable in NodeZero licences. Scope: car and garage placement, naming of the team's security-validation programme, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for CISOs and federal buyers, content on how a new team defends itself.

The askA 25-minute call with Andres Botero before the United States GP to test appetite for a 2027 start, clear the AI-partner language with Cadillac's TWG AI exclusivity, and size an Official Cybersecurity Partner entry, part-paid in NodeZero licences, against the team's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Andres Botero
Chief Marketing Officer, Horizon3.ai · verified
Botero joined on 7 January 2026 from Rubrik, where he was CMO through its April 2024 IPO and while the McLaren partnership announced on 28 January was built; his part in that deal is not confirmed. Sponsor: Snehal Antani, co-founder and CEO. Path: Holly Grey, CFO, and Matt Hartley, CRO.

Opening angle

Lead with Rubrik and the empty lane.
“Andres, you were at Rubrik while its McLaren deal came together. Cadillac has no cybersecurity partner and a first-season estate nobody has attacked yet. 25 minutes before Austin to see what NodeZero on a Formula 1 team looks like?”
Bottom line
$250M at more than $2B, 120% ARR growth, a CMO who has seen an F1 deal built and an open cybersecurity lane at the American debutant put Horizon3 at peak authority to move, with Austin and Las Vegas inside the window. The TWG AI exclusivity and a premium first-deal price hold the score at 78.

ThreatLocker, the Orlando zero-trust endpoint company protecting more than 70,000 organisations, closed a $190M Series F led by Elephant on 29 July 2026, with Koch Disruptive Technologies joining and total funding now near $500M. The money funds AI-risk controls and a first UK office in Reading.

The case

ThreatLocker announced a $190M Series F on 29 July 2026, led by Elephant, with D. E. Shaw Ventures and Arthur Ventures returning and Koch Disruptive Technologies new. It follows a $20M Series B, $100M Series C, $115M Series D (April 2024) and $60M Series E (April 2025): nearly $500M in total. SecurityWeek puts the pre-round valuation at $1.6B (reported); the company has not stated a new one and publishes no revenue. The platform, allowlisting and Ringfencing that block whatever is not explicitly permitted, protects more than 70,000 organisations. The round funds AI-risk controls and a Reading office.

Cybersecurity is the most-sold technology category on the grid: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, 1Password (Red Bull) and Cato Networks at Alpine. Each vendor bought the same thing, a paddock full of the enterprise buyers it sells to. ThreatLocker reaches the mid-market through managed service providers and has just committed to Europe. What it lacks is a brand stage for those partners and their customers.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
ThreatLocker announced on 29 July 2026 that it had secured $190M in Series F funding led by Elephant, with D. E. Shaw Ventures and Arthur Ventures continuing and Koch Disruptive Technologies investing for the first time. The company's own release names the uses: controls for AI-related security risks, the Zero Trust Platform, and international expansion starting with a Reading, UK office.
Six rounds, near $500M
The Series F follows a $20M Series B, $100M Series C, $115M Series D in April 2024 and $60M Series E in April 2025, taking total funding to nearly $500M. SecurityWeek reports the previous round valued the company at $1.6B; ThreatLocker has not stated a Series F valuation and does not publish revenue, so the brief sizes capacity on the raise, not the valuation.
Europe is the next spend
The company already runs its European headquarters from Dublin, with offices in Dubai and Brisbane. Reading is the first UK office, which puts a brand-building budget in the same country as eight Formula 1 teams and Silverstone, where Cadillac's UK operation sits.
Update since this date: a first motorsport trial
On 4 September 2026 ThreatLocker joined Juncos Hollinger Racing for the IndyCar season finale at Laguna Seca, a one-race presence on the JHR entry. Danny Jenkins said the aim was to introduce ThreatLocker to the IndyCar community. The company has now tested motorsport with a single-race buy; the next conversation is whether a multi-year F1 seat at an Indiana-based team is the scale-up.

A greenfield estate
Cadillac is building an entire Formula 1 operation from scratch: a $200M, roughly 400,000 sq ft campus in Fishers next to Indianapolis Metropolitan Airport, a Charlotte facility and a Silverstone base. Core Scientific is developing the team's Indianapolis data hub and optimising the cloud-hybrid environment across US and UK operations; IFS runs operations. There is no cybersecurity partner on the roster, which the team's profile lists as an open category.
Fewer, bigger partners
Cadillac has said it is not seeking a title sponsor for its debut and wants fewer, bigger partnerships. That favours a partner whose product is deployed across the team rather than a badge, which is the shape of a zero-trust endpoint deal.
Home market
ThreatLocker is headquartered in Orlando and sells mainly through US managed service providers. Cadillac is the American entry, with the Miami, Austin and Las Vegas rounds each year, and its Indiana base sits in the same city as the IndyCar team ThreatLocker has just tried.
Ruled out by the table
Every established security lane is taken: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, 1Password (Red Bull), Cato Networks at Alpine and NinjaOne at Audi. Of the open teams, Cadillac's combination of a new estate, a US identity and an explicit open category is the strongest.

Operational workstream (Mode A)
A debut team is defining its security baseline now. ThreatLocker's allowlisting denies any application not explicitly permitted, Ringfencing restricts how permitted applications touch data and each other, and Elevation Control removes standing admin rights: controls that fit engineering workstations, machining and additive cells, the Indianapolis data hub and trackside laptops that join a different circuit network every race weekend.
Cost-cap arithmetic
A default-deny posture stops ransomware and rogue tooling without the headcount of a large security operations centre, which matters for a team spending inside the FIA cost cap. Product and services can form part of the consideration, lowering the cash element.
Commercial lift for the team
ThreatLocker's channel is thousands of managed service providers and 70,000 end customers, a mid-market audience Cadillac's B2B partners do not yet reach. US-race hospitality for MSP partners and a factory reference story give the team a new pool of guests and prospects.
What the team gives back
Official Zero Trust Cybersecurity Partner designation, halo or sidepod placement, a published deployment case study with the team's IT leadership, hospitality at the US rounds, and driver and engineering access for ThreatLocker's channel events.

Deal architecture

The case

Zeev Ventures, Angular Ventures, Heavybit and Jibe returned; the $35M Series B, led by Zeev, closed in April 2025. Over the past year the company tripled annual recurring revenue, doubled headcount to about 140, roughly 80 in Israel and the rest in Boston and San Francisco, and passed 250 paying customers, startups to Fortune 5 enterprises. Its platform captures telemetry with eBPF inside the customer's own cloud, so nothing leaves the environment. Founders Shahar Azulay and Yechezkel Rabinovich served together in the cyber unit of Israel's Prime Minister's Office.

Observability is on the grid but thinly: Splunk sits with McLaren through Cisco and Dynatrace at Racing Bulls, and the rest of the field runs the same telemetry pipelines without a named partner. A challenger that needs to be seen beside the incumbents, and whose whole pitch is keeping sensitive data inside the customer's walls, has a story Formula 1 tells better than any conference.

The US push
Roughly 80 of the 140 staff are in Israel; the rest are in Boston and San Francisco, where the VP of Marketing sits. The Series C funds the US go-to-market that a partnership with an American team supports directly.
Calendar window
The Italian GP (early September), the United States GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) fall inside the horizon; teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027.

The product is prevention-first: it decides which software, AI agents and developer tools may run on employee devices rather than detecting them afterwards. Paying customers span healthcare, retail and financial services; the money goes to a US go-to-market team and Glow Labs.

Cybersecurity is the grid's most-sold technology category, and every vendor bought the same thing: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, Cato Networks at Alpine, a paddock full of the CISOs they sell to. Glow's leadership has run that playbook from inside: COO Emily Heath sat on Wiz's board through its $32B sale to Google and was a Cyberstarts partner. A stealth exit with $180M is when a company buys its stage.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 22 July 2026 Glow emerged from stealth with $180M in funding at a $1.2B valuation. The company's release names the leads, Sequoia, Cyberstarts, Greenoaks and Redpoint Ventures, and the participants, Index Ventures, Swish Ventures, Lux Capital, Operator Collective and Holly Ventures, and states the use of funds: accelerating the go-to-market team in the United States and expanding Glow Labs, its research arm.
Three rounds in a year
CTech reports the $180M as a $20M seed led by Sequoia and Cyberstarts, a $60M Series A led by Index Ventures with Greenoaks at a $400M valuation, and a $100M Series B, all in roughly a year; the company itself gives only the total, so the split is reported, not confirmed. Whatever the split, a company that tripled its valuation inside a year before showing a product has investors expecting a category to be built, and category-building is brand spend.
The first brand budget follows the first sales hires
The stated use of funds is a US go-to-market team. A security vendor's first brand line typically opens with its first enterprise sales cycle, and CISO-facing hospitality is what the other six security vendors on the grid bought. Glow is at the front of that cycle, not the end of it.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 161 · 16 JUL 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 161 · HOT · F1

SambaNova Systems

AI Inference Infrastructure · Chips & Systems · Palo Alto, California (founded 2017) · Private ($11B post-money; $1B Series F first close, Jul 2026)

SambaNova, the Palo Alto AI-chip maker, completed the first close of a $1B Series F at an $11B post-money valuation on 8 July 2026, led by General Atlantic, five months after a $350M Series E at a reported $2.2B. JPMorganChase was named an on-premises inference customer the same day.

The case

General Atlantic led the $1B first close, with Seligman Ventures, T. Rowe Price Associates and Capital Group, alongside BlackRock, Intel Capital, the Qatar Investment Authority, Battery Ventures and Vista Equity Partners; a second close was expected within weeks. Five months earlier SambaNova raised a $350M Series E with Intel after Bloomberg-reported takeover talks near $1.6B stalled, so the price has risen roughly fivefold since February. Proceeds expand production of the SN40L and the SN50, shipping in the second half of 2026 with SoftBank first. Liang says a 2027 IPO is under consideration (reported).

The grid has a precedent: McLaren named Groq an Official Partner in September 2025, putting an inference chip on the car from the Singapore GP with a pitch of fast, cost-efficient intelligence for analysis and development. SambaNova is the other US inference-silicon company at scale, now with JPMorganChase running its systems on-premises. It has no seat, and it is the one with a public-market clock starting to run.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 8 July 2026 SambaNova announced the first close of $1B in strategic financing as part of a Series F at an $11B post-money valuation, led by General Atlantic with Seligman Ventures, T. Rowe Price Associates and Capital Group, and with BlackRock, Intel Capital, the Qatar Investment Authority, Battery Ventures, Vista Equity Partners and Volantis among new and existing investors. The company said a second close was expected in the coming weeks; none had been announced by early September, so the brief anchors on the first close.
A fivefold re-rating in five months
In December 2025 Bloomberg reported Intel in advanced talks to buy SambaNova for about $1.6B including debt. The talks stalled; in February 2026 Intel instead took a stake in a $350M Series E at a reported ~$2.2B valuation and signed a multi-year partnership. Five months later the company priced at $11B. A business re-rated that fast has a story to tell to enterprise, sovereign and public-market audiences, and the money to tell it.
JPMorganChase and the SN50 ramp
The same day, JPMorganChase was named an inference-infrastructure customer, with SN40L and SN50 systems powering secure on-premises inference at the bank. The SN50 begins shipping in the second half of 2026 with SoftBank as first deployment partner in Japan; Saudi Aramco and OVHcloud are among named customers. Each shipment milestone is a moment a partnership can be timed to.
Calendar and listing window
The United States GP in October and the Las Vegas GP in November are the US rounds left in 2026, and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. Rodrigo Liang has said an IPO in 2027, most likely in the US, is under consideration (reported); a deal agreed before Austin runs through the listing year.

Why Tgr Haas F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title and technical partner, Mphasis as Official Digital Partner, CommScope and Ruckus for connectivity, Orion180, Haas Automation and Haas Tooling, but no compute, AI, cloud or chip partner. Official AI Inference Partner is a clean category. Mphasis sells IT services, including AI services, so it is a channel for a deployment, not a lock on the lane.
A team that needs the capability
Haas is the grid's lean privateer, operating from Kannapolis, Banbury and a design office in Maranello with a fraction of the headcount of the works teams. Capability installed by a partner, an inference system the team could not otherwise justify inside the cost cap, is worth more to Haas than to a team with its own data-centre programme.
American team, American buyers
SambaNova is headquartered in Palo Alto and sells to US banks, sovereign programmes and neo-clouds. Haas is the American team with three home rounds a year: Miami, Austin and Las Vegas, where the enterprise and capital-markets audience SambaNova needs for a 2027 listing already gathers.
The precedent, and the difference
Groq became an Official Partner of McLaren in September 2025 with its LPU chip on the car from the Singapore GP. That proved teams buy inference silicon. SambaNova's difference is the on-premises system: a deployment at Haas would be the JPMorgan story at racing speed, not a logo.

Value To Tgr Haas F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
An SN40L system installed at the Banbury operations base running open-weight models on the team's own data: post-session strategy analysis, telemetry anomaly detection across the car's sensor streams, engineering-document and simulation copilots for a small engineering staff. Data never leaves the building, which matters to a team whose design office sits inside Ferrari's home town.
Cost-cap arithmetic
Systems and support can form part of the consideration, so the team gains inference capacity without cost-cap capital. The SN50, shipping from the second half of 2026, gives the partnership a hardware refresh story in each of the three years.
Commercial lift for the team
SambaNova's buyers are CIOs and CTOs at banks, sovereign AI programmes and neo-clouds, an audience Haas's current partners do not bring. Hospitality at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas for those accounts, and a factory reference deployment SambaNova can show every prospect.
What the team gives back
Official AI Inference Partner designation, sidepod or rear-wing placement, naming of the team's inference environment, driver and engineering access for SambaNova's customer events, and engineering content from Banbury and Kannapolis on how the system is used.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Inference Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the SN50 ramp and a possible 2027 listing. Estimated $4-7M a year, part-payable in systems and support. Scope: sidepod or rear-wing placement, naming of the team's inference environment, US-race hospitality, engineering content from Banbury.

The askA 25-minute call with Rodrigo Liang before the United States GP to confirm the size of the completed Series F and the listing timetable, and to size an Official AI Inference Partner entry, part-paid in systems, against Haas's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Rodrigo Liang
Co-Founder & CEO, SambaNova Systems · verified
Liang co-founded SambaNova in 2017 with Stanford professors Kunle Olukotun and Christopher Ré after leading processor development at Sun Microsystems and Oracle. Path: Annie Shea Weckesser, Chief Marketing Officer; Harry Ault, Chief Revenue Officer; Matt Padfield, CFO since June 2026.

Opening angle

Lead with the Groq precedent.
“Rodrigo, Groq put its chip on a McLaren the season it needed the story. You have just raised $1B at $11B with a listing in view, and the American team has no silicon partner. JPMorgan runs you on-premises; a race team could. 25 minutes before Austin?”
Bottom line
A $1B first close at $11B, a fivefold re-rating in five months, JPMorganChase on-premises and an IPO under consideration put SambaNova at peak brand-investment authority. Haas has no compute or chip partner, Groq at McLaren proved the category, and two US races remain inside the window.

Fireworks AI

AI Infrastructure · Inference Cloud for Open Models · Redwood City, California (founded 2022) · Private ($17.5B; $1.505B Series D, Jul 2026)

Fireworks AI, the Redwood City inference cloud founded by the Meta engineers behind PyTorch, announced a $1.505B Series D at a $17.5B valuation on 16 July 2026, led by Atreides, Index Ventures and TCV with Nvidia participating, as annualised revenue passed $1B, fivefold in a year on the company's figures.

The case

Bloomberg reported on 27 May that Fireworks was in talks at $15B with Index co-leading; the round priced above that on 16 July at $17.5B, led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures and TCV, with Nvidia, Lightspeed, Evantic, Bessemer, Menlo, Insight, Ontario Teachers' and Lone Pine participating. It follows a $250M Series C at $4B in October 2025, a fourfold step in nine months; total funding is about $1.8B (reported). The company says annualised revenue passed $1B, up fivefold, and tokens served rose from 15 to over 40 trillion a day. Headcount goes from about 200 to 600 by year-end.

Inference has been sold to the grid twice: Groq at McLaren since September 2025 and CoreWeave at Aston Martin since May 2025, each signed in the year the vendor needed a public story. Fireworks is the inference company whose customers, Uber, DoorDash, Notion, Samsung and Verizon, are names a paddock recognises, and it has no seat. A $17.5B private company with $1B of revenue has the public market as its next audience.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 16 July 2026 Fireworks announced a $1.505B Series D at a $17.5B post-money valuation, led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures and TCV, with Nvidia, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Evantic Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, Insight Partners, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Lone Pine Capital and 20VC among the participants. Bloomberg had reported on 27 May that the company was in talks at $15B; it priced above that.
Fourfold in nine months
The Series C of October 2025 was $250M at $4B, led by Lightspeed, Index Ventures and Evantic with Sequoia participating, and brought total funding to $327M; two years earlier Sequoia led a $52M round at $552M with Nvidia, AMD and MongoDB. Total funding after the Series D is about $1.8B (reported). A company re-priced fourfold in nine months has a story for enterprise buyers and, eventually, the public market.
Revenue and scale, on the company's figures
Fireworks says annualised revenue run-rate has passed $1B, fivefold year on year, and that tokens served rose from 15 trillion to more than 40 trillion a day. Named customers include Uber, DoorDash, Notion, Samsung, Verizon, Cursor and Upwork; Cursor once provided more than half of revenue and the mix has since diversified. Lin Qiao told CNBC headcount is about 200 and will reach 600 by the end of 2026. None of these numbers is audited, and the brief says so.
Calendar window
The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the US rounds left in 2026, and teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin lands in the same quarter as the hiring plan and is activated in full for 2027.

Why Visa Cash App Racing Bulls — the open lane, the audience, the platform

A data stack without an inference layer
Racing Bulls carries Confluent for real-time data streaming (more than a million data points a second between car, pit wall and factory, multi-year since October 2025), Dynatrace as Official Observability and Performance Analytics Technology Partner, RebelDot as a software partner, and Neural Concept's engineering AI in aerodynamic development. There is no AI-inference, cloud or model partner: Official AI Inference Partner is a clean category that completes a stack the team has already advertised.
A challenger team at a challenger price
Racing Bulls is the Red Bull sister team with a younger audience and a partner tier priced below the works teams. For a developer-first brand whose buyers are engineering leaders, the fit is closer than a luxury-coded works team, and the price leaves room for inference credits to form part of the consideration.
Two sites fed by one stream
The team is based in Faenza, Italy, with aerodynamic and design facilities at the Red Bull Technology Campus in Milton Keynes since January 2025. Both consume the Confluent stream; an inference layer serves both without on-premises capital.
Ruled out by the table
Groq at McLaren, CoreWeave at Aston Martin, Oracle at Red Bull, Microsoft at Mercedes and Alpine, HP and IBM at Ferrari, Core Scientific and TWG AI at Cadillac, Claude and Airia at Williams and ElevenLabs at Audi each occupy the compute, cloud or AI lane. Haas is open but has no comparable real-time data stack to complete.

Value To Visa Cash App Racing Bulls — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Open-weight models fine-tuned on the team's own telemetry and strategy history, served by Fireworks at low latency: engineer copilots that answer questions over live session data, anomaly detection on the million-points-a-second stream, and post-session analysis across the archive. Fireworks runs this shape for Uber, DoorDash and Notion; the team supplies the data and Confluent supplies the pipe.
Cost-cap arithmetic
Hosted inference means no on-premises hardware or cost-cap capital, and inference credits can form part of the consideration. The team gains a capability it would otherwise have to build; the partnership carries a usage story that grows each season.
Commercial lift for the team
Fireworks sells to engineering and platform leaders at enterprises such as Uber, DoorDash, Samsung and Verizon, an audience the team's current partners do not bring. US-race hospitality for those accounts and a reference deployment give Racing Bulls a new guest list and Fireworks a customer story it can show on a car.
What the team gives back
Official AI Inference Partner designation, sidepod or halo placement alongside Confluent, naming of the team's model environment, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, and engineering content from Faenza and Milton Keynes on how the models are used.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Inference Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the hiring plan and any listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in inference credits. Scope: sidepod or halo placement, naming of the team's model environment, US-race hospitality for enterprise accounts, engineering content from Faenza.

The askA 25-minute call with Lin Qiao before the United States GP to confirm the customer mix behind the $1B run-rate, walk through an inference deployment on Racing Bulls' data stream, and size an Official AI Inference Partner entry, part-paid in credits, against the team's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Lin Qiao
CEO & Co-Founder, Fireworks AI · verified
Qiao led PyTorch at Meta as Senior Director of Engineering before founding Fireworks in 2022 with six PyTorch colleagues; she fronts every raise. Path: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, CTO and Co-Founder. No chief marketing officer, COO, chief revenue officer or CFO is named on the company's listings.

Opening angle

Lead with the stack that lacks a brain.
“Lin, Racing Bulls streams a million data points a second and has no inference partner on top of it. You have just raised $1.5B at $17.5B with revenue past $1B; Groq and CoreWeave took their seats at this stage. 25 minutes before Austin?”
Bottom line
A $1.505B Series D at $17.5B, revenue past $1B on the company's figures and headcount tripling put Fireworks at peak brand-investment authority. Racing Bulls has the real-time data stack and no inference partner, Groq at McLaren and CoreWeave at Aston Martin proved the category, and two US races remain inside the window.

The case

On 9 July Oxylabs announced a $130M investment from the Warburg Pincus Capital Solutions Founders Fund; the release does not print a valuation, and the $3.6B figure is reported by SiliconANGLE, TNW and Dealroom. It is the company's first external funding since 2015. The business serves over 350,000 customers across cybersecurity, e-commerce and finance, and Dealroom and IBTimes report $350M of annual recurring revenue, citing the company. Vytautas Savickas took over as chief executive in the second quarter, with founder Julius Černiauskas moving to chairman.

The grid has learned to sell data infrastructure: VAST at Williams, Confluent and Dynatrace at Racing Bulls, Alteryx at McLaren, TWG AI at Cadillac. None of them touches the public web, where the grounding data for AI agents comes from and where Oxylabs sits. A bootstrapped European company that just took growth capital from a New York investor has one job now: be known by the enterprises and AI builders that buy this.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 9 July 2026 Oxylabs announced a $130M investment from the Warburg Pincus Capital Solutions Founders Fund, its first outside capital since it was founded in Vilnius in 2015. The release does not state a valuation; SiliconANGLE, TNW, IBTimes and Dealroom report about $3.6B, and the brief labels that figure as reported.
A new chief executive
Vytautas Savickas became CEO of the Oxylabs group in the second quarter of 2026, with founder Julius Černiauskas moving to Chairman. A new CEO with a growth mandate and fresh capital is the moment a company chooses what it wants to be known for, and who it wants to be known by.
From proxies to AI data infrastructure
The release repositions Oxylabs as the data layer that lets AI systems access, interpret and act on the open web. That is a message aimed at enterprises and AI builders, an audience a bootstrapped Lithuanian company has never had to market to at scale.
Calendar window
The Dutch GP at Zandvoort in late August and the Italian GP at Monza in September fall inside the six-to-ten-week window; the US GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP close the US season; teams set their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter.

Why Audi Revolut F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Audi's 2026 roster carries Revolut as title partner, ElevenLabs, NinjaOne, Extreme Networks, JigSpace and Libertex on the technology side. There is no data-platform, web-data or AI-data partner, and the team's profile lists enterprise software as an open category.
The Vilnius connection
Revolut operates in Europe through Revolut Bank UAB, incorporated, licensed and headquartered in Vilnius under the Bank of Lithuania and the European Central Bank. The case

On 6 July Keyfactor announced a $1B+ strategic growth investment led by Summit Partners; Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth keep significant stakes and the valuation was not disclosed. It follows $77M from Insight in 2019, $125M with the PrimeKey merger in 2021 and a Sixth Street minority round at about $1.3B in October 2023. The company manages billions of machine identities a year for more than 2,500 customers in 150 countries, over 40% of the Fortune 100 among them, and reached FedRAMP status this year. Stated use of funds: product, expansion, team, acquisitions.

Cybersecurity is a proven Formula 1 category: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Keeper at Williams, 1Password at Red Bull, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Okta at McLaren and, since November 2025, SEALSQ's post-quantum chips at Alpine. Machine identity, the layer beneath all of them, is not yet on the grid. Keyfactor's automotive practice already issues certificate identities to vehicles and signs their firmware, which is the language a works team owned by a carmaker speaks.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 6 July 2026 Keyfactor announced a $1B+ strategic growth investment led by Summit Partners. Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth keep significant ownership after the close. The valuation was not disclosed, and the brief does not guess one.
A scale mandate
The stated use of funds is product innovation, geographic expansion, team building and strategic acquisitions. Growth equity of this size is deployed against a plan to become the category name, and a category name needs reach outside the security conference circuit: the boardrooms of banks, retailers and government buyers.
The post-quantum clock
Keyfactor's own framing of the round is securing the AI and post-quantum enterprise. Migration to quantum-safe cryptography is now a dated programme in the regulated industries it sells to, which makes trust infrastructure a board-level topic rather than an IT line item for the first time.
Calendar window
Cadillac's debut season still has the US GP in Austin in October and the Las Vegas GP in November, and teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.

briefs.page_html:
Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 172 · 01 JUL 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 172 · HOT · F1

TwelveLabs

Video AI · Video Understanding Models / Media Technology · San Francisco & Seoul (founded 2021) · Private (~$150M raised; $100M Series B, Jul 2026)

TwelveLabs, the San Francisco and Seoul video-understanding company whose models let broadcasters search footage by what happens in it, closed a $100M Series B on 1 July 2026 co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with Amazon as strategic investor and Red Bull Ventures joining the cap table.

The case

TwelveLabs announced on 1 July 2026 a $100M Series B co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with Amazon, Radical Ventures, Korea Investment Partners, Index Ventures, Quadrille Capital and Red Bull Ventures, taking total funding to roughly $150M. Amazon made AWS its preferred cloud in a multi-year commitment built on Trainium chips. The money opens offices in New York and London alongside San Francisco and Seoul. Its Marengo and Pegasus models already serve NFL Media and Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, which use them to find exact moments in game footage and package content faster.

Red Bull Ventures, the group's corporate venture arm launched in 2025 with a €200M fund and led by Nai-Tseng Chen, Red Bull's Global Head of Corporate Finance, calls TwelveLabs its most prominent investment. That is a structural introduction to both Red Bull teams, not a sponsorship. The grid's nearest incumbents are cloud and data platforms, which TwelveLabs runs on rather than against, so the category is a new line on a roster, not a displacement.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 1 July 2026 TwelveLabs announced a $100M Series B co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with Amazon as strategic investor, existing investors Radical Ventures, Korea Investment Partners and Index Ventures, and new investors Quadrille Capital and Red Bull Ventures. Total funding is roughly $150M. This is a company release, so the figures are confirmed.
Amazon as preferred cloud
Amazon used the round to make AWS the company's preferred cloud in a multi-year commitment: inference optimised on Trainium chips, new models launching on AWS first. A hyperscaler betting on a video model is the signal that the product has crossed from research into production media workflows.
Offices in the two sports-media capitals
The company is opening offices in New York and London alongside San Francisco and Seoul, and expanding in Los Angeles. Those are the cities where leagues, broadcasters and rights-holders buy technology, and a racing team's content operation is the reference customer that sells to all of them.
Calendar window
Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US stages on which a San Francisco company would announce, with the Belgian, Hungarian, Dutch and Italian GPs inside the working window for a paid pilot.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

$100M
$100M Series B co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, announced 1 Jul 2026 (company release, GlobeNewswire); tot…
€200M
Red Bull Ventures, the group's corporate venture arm launched in 2025 with a €200M fund and led by Nai-Tsen…

Why Visa Cash App Racing Bulls — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Racing Bulls' technology roster is Dynatrace (observability), Confluent (data streaming), Siemens and Randstad, joined in June 2026 by a Salesforce Agentforce deployment for fan engagement and hospitality. Nothing on the roster indexes, searches or understands video. Official Video Intelligence Partner is a new line, not a displacement, and Racing Bulls partnerships are priced below the front of the grid.
The group path
Red Bull Ventures, Red Bull GmbH's corporate venture arm launched in 2025 with a €200M fund and led by Nai-Tseng Chen, the group's Global Head of Corporate Finance, joined the Series B and describes TwelveLabs as its most prominent investment. The introduction to both Red Bull teams therefore exists at group level; the sponsorship still has to be won on product.
The content team of the grid
CEO Peter Bayer says 60 per cent of fans rated the team's content excellent in F1's latest monitoring report, clear of the field. Its Creator Platform has spent two years giving young fans real work inside the team, from a graffiti artist on the São Paulo garage to a designer inside HUGO's studio. A team whose differentiator is content is the team that will use a video-search product every weekend.
Why not Oracle Red Bull Racing
The same group path leads to the senior team, but Oracle's title partnership puts cloud and AI at the centre of that team's story and TwelveLabs has just named AWS its preferred cloud. At Racing Bulls there is no cloud incumbent to argue with, and the entry price matches a company that has raised $150M.

Value To Visa Cash App Racing Bulls — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Every session produces hours of onboard, garage, pit-lane and broadcast video that sits in folders nobody can search. Marengo indexes it by what actually happens in the frame; Pegasus writes the metadata. The content team can ask for Lindblad's debut points celebration, every Lawson pit stop from the left camera, or the moment the garage reacts to a result, and cut clips while the session is still running.
Fuel for the Creator Platform
The Creator Platform gives young fans real production work. A searchable, tagged archive is the raw material they need, delivered as text queries rather than a media-asset-management training course, which is how the programme scales from a handful of creators to thousands of applicants.
Engineering review
The same search runs over pit-stop and incident footage: every stop, every wheel-gun angle, every unsafe release across a season, retrieved by description rather than timestamp. It is the video equivalent of what Dynatrace and Confluent do for the team's data streams.
What the team gives back
Official Video Intelligence Partner designation, nose or rear-wing endplate placement, naming of the team's video-search environment, Creator Platform integration, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, and a racing reference customer for TwelveLabs' New York and London sales teams.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Video Intelligence Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the New York and London build-out and the next raise. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year, part-payable in platform usage. Scope: nose or endplate placement, naming of the video-search environment, Creator Platform integration, US hospitality.

The askA 25-minute call with Jae Lee before the United States GP to confirm appetite for a first sports partnership, propose a paid pilot with the Racing Bulls content team over the autumn rounds, and size an Official Video Intelligence Partner entry against the 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Jae Lee
Co-Founder & CEO, TwelveLabs · verified
Lee co-founded TwelveLabs in 2021 after data-science work at Korea's Ministry of National Defense and a UC Berkeley degree; he fronts every raise. Path: Yoon Kim, President and Chief Strategy Officer since December 2024 (ex-SK Telecom CTO, Apple Siri), and co-founder Soyoung Lee, Head of Business Development. No CMO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Red Bull Ventures link.
“Jae, Red Bull Ventures backed you a month ago, and its racing teams sit on the most valuable video archive in sport nobody can search. Racing Bulls has no video partner. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $100M Series B, Amazon as preferred cloud and Red Bull Ventures on the cap table give TwelveLabs a fresh budget and a structural path into the Red Bull teams. The video-intelligence lane at Racing Bulls is open and the product would be used every race weekend.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 170 · 01 JUL 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 170 · HOT · F1

Together AI

AI Infrastructure · Open-Source AI Cloud / Inference · San Francisco (founded 2022) · Private ($8.3B post-money; $800M Series C, Jul 2026)

Together AI, the San Francisco cloud built for open-source AI, closed an $800M Series C at an $8.3B valuation on 1 July 2026, led by Aramco Ventures with Nvidia, Vista and General Catalyst: two and a half times its February 2025 price, with annual bookings past $1.15B.

The case

Together AI announced on 1 July 2026 an $800M Series C at an $8.3B post-money valuation, led by Aramco Ventures with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia, March Capital, Pegatron and S Ventures. Annual bookings topped $1.15B in the last quarter, with thousands of paying customers including Cursor, Cognition and Decagon. The $305M Series B at $3.3B, led by General Catalyst, closed only in February 2025. The company says its infrastructure footprint will grow roughly 50-fold over five years: for an infrastructure business, the brand-building moment arrives with the build-out.

The grid has already priced the neocloud archetype: CoreWeave became Aston Martin Aramco's Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in May 2025, Core Scientific and TWG AI opened on Cadillac's first roster, and Groq holds inference silicon on McLaren's. Aramco, the lead investor here, is both F1's Global Partner and the Aston Martin title, so the ecosystem knows the name; the seat, though, has to be one CoreWeave does not already hold.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 1 July 2026 Together AI announced an $800M Series C at an $8.3B post-money valuation, led by Aramco Ventures with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia, March Capital, Pegatron and S Ventures. This is a company release, not a press report, so the figures are confirmed.
Price up two and a half times in sixteen months
The $305M Series B at $3.3B, led by General Catalyst, closed in February 2025. Annual bookings passed $1.15B in the quarter before the Series C, with thousands of paying customers including Cursor, Cognition and Decagon. A company re-priced that fast, selling to developers and enterprises, has a story to tell and a budget to tell it with.
A build-out that needs a name
Management says the infrastructure footprint will grow roughly 50-fold over five years. An infrastructure brand is built while the capacity is built: the enterprise buyers, bankers and hyperscaler partners it must win are exactly the audience an F1 paddock assembles.
Calendar window
Brand budgets are set in the quarter after a raise and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US stages on which a San Francisco company would announce. Since this brief's date, IBM signed a $240M multi-year agreement (11 August 2026) to host a Together AI inference cluster on IBM Cloud from the first quarter of 2027, which strengthens the capacity story rather than changing the recommendation.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

Why Tgr Haas F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
The Haas technology roster is Toyota Gazoo Racing (title), Mphasis (IT services), CommScope and Ruckus (networking) and Infobip (cloud communications), joined in July 2026 by Exein for device-level security. There is no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner: Official AI Cloud Partner is a clean category, and Haas partnerships are priced below the front of the grid.
The American team
Haas is run from Kannapolis, North Carolina, and is the only US-owned team on the grid until Cadillac's arrival this season. A San Francisco company gets a home team for Miami, Austin and Las Vegas and a story that plays to the US enterprise market where its customers sit.
A team that will use the product
A team without a hyperscaler partner buys its compute at list price. Elastic GPU clusters for surrogate models, simulation and analytics, and private inference for engineering assistants, are consumed in the factory rather than displayed on the car, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
The ecosystem path
Aramco, the round's lead investor, is F1's Global Partner and the title partner at Aston Martin through 2028, so the sport already knows the name. That path leads into F1, not to a specific team: at Aston Martin the lane belongs to CoreWeave, which is why the recommendation is Haas.

Value To Tgr Haas F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Together Instant GPU Clusters are self-service and spin up in minutes; the Frontier AI Factory offers dedicated Blackwell clusters at scale. For Haas that means on-demand capacity for machine-learning surrogates, strategy and driver-in-the-loop simulation, and telemetry and video analytics between sessions, without capital tied up inside the cost cap.
Private inference for the engineering office
Open models fine-tuned on the team's own documentation and data, served from private endpoints, give engineers and strategists assistants that never send team data to a third-party model. That is the concrete product a team without a hyperscaler partner cannot buy cheaply elsewhere.
Commercial lift for the team
Together sells to developers, CTOs and hyperscalers. Its guest list at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas is enterprise buyers, investors and bankers: the audience Haas's B2B partners (Mphasis, CommScope, Infobip) want in the suite.
What the team gives back
Official AI Cloud Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at the three US rounds, and co-produced engineering content from Kannapolis for Together's developer channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Cloud Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the 50-fold build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in compute credits. Scope: sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, US-round hospitality, engineering content.

The askA 25-minute call with Vipul Ved Prakash before the United States GP to test appetite for a first sports partnership, agree an Austin or Las Vegas announcement window, and size an Official AI Cloud Partner entry against the Haas 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Vipul Ved Prakash
Co-Founder & CEO, Together AI · verified
Prakash co-founded Together AI in 2022 after selling Topsy to Apple and leading search and AI for Siri; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Kai Mak, Chief Revenue Officer, Charles Zedlewski, Chief Product Officer, Meicheng Shi, SVP Finance. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Aramco connection.
“Vipul, your lead investor is F1's Global Partner, and CoreWeave took its Aston Martin seat the year it listed. The American team has no compute partner. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
An $800M round at $8.3B, bookings above $1.15B and a 50-fold build-out put Together AI at peak brand-investment authority with an F1-literate lead investor. The compute lane at TGR Haas is open and the US rounds sit inside the planning window.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 175 · 30 JUN 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 175 · HOT · F1

Odyssey

Physical AI · World Models / Real-Time Simulation · Palo Alto, California (offices in London and Zurich) · Private ($310M Series B at $1.45B, Jun 2026)

Odyssey, the Palo Alto world-model lab founded by the Voyage and Wayve autonomy veterans, closed a $310M Series B at a $1.45B valuation on 17 June 2026, led by Natural Capital with Amazon, AMD Ventures, GV, EQT and IQT, and named AWS its preferred cloud provider.

The case

Odyssey announced on 17 June a $310M Series B at a $1.45B valuation, led by Natural Capital with Amazon, AMD Ventures, GV, EQT and IQT participating; total funding stands at $337M (Crunchbase). NVentures had backed the Series A only in February. Founded in 2023 by Oliver Cameron, who founded Voyage and ran product at Cruise, and Jeff Hawke, formerly of Wayve, the company ships physics-accurate world models, Odyssey-2 Max and the real-time Starchild-1, through an API. AWS becomes its preferred cloud provider, with Trainium chips in the mix.

A world model is a simulator that learns physics from video and runs in real time. That is a tool for a race team's simulation group, not a chatbot, and it arrives in the year the grid has to learn a new car from scratch. Odyssey has a Zurich office on Hinwil's doorstep, a founding team fluent in vehicles, and a fresh $310M that will be spent on being known to enterprise buyers.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 17 June 2026 Odyssey announced a $310M Series B at a $1.45B valuation, led by Natural Capital with Amazon, AMD Ventures, GV, EQT and IQT participating, and named AWS its preferred cloud provider. The release is the company's own (Business Wire) and TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE and HPCwire carried it the same day; total funding is $337M per Crunchbase.
Two rounds in four months
NVentures backed the Series A in February 2026; four months later the Series B priced the company at $1.45B. A lab that has re-priced that fast has a story to tell to enterprise buyers, robotics customers and the public markets, and the budget to tell it.
The product is a simulator
Odyssey-2 Max is a physics-accurate general world simulator; Starchild-1 runs in real time across modalities; Odyssey-2 Pro ships through an API. These are simulation products sold to robotics and long-horizon-simulation customers, which is the language a Formula 1 vehicle-dynamics group already speaks.
Calendar window
The Dutch and Italian GPs fall inside the six-to-ten-week window after the row's date, with the US GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP later in the year for the American audience. Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter; a pilot agreed before Monza can be announced in full for 2027.

Why Audi Revolut F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Audi's 2026 roster was built from nothing: Revolut as title partner, Extreme Networks, JigSpace, ElevenLabs and NinjaOne on the technology side, bp/Castrol, adidas and the rest. No partner covers vehicle-dynamics, driver-in-the-loop or world simulation, a lane the sponsor table shows almost no team has branded. Additive Industries and Hewlett Packard Enterprise left within the last twelve months, so engineering slots are being re-let.
Zurich to Hinwil
Odyssey keeps an office in Zurich; Audi's chassis operation is in Hinwil, in the same canton. A partner whose engineers can be at the simulator in an afternoon is worth more to a new works team than one flying in from California.
A team learning a new car
Audi's first Formula 1 season is also the first season of a new regulation set, with a Neuburg-built power unit and a Hinwil chassis. Simulation is where a new entrant closes the experience gap, and a technical partner that helps do it earns a story the team will tell on camera.
Why not the investor-linked teams
AMD's presence at Mercedes and GV's link to Google Cloud at McLaren would give Odyssey a warm path, but both rosters already carry AI and cloud incumbents, and both are priced at the top of the grid. Audi offers the open lane at a price a $310M company can carry.

Value To Audi Revolut F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
World models that learn physics from video can generate interactive track environments: new or resurfaced circuits for the driver-in-the-loop simulator before a laser scan exists, wet, dusk and night conditions on demand, and synthetic onboard footage to train the team's own vision analytics. Audi's Hinwil simulation group trials the API under engineering supervision; the deliverable is a working environment, not a demo.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner backed by Amazon, AMD and GV brings enterprise and robotics buyers, and their investors, into the Audi suite at Monza, Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Audi's technology partners want to meet.
Content and ecosystem
The simulator as a story: co-produced engineering content on how a new team builds a track it has never raced, a Formula 1 reference customer for Odyssey's enterprise sales, and an AWS-compute-to-Hinwil narrative the team can carry to its own partners.
What the team gives back
Official World Simulation Partner designation, sidepod or halo placement, naming of the simulation programme, Hinwil engineering content, driver and engineering access for Odyssey's channels, and hospitality at Monza, Austin and Las Vegas.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official World Simulation Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning Audi's first regulation cycle. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in model access and compute. Scope: sidepod or halo placement, naming of the simulation programme, Hinwil engineering content, hospitality at Monza, Austin and Las Vegas.

The askA 25-minute call with Oliver Cameron before the Italian GP to scope a paid simulation pilot with Audi's Hinwil group, agree what a 2027 Official World Simulation Partner entry would cost, and confirm who at Odyssey owns partnerships after the round.

Primary decision-maker

Oliver Cameron
Co-Founder & CEO, Odyssey · verified
Cameron founded Voyage, sold it to Cruise and ran product there; he fronts every Odyssey raise, and a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Jessica Inman, VP of GTM & Operations (commercial), and Jeff Hawke, Co-Founder & CTO (technical counterpart). No chief marketing officer or CFO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the simulator, not the logo.
“Oliver, your models learn physics from video and run in real time; Audi's Hinwil simulation group still builds its worlds by hand. You have a Zurich office and a fresh $310M to be seen with. 25 minutes before Monza to walk through a pilot?”
Bottom line
A $310M round at $1.45B backed by Amazon, AMD and GV, an AWS compute deal, and a Zurich office beside Formula 1's newest works team put Odyssey at peak authority to sign a first sports partnership. The world-simulation lane at Audi is open, and the pilot is real engineering work.

Risks & counters

UNPROVEN IN A RACE TEAM
No F1 team has used a generative world model in its simulator; Audi's engineers may see a research tool, not a product. Counter: Frame year one as a paid pilot with named deliverables; the partnership badge follows a working track environment.

About fifty people run a $1.45B company; a sponsorship can outrun the bandwidth to activate it. Counter: Keep the scope narrow: one workstream, one hospitality calendar, model access in kind.

Divergent Technologies

Digital Manufacturing · AI Design + Metal Additive + Robotic Assembly · Torrance, California · Private ($2.3B valuation, Series E, Sep 2025)

Divergent, the Torrance digital-manufacturing company whose printed titanium suspension sits on the McLaren W1, unveiled Monolith One, a twelve-laser metal printer, and a 430,000 sq ft second factory in Long Beach on 17 June 2026, an 8X step in output nine months after a $290M Series E at $2.3B.

The case

On 17 June Divergent announced Monolith One, a laser powder-bed printer with twelve 2kW lasers, and a second factory: 430,000 sq ft in Long Beach, California, 64 printers, production from early 2027, an 8X rise in annual output. It follows the $290M Series E closed on 15 September 2025 at a $2.3B valuation, led by Rochefort Asset Management, after a $230M Series D in November 2023. The platform, DAPS, pairs AI-enabled design with metal additive and robotic assembly, and has delivered 600+ unique parts for Lockheed Martin, RTX, McLaren, Aston Martin and Bugatti.

Divergent already builds the McLaren W1's Formula 1-inspired front suspension: titanium upper and lower wishbones and the upright, printed by Divergent under a multi-year collaboration with McLaren Automotive. The road-car side of the brand is a customer; the racing side, operationally separate under Zak Brown, is not yet a partner. A second factory needs a flagship to fill it, and a race car is the fastest proof a structural printer can give.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 17 June 2026 Divergent announced Monolith One, a laser powder-bed fusion printer with twelve 2kW lasers and a 700 x 700 x 835 mm build volume, and a second factory in Long Beach, California: 430,000 sq ft, 64 printers, about 1,000 jobs, an 8X increase in annual output, production from the first half of 2027. The release is Divergent's own; TCT, Metal AM, Breaking Defense and the Long Beach Post carried it.
Capital already in place
The $290M Series E closed on 15 September 2025 at a $2.3B valuation, led by Rochefort Asset Management with $120M of the round, on top of a $230M Series D in November 2023; total funding is reported at about $1.1B. The thin row scored the Series E as the trigger; it is nine months old. The fresh event is the factory, funded by that round.
A leadership team built in one month
Cooper Keller was promoted to Chief Operating Officer on 1 June, Brian Erhartic named Chief Technology Officer on 8 June and Ben Nicholson, from Ursa Major, appointed Chief Commercial Officer on 15 June. A company that hires its first CCO in the month it announces a factory is about to sell capacity, and a brand partnership is part of how it does that.
Calendar window
The British GP at Silverstone falls days after the row, the Dutch and Italian GPs inside the six-to-ten-week window, and the US GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP later in the year on Divergent's home ground. Teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
