Why Mclaren Mastercard F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
McLaren's 2026 roster is engineering-heavy, Dell Technologies, Cisco, Google Cloud, Groq, Arrow Electronics, Greene Tweed, Smartsheet, Workday, but the sponsor table shows no additive-manufacturing or digital-manufacturing partner. Stratasys supplies the team's polymer printing; metal structural components and robotic assembly are a different lane.
The warm path
McLaren Automotive's engineers worked with Divergent on the W1's titanium front upper wishbone, aero-form lower wishbone and front upright, printed by Divergent under a multi-year collaboration. McLaren Racing is a separate company, majority-owned by Bahrain Mumtalakat with CYVN Holdings, the owner of Automotive, holding a non-controlling stake, so the introduction runs through engineers who already trust the parts, not through a shared commercial team.
Why not the alternatives
Alpine carries 3D Systems as its additive partner. Haas is owned by a machine-tool brand, Haas Automation, whose identity a digital-manufacturing partner would cut across. Audi's Additive Industries relationship ended within the last 12 months, so the lane is open there, but Audi has no Divergent lineage. Aston Martin's road-car arm used DAPS for the DBR22 subframe and Mercedes-AMG is a customer too, so both are credible second choices; McLaren is where a live production programme already sits.
Story fit
The W1's suspension is described by McLaren as Formula 1-inspired. Putting the company that prints it onto the Formula 1 car closes the loop in a single sentence, and gives McLaren's technology-forward identity a manufacturing chapter it currently lacks.

It is the workflow that produced the W1's suspension, applied to a race car's fast-iteration parts; the value to the team is shorter design-to-track cycles and a second, US-based source of structural parts inside the cost cap.
Commercial lift for the team
Divergent's customers are aerospace primes, defence contractors and hypercar makers; its guest list at Austin and Las Vegas is an industrial and capital-markets audience that McLaren's technology partners want to meet.
Content and ecosystem

Entry as Official Digital Manufacturing Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the Long Beach ramp. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in printed parts and engineering time. Bloom Energy

On-Site Energy Generation · SOFC Systems · San Jose, California · NYSE: BE (2026 revenue guidance $3.4-3.8B)

Bloom Energy, the San Jose fuel-cell maker now powering AI data centres for Oracle, American Electric Power and Brookfield, signed a master agreement for up to 2.8 GW of its systems with Oracle on 13 April 2026 and posted a record first quarter, lifting 2026 revenue guidance to $3.4-3.8B.

The case

On 13 April Bloom and Oracle announced a master services agreement under which Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 GW of Bloom fuel-cell systems, 1.2 GW contracted. Two weeks later Bloom reported first-quarter revenue of $751.1M, up 130.4%, and raised 2026 guidance to $3.4-3.8B; total backlog is about $20B. American Electric Power exercised a $2.65B option for 900 MW in January, and Brookfield committed $5B in October 2025 to finance Bloom-powered AI data centres. A niche fuel-cell company has become the power supplier of the AI build-out, and its brand has not caught up.

The grid sells energy at scale, but every energy partner on it is a fuel or lubricant brand: Aramco at Aston Martin, Petronas at Mercedes, Shell at Ferrari, Eni at Alpine, Mobil 1 and Esso at Red Bull. No team carries an on-site power generation partner, even as factories add simulators, data halls and wind-tunnel hours that local grids were never sized for. Bloom's product is that: baseload power delivered in months, not years.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 13 April 2026 Bloom Energy and Oracle announced a master services agreement under which Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 GW of Bloom's fuel-cell systems, with 1.2 GW already contracted and deployment running into 2027. It is the largest single commitment in Bloom's history and it was announced by the company itself.
Record quarter, guidance raised
On 28 April Bloom reported first-quarter revenue of $751.1M, up 130.4% on the year, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $3.4-3.8B, roughly 80% growth at the midpoint. On the call the company put total backlog at about $20B, more than half of the data-centre portion from hyperscalers, neoclouds and colocation providers other than Oracle.
The order book behind it
American Electric Power exercised a $2.65B option for 900 MW of Bloom fuel cells on 8 January 2026 for a Wyoming data-centre campus, and Brookfield committed $5B in October 2025 to finance Bloom-powered AI data centres. A company selling power to the AI build-out in gigawatts is buying brand for the first time at scale; its CMO's stated brief is to build an iconic brand.
Calendar window
The US GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026, and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US, where Bloom's customers sit, and activated in full for 2027.

Why Atlassian Williams Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, Gulf in fuel, Duracell in consumer batteries, Komatsu in industrial equipment, VAST, Keeper, Airia and Brillio in technology. No power-generation or energy-infrastructure partner: Official Power Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price, without a title-level cheque.
A factory that needs power
Williams is in a phased modernisation of the Grove campus, adding new and larger factory, technology and testing facilities, offices and staff buildings, with a scoping opinion lodged with the district council. New buildings mean new load; on-site generation is a workstream the team would actually commission, not a logo.
Ownership and audience
Dorilton has invested heavily since taking ownership in 2020 and brought in James Vowles to run a data-led revival. A US-owned British team gives a San Jose industrial brand a home story on both sides of the Atlantic, and the Austin and Las Vegas suites put Bloom in front of the hyperscaler, utility and capital-markets guests it sells to.
Category discipline
Gulf and Duracell are energy-adjacent, so the category must be defined as stationary power generation from the first conversation; neither brand sells it. Aggreko supplies temporary power to the championship, not to a team, and does not block a team-level power partner.

Value To Atlassian Williams Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Bloom Energy Servers convert natural gas, biogas or hydrogen into electricity on site without combustion. For Grove that means resilient baseload for the simulator, data hall and wind-tunnel programme as the campus grows, delivered on Bloom's data-centre timescales (Oracle took its first system in 55 days) rather than a grid-upgrade timescale, with a lower-carbon footprint the team can report.
Commercial lift for the team
Bloom sells to CIOs, utility executives and infrastructure investors. Its guest list at Austin and Las Vegas is the audience Williams' B2B partners want in the suite, and a partner with a $3.4-3.8B revenue base is a credible multi-year counterparty.
Content and ecosystem
A factory-power story the team can tell on camera: how a Formula 1 campus is powered, what the new buildings draw, and how fuel cells fit a lower-carbon plan. For Bloom, a reference installation outside the data-centre world, and engineering content with a team known for data.
What the team gives back
Official Power Partner designation, rear-wing or engine-cover placement, naming of the factory's power plant, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, and driver and engineering access for Bloom's customer events.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Power Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the Grove build-out and the first Oracle gigawatts. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-deliverable as installed Energy Server capacity at Grove. Scope: rear-wing or engine-cover placement, naming of the factory's power plant, US-race hospitality, content on powering the campus.

The askA 25-minute call with KR Sridhar before the US GP to confirm the Grove workstream is real for Williams, agree an Austin announcement window, and size an Official Power Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

KR Sridhar
Founder, Chairman & CEO, Bloom Energy · verified
Sridhar founded Bloom in 2001; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Natalie Sunderland, CMO, briefed to build an iconic brand; Aman Joshi, EVP and Chief Commercial Officer since January 2024; Simon Edwards, CFO since April 2026, previously CFO then CEO of McLaren partner Groq.

Opening angle

Lead with the Oracle gigawatts and the Grove build.
“KR, Oracle is putting up to 2.8 GW of your servers under its AI factories; Williams is rebuilding Grove and has no power partner. Your new CFO watched Groq take a McLaren seat. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
Up to 2.8 GW with Oracle, a $2.65B AEP order, $5B from Brookfield and guidance of $3.4-3.8B put Bloom at peak brand-building capacity with a brand few outside energy know. Williams is expanding Grove and carries no power partner; the lane, the workstream and two US races line up before 2027 rosters close.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential

1KOMMA5°

1KOMMA5°, the Hamburg home-electrification group running Europe's largest residential virtual power plant, mobilised a €1bn customer-financing programme with European banks and investors on 17 June 2026 and, manager magazin reports, has its CEO on an IPO roadshow with 2026 revenue expected near €660M.

The case

On 17 June 1KOMMA5° announced, with European investors and banks, a financing programme of up to one billion euros so German homeowners can buy solar, storage, heat pumps and wallboxes on instalments of up to 25 years at 5.99%. Next day manager magazin reported IPO preparations, the CEO on a roadshow, and 2026 revenue projected around €660M with EBITDA profitability. The base is real: revenue of €520M in 2024, up from €450M, 2,500 staff, 170,000 systems installed, and €150M of pre-IPO financing led by CalSTRS in December 2024.

Formula E's team rosters carry energy majors and battery makers, not the home. Shell sits with Lola Yamaha ABT and owns sonnen, a direct rival in German home storage; TotalEnergies sits with DS Penske; Envision Group, a wind and battery group, owns Envision Racing; Castrol, a bp brand, is at Jaguar TCS Racing. No team carries a residential energy brand, yet Berlin, Zandvoort and Madrid are raced in countries where 1KOMMA5° sells.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 17 June 2026 1KOMMA5° announced, with leading European investors and banks, a financing volume of up to one billion euros so that homeowners in Germany can buy photovoltaic systems, battery storage, heat pumps and wallboxes on monthly instalments over terms of up to 25 years at 5.99%, with free early repayment. It is a customer-demand programme, not a corporate raise, and the company is subsidising it.
IPO preparations, reported
On 18 June manager magazin reported that 1KOMMA5° is preparing a possible IPO with its CEO already on a roadshow, and that 2026 revenue is projected at around €660M with profitability at EBITDA level. This is press reporting summarised by the company's investor eCAPITAL; the company has not confirmed a listing date, and the brief says so.
The base
Revenue was about €520M in 2024, up from €450M in 2023, with organic growth of 36%; the group has around 2,500 staff, more than 170,000 systems installed and operates in Germany, Sweden, Finland, Denmark, the Netherlands, Spain and Australia. The €150M pre-IPO financing of December 2024 was led by CalSTRS and extended in July 2025 by Sabancı Climate Ventures; the valuation has not been disclosed.
Calendar window
Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah E-Prix on 18-19 December 2026; partner rosters for the debut season are closed in the autumn. The 2027 European swing, Berlin E-Prix (8-9 May), Zandvoort E-Prix (18-19 June) and Madrid E-Prix (26-27 June), lands in three of 1KOMMA5°'s seven markets, in what the company hopes is its IPO year.

Why Mahindra Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Mahindra Racing's roster is Mahindra & Mahindra as title partner and Tech Mahindra in technology, nothing in energy, batteries or home electrification. Official Home Energy Partner is a clean category at a price a pre-IPO company can carry, on a team whose commercial list has room.
A horizon that matches
In November 2025 Mahindra Racing committed to race as a full manufacturer through the GEN4 era to 2030, building its own powertrain at Banbury. A three-season deal from the GEN4 debut sits inside that commitment, with a manufacturer that is not going anywhere.
No group conflict
The obvious German pairing, Porsche, sits inside the Volkswagen Group, whose energy subsidiary Elli launches a vehicle-to-grid tariff-and-charger offer for German households in the fourth quarter of 2026, a direct competitor to Heartbeat AI; Cupra Kiro shares the same parent. Mahindra has no European home-energy arm. Schröder's 2021 Porsche founder profile is a warm contact, not an open lane.
Where it races
Berlin, Zandvoort and Madrid in 2027 are in Germany, the Netherlands and Spain, three of 1KOMMA5°'s markets, and London and Monaco carry the investor audience a pre-IPO company wants in its hospitality. Formula E's city-centre format reaches homeowners, the buyer of a home energy system, in a way a permanent circuit does not.

Commercial lift for the team

Official Home Energy Partner designation, car and race-suit placement at every round, a content series with team engineers, hospitality at Berlin, Zandvoort, Madrid and London, and driver appearances at 1KOMMA5° showrooms in E-Prix cities.

Entry as Official Home Energy Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27 to 2028/29), covering the GEN4 debut and the listing window. Estimated €1.5-2.5M a year in cash and media. Scope: car and race-suit placement, a Heartbeat AI content series, Berlin and Zandvoort hospitality, showroom activations.

“Philipp, you have a billion euros to put into German homes and a roadshow to run; Mahindra Racing has no energy brand on the car and races Berlin, Zandvoort and Madrid in your IPO year. 25 minutes before the GEN4 season opens?”
Bottom line
A €1bn customer programme, a reported IPO roadshow and €520M of revenue give 1KOMMA5° the motive and the means for its first European brand platform. Mahindra Racing's roster has no energy brand, its GEN4 commitment runs to 2030, and Berlin, Zandvoort and Madrid in 2027 are 1KOMMA5°'s home markets.

Lime

Shared Electric Micromobility · E-bikes and E-scooters · San Francisco (about 230 cities, 29 countries) · Nasdaq: LIME (roadshow live; pricing expected next week)

Lime launched its IPO roadshow on 22 June: 6.96M shares at $24-$26, up to about $181M at a valuation of up to about $1.8B (Renaissance Capital), Nasdaq ticker LIME. A profitable, electric, city-centre mobility brand is about to become public in the cities where Formula E races.

The case

Lime announced the roadshow on 22 June with pricing expected the following week; Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan lead the books and Uber, holder of 24.4% pre-IPO, has indicated interest in up to $20M of shares. The business on sale is no longer a scooter story: FY2025 revenue was $886.7M, up 29%, with adjusted EBITDA of $218.1M and free cash flow of $103.8M, a third positive year, against a $59.3M net loss driven by debt costs. Proceeds repay a $115M term loan at 10% due in September 2026, which frees the cash flow behind it.

A newly listed consumer brand needs a public-market story about scale and cities, and Formula E races in Lime's cities. London, where Lime has served more than 400,000 customers, hosts the season finale on 15-16 August; Berlin and Madrid follow in the GEN4 season. No shared-mobility brand has ever raced on the grid, so the first one defines the category.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 22 June 2026 Lime announced the launch of its IPO roadshow: 6,956,522 shares (6,679,791 from Lime, 276,731 from selling stockholders) at $24-$26, listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as LIME, with Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan leading. Renaissance Capital sized the deal at up to $181M and a valuation of up to $1.8B; pricing was expected the following week.
The business behind the listing
FY2025 revenue was $886.7M, up 29%, adjusted EBITDA $218.1M, operating income $70.4M and free cash flow $103.8M, the third positive year. The $59.3M net loss is a debt-cost story: proceeds repay a $115M term loan at 10% due September 2026. After the listing Lime's cash flow is its own.
A public brand needs a public story
Uber, Lime's largest holder at 24.4%, has indicated interest in up to $20M of shares. A newly public consumer brand has to explain to investors and city governments why it belongs in the centre of cities. Formula E's street circuits in London, Berlin, Madrid, Miami and Austin are that argument on television.
Update since issue
The IPO priced on 30 June 2026 at $25, the mid-point, and trading began on 1 July; TechCrunch reported $167M raised at an implied valuation of about $1.66B (about $174M including selling stockholders). The London E-Prix on 15-16 August remains the first activation window; Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18-19 December.

Why Envision Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Envision Racing's roster is Envision Group (title), Sand Technologies, Teijin and Genpact. No Formula E team carries a shared-mobility, e-bike or e-scooter partner, so Official Micromobility Partner is a first-of-category designation at a team-partner price.
Climate identity
Envision Racing built its brand on the Race Against Climate Change programme; Lime's pitch to cities is car-trip replacement. The two stories are the same story, told to fans and to city halls.
Independent, not a works team
Six Formula E teams are owned by car makers or two-wheel makers (Jaguar, Nissan, Porsche, Cupra, Citroën, Mahindra, and Yamaha in the Lola entry). An independent team can put a scooter brand on the car without an OEM marketing department objecting.
London is home for both
Envision is British-based and the London E-Prix is its home race. Lime has served more than 400,000 London customers and runs both e-bikes and e-scooters there. A finale activation in August needs only a July decision.

Value To Envision Racing — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Race-week mechanics (Mode B)
Lime rider zones and ticket-holder ride credits at the London, Berlin and Madrid E-Prix; Envision-liveried e-bikes in each host city during race week; push and in-app messaging to riders in those cities. The team gets a city-wide presence for a city race.
Audience the roster lacks
Envision's partners are industrial and enterprise brands. Lime brings a consumer audience across about 230 cities and the Uber ecosystem behind its largest shareholder, which is reach the team cannot buy at this price elsewhere.
Content
Driver and team commutes on Lime, a season-long 'last mile to the grid' series, and a shared climate-impact scoreboard built from Lime's ride data and the team's Race Against Climate Change reporting.
What Envision gives back
Official Micromobility Partner designation, car and race-suit placement, host-city activation rights, hospitality at London and Berlin, and a public-company partner announcement timed to the GEN4 launch in December.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Micromobility Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, the whole first GEN4 cycle. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year plus in-kind fleet and ride credits. Scope: car and suit placement, host-city activation in Lime cities, app and rider communications, hospitality at London and Berlin.

The askA 25-minute call with Wayne Ting in the week after pricing to agree a London E-Prix activation for 15-16 August and size a three-season Official Micromobility Partner entry with Envision Racing for the GEN4 era.

Primary decision-maker

Wayne Ting
Chief Executive Officer, Lime · verified
Ting has run Lime since May 2020, joining in 2018 after four years at Uber including Chief of Staff to its CEO. Path: Joseph Kraus, President; Ann Gugino, CFO since December 2023; Hannah McClellan Richards, COO from June 2026. No chief marketing officer is listed among the executive officers.

Opening angle

Lead with the cities.
“Wayne, you are about to list a brand that lives in London, Berlin and Madrid, and Formula E races in all three. No mobility brand has ever been on that grid. 25 minutes after pricing to see how Envision would put Lime in the finale?”
Bottom line
A profitable electric mobility brand listing on Nasdaq this month, an open micromobility lane on every Formula E roster, and a season finale in its biggest European market eight weeks out. Envision Racing is the clean, independent, climate-led home; the deal is small, in-kind heavy and time-bound.

Baseten

AI Infrastructure · Inference Platform · San Francisco (founded 2019) · Private ($13B; $1.5B Series F, Jun 2026)

Baseten, the inference platform behind Cursor, Abridge and Lovable, announced a $1.5B Series F on 22 June in two tranches at $13B and $11B, led by Altimeter, Conviction and Spark Capital. It is the fourth raise in 18 months for a company whose revenue grew 20x in a year.

The case

Baseten's own release of 22 June puts the numbers on record: $1.5B across two tranches at $13B and $11B, co-led by Sands Capital and Wellington, with Greylock, IVP, Battery and D.E. Shaw Ventures behind them; more than $2B raised in total. The price has moved from $2.15B in September 2025 to $5B in January to $13B now. The platform serves more than 1 billion inference calls a day across 87 clusters on 18 clouds, revenue grew 20x in a year, and headcount is to triple in 2026 as the company builds an enterprise sales motion.

That last point is the opening. A developer-led brand that must now sell to CIOs needs a stage its rivals already occupy: CoreWeave took Aston Martin Aramco's AI cloud seat in May 2025 and Core Scientific sits on Cadillac's car. Baseten is the inference layer that runs on those clouds, not one of them, and it has no seat.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 22 June 2026 Baseten announced a $1.5B Series F in two tranches at $13B and $11B valuations, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction and Spark Capital and co-led by Sands Capital and Wellington Management, with Battery Ventures, Blackbird, D.E. Shaw Ventures, Durable Capital, Greylock, IVP, Verified Capital and 01A. Total raised now exceeds $2B (company release).
Six times the price in nine months
BOND led $150M at $2.15B in September 2025; IVP and CapitalG led $300M at $5B in January 2026; the June financing prices the company at up to $13B. Four raises in 18 months is a company that expects to be much larger, and public, soon.
From developers to enterprises
The release says headcount will triple in 2026 to meet enterprise demand, and the customer list (Abridge, Clay, Cursor, Lovable, Mercor, OpenEvidence) is AI-native companies rather than large enterprises. Selling to CIOs is a brand problem, which is what a Formula 1 partnership is for. Sacra estimates annualised revenue at about $600M as of March 2026; that is an estimate, not a company figure.
Calendar window
The US GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the US rounds left in 2026, and teams close their 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced at the American team's home race and activated in full for 2027.

Why Tgr Haas F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
TGR Haas F1 Team carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner with Mphasis (digital), CommScope (connectivity), Ruckus and Infobip on the technology side. No cloud, GPU or AI-inference partner: Official AI Inference Partner is a clean category at the lowest team-partner price on the grid.
A team that buys capacity
Haas runs the leanest engineering operation in Formula 1 and has always bought what others build, from Ferrari power units to Toyota's design and manufacturing services. An inference platform that removes the need to own GPUs is the same trade: capacity without capital.
American team, American company
Haas is the only US-owned team; Baseten is a San Francisco company entering enterprise sales in the US market. Austin is the team's home race and the natural announcement stage; Las Vegas and Miami follow.
Precedent without conflict
The grid has priced the archetype (CoreWeave at Aston Martin, Core Scientific at Cadillac) but those are clouds. Baseten runs on 18 clouds; it competes with none of the team's existing partners and would sit alongside Toyota's technical programme rather than under a hyperscaler's brand.

Value To Tgr Haas F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Serving the team's trained models at race weekends: race-strategy and tyre-degradation models, computer vision on pit-lane and onboard video, telemetry anomaly detection. Baseten hosts them from cloud regions near each circuit with autoscaling, so latency and cost fit a small team's weekend.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner selling to CIOs and AI-native founders brings a guest list of enterprise buyers and investors to Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Haas's B2B partners (Mphasis, CommScope, Infobip) want in the suite.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced engineering content on how a small team uses AI at the track; a reference customer for Baseten's enterprise sales; a developer programme around the team's public data that reaches Baseten's core audience.
What the team gives back
Official AI Inference Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the model-serving environment, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, driver and engineering access for Baseten's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Inference Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the enterprise build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in platform credits. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of the team's model-serving environment, US-race hospitality, engineering content with the Toyota programme.

The askA 25-minute call with Tuhin Srivastava before the US GP in Austin to test the enterprise-brand need, size an Official AI Inference Partner entry against TGR Haas F1 Team's 2027 roster, and agree an Austin announcement window.

Primary decision-maker

Tuhin Srivastava
CEO & Co-Founder, Baseten · verified
Srivastava co-founded Baseten in San Francisco in 2019 with Amir Haghighat (CTO), Philip Howes (Chief Scientist) and Pankaj Gupta, and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Matt Slagle, Chief Revenue Officer, who owns the enterprise motion. No CMO or CFO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the enterprise pivot.
“Tuhin, you have raised $1.5B to sell inference to enterprises, and CoreWeave already bought the Aston Martin seat to sell them compute. The American team has an open AI lane and its home race in October. 25 minutes before Austin to see how it prices?”

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 188 · 20 JUN 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 188 · HOT · F1

Eaton

Intelligent Power Management · Industrial Electrical Equipment · Dublin (operations run from the United States) · NYSE: ETN ($27.4B sales, 2025)

Eaton, the $27.4B intelligent-power group, agreed on 10 June 2026 to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana in a ~$5.1B Reverse Morris Trust, taking about $1.1B in cash. What remains is a pure electrical and aerospace company riding a 240% surge in US data-centre orders.

The case

On 10 June 2026 Eaton signed definitive agreements to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana in a Reverse Morris Trust valued at about $5.1B. Eaton shareholders keep at least 50.1% of the combined company, Eaton receives roughly $1.1B in cash, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. The vehicle heritage leaves; intelligent power stays. First-quarter sales were a record $7.5B, up 17%, Electrical Americas reached $3.6B, up 20%, data-centre orders rose about 240% and organic growth guidance went to 10%.

The identity reset arrives with money and a story: 2025 sales were a record $27.4B, and in March Eaton and NVIDIA unveiled the Beam Rubin DSX platform for 800-volt AI factories. Every F1 factory, wind tunnel and garage is a power problem, and from 2026 the cars draw about half their output electrically. The electrical-equipment category on the grid is held by two European rivals, Siemens and Schneider Electric; the American incumbent is absent.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 10 June 2026 Eaton signed definitive agreements to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana Incorporated in a Reverse Morris Trust. The transaction is valued at about $5.1B; Eaton shareholders will own at least 50.1% of the combined company and Eaton receives a cash distribution of about $1.1B. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
A company changing what it is
The vehicle and mobility heritage leaves with Dana. What remains is intelligent power: electrical equipment for data centres, utilities, buildings and industry, plus aerospace. A company that has just redrawn its perimeter has to tell customers, investors and recruits what it now stands for, and that is when brand budgets are re-cut.
Peak demand
First-quarter 2026 sales were a record $7.5B, up 17%; Electrical Americas reached $3.6B, up 20%, with data-centre orders up about 240% and sector backlog up 48%. In March Eaton and NVIDIA unveiled the Beam Rubin DSX platform for 800-volt AI factories. Eaton is selling into the largest capital build-out in the US economy and has raised 2026 organic growth guidance to 10%.
Calendar window
Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP (Austin) in late October and the Las Vegas GP in November are the US stages inside that window; a deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and launched in full when the Dana transaction closes in Q1 2027.

Why Cadillac F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Cadillac's inaugural 2026 roster is Claro, Core Scientific, IFS, Jim Beam, Tenneco, Tommy Hilfiger and TWG AI. There is no electrical-equipment, power or energy brand. Official Power Management Partner is a clean category on a team whose commercial inventory is still being built.
An American works team
Cadillac is the only entry owned by an American manufacturer, General Motors, with TWG Motorsports. Eaton is the incumbent US name in switchgear, UPS and power distribution, Dublin-domiciled but run from the United States. The pairing reads naturally in Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, where Eaton's utility, data-centre and industrial customers sit.
Three sites to power
A $200M, 400,000 sq ft headquarters is under construction in Fishers, Indiana; a power-unit facility runs in Concord, North Carolina; European operations are led from Silverstone. New buildings are specified once. A power partner who arrives during the fit-out becomes part of the building, not a sticker on it.
Rivals are elsewhere
Siemens sits on the rosters of both Red Bull teams and Schneider Electric joined McLaren for 2026. Neither can be displaced; Cadillac is the one competitive, well-funded team where the category has never been sold.

Value To Cadillac F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Medium-voltage switchgear, power distribution, uninterruptible power and circuit protection for the Fishers, Concord and Silverstone sites, with the same monitoring and energy-management layer Eaton sells to data-centre operators applied to dyno rooms, simulators and machine shops. Trackside, Eaton power-quality and backup equipment runs the garage and pit-wall systems at 24 rounds.
Commercial lift for the team
Eaton brings the buyers of the AI build-out, utilities, hyperscalers, contractors and industrial groups, to Cadillac's hospitality at the three US rounds, and a founding-partner story for a team whose inventory is still being priced.
Content and ecosystem
The build of an F1 headquarters from the switchgear up is a story Eaton can tell to every data-centre customer: engineering films from Fishers, a pit-wall power reference, and a case study that maps a race garage onto an AI factory.
What the team gives back
Official Power Management Partner designation, engine-cover or halo placement, hospitality at the United States GP, Miami GP and Las Vegas GP, driver and engineering access for Eaton's customer events.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Power Management Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, bridging the Dana closing and the first seasons of the pure-play Eaton. Estimated $5-8M a year, part in equipment and engineering. Scope: campus and trackside power infrastructure, engine-cover or halo branding, US-race hospitality, engineering content from the Fishers build.

The askA 25-minute call with Paulo Ruiz before the United States GP to size an Official Power Management Partner entry against Cadillac's 2027 roster, scope the Fishers and Silverstone power specification, and align the announcement with the Dana closing.

Primary decision-maker

Paulo Ruiz
Chief Executive Officer, Eaton · verified
Ruiz became CEO on 1 June 2025 after 18 years at Siemens and a start at Fiat; the Dana deal is his first major reshaping. Path: David Foster, EVP and CFO since 2 March 2026, and Heath Monesmith, President and COO, Electrical Sector. No CMO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the reshaping.
“Paulo, when Dana closes, Eaton is a pure power company for the first time. Cadillac is fitting out three sites and carries no power brand. 25 minutes before Austin to see what an American works team on Eaton power looks like?”
Bottom line
A $27.4B company becomes pure-play intelligent power in Q1 2027, with about $1.1B of cash and data-centre orders up 240%. Cadillac is fitting out three sites and its inaugural roster carries no electrical brand; the lane and the launch date are both open.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 190 · 16 JUN 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 190 · HOT · FE

Infineon Technologies

Power Semiconductors · Silicon Carbide / EV Traction · Neubiberg, Germany (Americas HQ Milpitas, California) · FSE: IFX (EUR 14.7B revenue, FY2025)

Infineon, the world's number one power-semiconductor maker, raised guidance on 6 May 2026 as AI data-centre demand surged, then on 8 June put its silicon carbide into Siemens' circuit breakers. Formula E's 600 kW GEN4 car debuts in December; the one team that has run a power-semiconductor partner has none.

The case

On 6 May 2026 Infineon reported second-quarter revenue of EUR 3.81B, up 6%, and raised fiscal 2026 guidance: revenue growing significantly, a segment result margin of about 20% and adjusted free cash flow of about EUR 1.65B, up from EUR 1.4B. AI data-centre revenue is expected at about EUR 1.5B this year and EUR 2.5B next. On 8 June it announced with Siemens that its silicon-carbide modules will sit inside Siemens' semiconductor circuit breakers. This is a EUR 14.7B, 57,000-person company at a demand peak, with a board-level chief marketing officer.

Silicon carbide lets an inverter switch faster and waste less, which in an electric race car is range and lap time. Jaguar first ran it in 2017 and made its US supplier Official Power Semiconductor Partner in 2023; that supplier went through Chapter 11 last year and is absent from the 2025/26 roster. GEN4 arrives in December with 600 kW, permanent all-wheel drive and 700 kW regeneration: the series' biggest power-electronics step.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 6 May 2026 Infineon raised its fiscal 2026 guidance: revenue now expected to grow significantly, a segment result margin of about 20%, adjusted free cash flow of about EUR 1.65B (from EUR 1.4B), with AI data-centre revenue expected at about EUR 1.5B this fiscal year and about EUR 2.5B next. On 8 June it announced with Siemens that its silicon-carbide power modules will be built into Siemens' semiconductor circuit breakers. The thin desk row called this a funding event; it is a peak-demand moment at a public incumbent, which is inside 1440's profile.
Peak demand meets a new identity
Infineon is telling the market that its power semiconductors sit at the centre of two build-outs at once: the AI data centre and the electric drivetrain. A company reframing itself from 'chip supplier' to 'the power behind electrification' needs a stage where that story is visible, and Formula E is the only championship whose whole product is the inverter.
The GEN4 window
GEN4 debuts at the Jeddah E-Prix on 18-19 December 2026 with 600 kW, permanent all-wheel drive, a 55 kWh battery and up to 700 kW of regeneration. Season 13 partner rosters close in the autumn. A partner agreed before the London E-Prix in August is on the car for the first race of a four-season era.
Calendar and markets
Season 13 visits Austin on 6 February 2027 and Miami on 20 February 2027, in the market where Infineon's Americas headquarters (Milpitas) and Austin site sit, and returns to Berlin in May, the home race for a Munich-area company.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

6%
EUR 14.7B in fiscal 2025; Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue EUR 3.81B, up 6%
20%
Full-year guidance raised on 6 May 2026 (revenue now to grow significantly; segment result margin about 20%…

Why Jaguar Tcs Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Jaguar TCS Racing's roster in the sponsor table is TCS (title and technology), Castrol and Jaguar's own powertrain; the 2025/26 livery release adds Dow, Reflo, Alpinestars and Chase. No semiconductor or electronics brand. The team ran a US silicon-carbide supplier as Official Power Semiconductor Partner from 2023; that company went through Chapter 11 in 2025 and is not named on the current roster.
The team that proved the material
Jaguar first used silicon carbide in its Formula E inverter in 2017 and has spoken about it publicly ever since. Selling Infineon into Jaguar is not an education job: the engineers already know what the technology is worth in efficiency and lap time.
Committed for the whole era
Jaguar TCS Racing has signed for the GEN4 era, Seasons 13 to 16, from 2026. A three-season partnership sits entirely inside a period the team has already committed to, with a road-car parent (JLR) whose next electric models are the transfer story.
Where the rivals are
The electronic-components cluster at DS Penske (Mouser Electronics, TTI, Molex, KYOCERA AVX) makes that team a distributor showcase rather than a semiconductor lane; the works teams Porsche and Nissan carry only their parent brands and their own supplier relationships. Jaguar is the one team where a power-semiconductor partner has a precedent and an empty seat.

Value To Jaguar Tcs Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
CoolSiC silicon-carbide power modules and gate drivers for the GEN4 traction inverters, where switching losses and thermal headroom decide how much of 600 kW reaches the tyres and how much of 700 kW regeneration comes back; application engineering on inverter topology and cooling; silicon carbide for the team's charging and pit-garage power equipment. Infineon's HybridPACK Drive family already runs on more than 20 EV platforms.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to every carmaker and every hyperscaler brings an automotive and data-centre guest list to Austin, Miami and Berlin, and a component-level technical partnership that TCS and Castrol can build joint content around.
Content and ecosystem
The inverter is Formula E's least visible and most important component. An engineering series from the dyno to the E-Prix, with Jaguar's power-electronics engineers, gives Infineon the visible story behind 'the power behind electrification' and gives the team technical content its title partner can amplify.
What the team gives back
Official Power Semiconductor Partner designation, halo and rear-wing placement, hospitality at the Austin, Miami and Berlin E-Prix, driver and engineering access for Infineon's customer events and PCIM-week activations.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Power Semiconductor Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15 (2026-2029), inside the GEN4 era. Estimated EUR 3-5M a year, part in components and engineering. Scope: inverter modules and support, halo and rear-wing branding, Austin, Miami and Berlin hospitality, technical content.

The askA 25-minute call with Andreas Urschitz before the London E-Prix to size an Official Power Semiconductor Partner entry for Seasons 13-15, scope the GEN4 inverter workstream with Jaguar's engineers, and settle the road-car supplier question up front.

Primary decision-maker

Andreas Urschitz
Chief Marketing Officer, Member of the Management Board, Infineon · verified
Urschitz has sat on the Management Board as Chief Marketing Officer since 2022, with a mandate to 2030; brand and sponsorship are his call. Path: Jochen Hanebeck, CEO since 2022, and Sven Schneider, CFO since 2019. Infineon last bought motorsport with the Infineon Raceway naming rights, 2002-2012.

Opening angle

Lead with the empty lane.
“Andreas, Jaguar proved silicon carbide in Formula E and its power-semiconductor partner has gone. GEN4 is a 600 kW car in December and Infineon is number one in the material. 25 minutes before London to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A EUR 14.7B power-semiconductor leader at peak demand, a board-level CMO, and the one Formula E team that has run a power-semiconductor partner now without one, five months before a 600 kW car arrives. Warm rather than hot: no capital event, but the lane and the calendar line up.

Risks & counters

ROAD-CAR SUPPLIER TENSION
JLR contracted its road-car silicon carbide to Wolfspeed in 2022, and Infineon buys wafers from Wolfspeed. Counter: Position Infineon as the GEN4 racing partner, separate from road-car supply; the wafer link makes it familiar, not a rival.
NO SPORT SINCE 2012
Infineon has not bought a sports property since the raceway naming rights lapsed; appetite is unproven. Counter: Anchor on the engineering workstream and the CMO's board mandate; a component-level deal is cheaper than a circuit name.

Ramp

Corporate Cards / Spend Management · Expense Software · New York (offices in Miami and San Francisco) · Private ($44B; $750M Series F, Jun 2026)

Ramp, the New York corporate-card and spend-management platform, announced a $750M Series F at a $44B valuation on 4 June 2026, led by ICONIQ, GIC and Ontario Teachers', nearly tripling its $16B mark of a year ago. It has passed $1B in annualized revenue and is free-cash-flow positive.

The case

On 4 June 2026 Ramp announced a $750M primary Series F at a $44B valuation, led by ICONIQ, GIC and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, with Goldman Sachs Alternatives, D.E. Shaw, Morgan Stanley Investment Management and Insight Partners joining. The company says it has surpassed $1B in annualized revenue, is free-cash-flow positive and serves more than 70,000 businesses, among them Visa, Uber, Shopify, Anduril and Figma; Bloomberg puts run-rate revenue above $1.5B. In March it bought Billhop to open London and Stockholm offices and onboard UK- and EU-headquartered businesses directly from summer 2026.

Ramp has started buying sport: in April it became Official Exclusive Corporate Card of The Snow League in a multi-season deal. Its cards run on the Visa network and Visa is a customer. Fintech is the fastest-growing category on the grid, but this lane is corporate cards and spend software, not consumer payments, and it belongs to no team. Note: the 1440 human layer has already approached Ramp; this brief refreshes that conversation.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 4 June 2026 Ramp announced a $750M primary Series F at a $44B valuation, led by ICONIQ, GIC and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, with Goldman Sachs Alternatives, D.E. Shaw & Co., Morgan Stanley Investment Management, Generation Investment Management, Insight Partners and BroadLight Capital as new investors. The company states it has surpassed $1B in annualized revenue and is free-cash-flow positive; Bloomberg reports run-rate revenue above $1.5B.
Price nearly tripled in a year
Ramp was valued at $16B in June 2025. A company re-priced to $44B in twelve months has a public-market story to build and a budget to build it with; the investor list (pension funds, sovereign wealth, crossover managers) is the roster of a company preparing for a listing.
Europe opens this summer
Ramp acquired Billhop, a UK- and Sweden-licensed payments platform, on 13 March 2026, is opening its first international offices in London and Stockholm, and begins onboarding businesses headquartered in the UK and EU directly from summer 2026. A European team partner announced in the same quarter is the launch campaign.
Calendar window
Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The Italian GP in September is Racing Bulls' home race; the United States GP (Austin) in late October and the Las Vegas GP in November are the US stages where Ramp's customers and investors sit. A deal agreed before Monza can be announced at home and activated in the US.

Why Visa Cash App Racing Bulls — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Racing Bulls carries Visa and Cash App as title partners, with Siemens, Dynatrace, Confluent, Randstad, Tudor and Hugo on the roster. The team profile lists spend management as an open category that complements Visa rather than conflicting with it. Official Corporate Card and Spend Management Partner is a clean designation.
The warm path
Ramp's cards are Visa cards, issued by Sutton Bank under a Visa licence, and Visa itself is a Ramp customer. The introduction runs through the title partner, and the activation puts a Visa-network card programme on the Visa-titled car rather than a competing scheme.
A team that will use the product
A travelling team of a few hundred people at 24 rounds generates the expense, procurement and vendor-payment load Ramp is built for, under a cost cap that rewards real-time spend control. The platform is consumed in the finance office, not just displayed on the sidepod.
Audience and geography
Racing Bulls is the younger, digital-first team in the Red Bull family; Ramp sells to founder-led companies. The team is based in Italy, which makes it the first European customer reference Ramp can name as it opens London and Stockholm.

Intelligence Brief / N° 193 · HOT · F1

UiPath

Enterprise Software · Agentic Automation · New York (founded in Bucharest, 2005) · NYSE: PATH

UiPath, the New York-headquartered enterprise-automation company, reported on 28 May 2026 the first GAAP-profitable quarter in its history: revenue of $418M, up 17%, ARR of $1.901B and $1.42B of cash, with a chief marketing officer nine months into rebuilding the brand around agentic AI.

The case

On 28 May UiPath reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $418M, up 17% year on year, ARR of $1.901B and GAAP operating income of $28M, its first GAAP-profitable quarter. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities stood at $1.42B and the board authorised a $500M buyback in March; full-year guidance is $1.776-1.781B of revenue. Founder Daniel Dines returned as CEO in June 2024 and has re-positioned the company around agentic automation: software robots, AI agents and orchestration in one governed system. Marketing sits with Michael Atalla, CMO since August 2025 after F5 and fifteen years at Microsoft.

The enterprise-software archetype is already priced on the grid: ServiceNow sits with Aston Martin Aramco, SAP with Mercedes, and Salesforce is a Formula 1 global partner. UiPath has never held a motorsport position. A first profitable quarter, a founder back in the chair and a new CMO with a brand to rebuild is the moment a public software company can justify a global platform to its board.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 28 May 2026 UiPath reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $418M, up 17% year on year, ARR of $1.901B and GAAP operating income of $28M: the first GAAP-profitable quarter in the company's history. The release is UiPath's own, filed with the SEC, so the figures are VERIFIED rather than reported.
Budget exists
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $1.42B at 30 April 2026, the board authorised a $500M buyback in March, and full-year guidance is $1.776-1.781B of revenue with about $430M of non-GAAP operating income. A multi-year team partnership is well inside the marketing budget of a business this size.
A CMO with a brand to rebuild
Michael Atalla became Chief Marketing Officer on 25 August 2025, hired to position UiPath as the leader in agentic AI and orchestration after the founder's return as CEO. Nine months in, he is building his first full fiscal-year plan; UiPath's fiscal 2028 starts on 1 February 2027, which is when a 2027 partnership would go live.
Calendar window
The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American team's home rounds and the two US races left in 2026; teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A conversation opened in June can be sized over the summer and announced in Austin for 2027.

The open lane
Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner with Mphasis (services), Haas Automation (machine tools), Ruckus (networking) and CommScope on the technology side. There is no enterprise-automation, AI-agent or workflow partner, so Official Enterprise Automation Partner is a clean category. Emburse became the team's travel-and-expense partner in June 2026, so the UiPath workstream is scoped to freight, procurement and cost-cap reporting rather than expenses.
The right price point
McLaren, Mercedes and Aston Martin already sell the enterprise-software story at top-tier prices to Workday, SAP and ServiceNow. Haas offers the same paddock and broadcast reach at a team-partner entry point suited to a public company's first motorsport commitment.
Audience and geography
An American team headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina, with three US races (Miami, Austin, Las Vegas) fits a New York-headquartered brand selling to the Global 2000; the Banbury and Maranello sites give the story a European and Italian leg.
A team that would use the product
The leanest team on the cost cap is the customer that most needs back-office hours turned into car spend. That is a real reference customer, not a logo, and it is what a documented case study needs.

Official Enterprise Automation Partner designation, sidepod placement, driver access, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, and a documented operational programme.

Entry as Official Enterprise Automation Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, aligned to UiPath's fiscal years from February 2027. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-deliverable as platform licences. Scope: sidepod placement, driver access, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, a cost-cap automation case study.

Bottom line
A first GAAP-profitable quarter on 28 May, $1.42B of cash and a CMO rebuilding the brand around agentic AI give UiPath the budget and the motive; the automation lane at Haas is open and the two US rounds sit inside the window.

Helion Energy

Fusion Energy · Clean Power Generation · Everett, Washington (founded 2013) · Private ($15.5B post-money; $465M Series G, Jun 2026)

Helion, the fusion company building the world's first fusion power plant for Microsoft, announced on 4 June 2026 a $465M Series G led by Thrive Capital at a $15.5B valuation, nearly triple its January 2025 mark, taking total funding to $1.5B as it moves from lab milestone to construction site.

The case

On 4 June Helion announced a $465M Series G led by Thrive Capital at a $15.5B post-money valuation, with Lux Capital, Peak XV, BoxGroup and Bill Ford joining Lightspeed, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Good Ventures; total raised is $1.5B, nearly triple the $5.425B set by the $425M Series F in January 2025. The story is physical: Orion, the first fusion power plant, has been under construction in Malaga, Washington since July 2025 to supply Microsoft by 2028, and in February Polaris became the first private machine to demonstrate deuterium-tritium fusion at 150 million degrees.

Fusion is the definitive clean-energy story and Formula E is the championship built to prove clean mobility; pairing the two is the most on-message sustainability partnership on any grid, and Helion has never touched motorsport. The energy lane belongs to incumbents: Shell sits with Lola Yamaha ABT, TotalEnergies with DS Penske, Castrol with Jaguar. The counterweight: Helion is pre-revenue and pouring capital into reactors, so this is a measured brand and talent platform.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 4 June 2026 Helion announced a $465M Series G led by Thrive Capital at a $15.5B post-money valuation, with Lux Capital, Peak XV Partners, BoxGroup, Anti Fund, Alta Park Capital and Bill Ford joining Lightspeed, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Mithril, Capricorn and Good Ventures. Total raised is $1.5B. The release is Helion's own, so the figures are VERIFIED.
Valuation nearly tripled in seventeen months
The $425M Series F of 28 January 2025 valued Helion at $5.425B; the Series G nearly triples that. A company re-priced this fast has a story to tell to utilities, regulators, hyperscaler customers and the talent it is hiring, and a budget to tell it with.
From lab to construction site
Orion, the first fusion power plant, has been under construction in Malaga, Chelan County, Washington since July 2025 under the world's first fusion power purchase agreement, supplying Microsoft by 2028 at 50 MW or more. In February 2026 Polaris became the first privately developed machine to demonstrate deuterium-tritium fusion and reach 150 million degrees Celsius. Each milestone from here is a moment a partnership can be timed to.
Calendar window
Season 13, the GEN4 era, opens with the Jeddah E-Prix double-header on 18-19 December 2026; the Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027 is a new US round and the Miami E-Prix follows on 20 February. Teams are setting partner rosters for the new car now, so a deal agreed over the summer launches with GEN4.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti Formula E carries TWG AI as primary partner and Official AI Partner, Quest Global on engineering services, Crowe UK and Reflo, with Andretti Global and TWG Motorsports as parents. There is no energy, power or fuel partner: Official Clean Energy Partner is a clean category with exclusivity available.
The American team for a US audience
Helion's next customers and gatekeepers are US utilities, hyperscalers and state and federal regulators. Andretti is the American entry on the grid, Austin and Miami are the two US rounds, and the Andretti name carries in Washington and Indianapolis in a way no European works team can match.
Why not the sustainability-first independent
Envision Racing is the obvious thematic match, but it is owned by Envision Group, a wind-turbine, storage, green-hydrogen and battery company whose entire purpose for the team is to carry its own energy story. A fusion brand on that car competes with the owner's message.
A path to a bigger stage
TWG Motorsports, Andretti's parent, also owns the Cadillac F1 Team. A Formula E relationship that works gives Helion a known counterparty for a Formula 1 conversation when Orion is delivering power.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Narrative (Mode B)
Fusion is the definitive clean-energy story and Formula E is the championship built to prove clean mobility. Co-produced content pairing the first fusion power plant with the first GEN4 season gives Andretti the grid's strongest sustainability narrative and Helion a global stage as it moves from lab to grid.
Audience the team can sell
Hospitality at Austin and Miami for utilities, hyperscaler energy buyers, regulators and investors is a guest list Andretti's other B2B partners want in the suite, and it is the audience Helion has to win for offtake and licensing.
Talent and STEM
Helion is hiring physicists and engineers at speed; a joint recruiting and STEM programme built on the team's engineering content gives both sides a measurable outcome that does not depend on signage.
What the team gives back
Official Clean Energy Partner designation with category exclusivity, livery presence sized to the fee, driver and engineering access, GEN4 launch content and Austin and Miami hospitality.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Clean Energy Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, spanning Orion's construction and its 2028 delivery to Microsoft. Estimated $1.5-3M a year, sized to a pre-revenue company and stepped up at first power. Scope: energy-category exclusivity, GEN4 content, Austin and Miami hospitality, a talent programme.

The askA 25-minute call with David Kirtley before the Season 13 roster closes to test a milestone-linked Official Clean Energy Partner entry at Andretti Formula E, launching with GEN4 in December and stepping up at Orion's first power.

Primary decision-maker

David Kirtley
Founder & CEO, Helion Energy · verified
Kirtley founded Helion in 2013 and fronts every raise, customer deal and milestone; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Pragav Jain, CFO since July 2024 (ex-Waymo, Goldman Sachs), and Savanna Thompson, Chief Business Operations Officer. No CMO listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the stage, not the signage.
“David, fusion is the clean-energy story and Formula E is the stage built to prove clean mobility. No energy brand sits with the American team, and Austin joins the calendar in February. 25 minutes on a milestone-linked partnership before the Season 13 opener?”
Bottom line
A $465M round at $15.5B on 4 June, a licensed fusion plant under construction for Microsoft and a first-of-its-kind Polaris result put Helion at peak brand-investment visibility; the clean-energy lane at the American Formula E team is open as the GEN4 era and a new Austin E-Prix arrive.

TensorWave

AI Infrastructure · GPU Cloud (all-AMD) · Las Vegas, Nevada (founded 2023) · Private ($1.55B; $350M Series B, Jun 2026)

TensorWave, the Las Vegas-based all-AMD GPU cloud, announced on 10 June 2026 a $350M Series B at a $1.55B valuation co-led by Magnetar and AMD Ventures, almost four times the price of its $100M Series A thirteen months earlier, with an 8,192-GPU cluster live and 2 GW of capacity secured.

The case

On 10 June TensorWave announced a $350M Series B at a $1.55B valuation, co-led by Magnetar and AMD Ventures with Maverick Silicon, Nexus Venture Partners and Western Frontier; the same leads backed the $100M Series A of May 2025 at a reported $400M. The capital funds AMD Instinct MI355X clusters on top of an 8,192-GPU MI325X training cluster already live and more than 2 GW of data-centre capacity secured. Revenue is reported only: the 2025 release projected a run rate above $100M by year-end. Founded in Las Vegas in 2023, it is AMD's flagship challenger in the cloud.

The grid has priced this archetype: CoreWeave became Aston Martin Aramco's Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in May 2025 and Core Scientific sits with Cadillac. Both run Nvidia silicon; TensorWave is the AMD alternative, and AMD, its co-lead investor, is already a partner of Mercedes. A neocloud that has just quadrupled its price needs enterprise buyers, not only AI labs, and a home race in Las Vegas in November.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 10 June 2026 TensorWave announced a $350M Series B at a $1.55B valuation, co-led by Magnetar and AMD Ventures with Maverick Silicon, Nexus Venture Partners and Western Frontier. The release is the company's own on Business Wire, so the round and valuation are VERIFIED; the revenue figure is not, and the brief says so.
Price quadrupled in thirteen months
The $100M Series A of May 2025 valued the company at a reported $400M; the Series B is almost four times that. A company re-priced this fast has a story to tell to enterprise buyers, bankers and the public markets, and a budget to tell it with.
Capacity is real
An 8,192-GPU AMD Instinct MI325X training cluster is live, more than 2 GW of long-term data-centre capacity is secured, and the new capital funds MI355X clusters. Each cluster that goes live is a milestone the partnership can be timed to.
Calendar window
The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026; Las Vegas is TensorWave's home city. Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed before Austin can be announced at home and activated in full for 2027.

Why Tgr Haas F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner with Mphasis (services), Ruckus (networking), CommScope and Haas Automation on the technology side. No cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner: Official AI Compute Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The American team for a Las Vegas company
Haas is headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina, and races three US rounds (Miami, Austin, Las Vegas). For a Las Vegas company selling to US enterprises, the Las Vegas GP is a home race on the only American team.
Where compute in kind counts most
The leanest team on the cost cap is the one where elastic GPU capacity delivered as part of the fee changes what the engineering team can do. That makes Haas a reference customer, not a logo, which is what TensorWave's enterprise sellers need.
The incumbents elsewhere
CoreWeave at Aston Martin, Core Scientific at Cadillac, Google Cloud and Dell at McLaren, Oracle at Red Bull, Microsoft at Mercedes and Alpine, HP and IBM at Ferrari: every other large team carries a cloud or compute partner. Williams and Audi are open but offer no US or Las Vegas thread.

Value To Tgr Haas F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Compute for the work outside the aerodynamic-testing restrictions: machine-learning surrogates, driver-in-the-loop and race-strategy simulation, telemetry and video analytics between sessions. TensorWave supplies AMD Instinct GPU capacity on demand, part of it as credits inside the fee, so the team buys capability without capital.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to CIOs, AI labs and enterprises brings a guest list of technology buyers, investors and bankers to Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Haas's other B2B partners want in the suite.
Content and ecosystem
A data-centre-to-pit-wall story the team can tell on camera; a documented factory reference customer for TensorWave's enterprise sales; and a bridge into AMD's ecosystem of software and silicon partners.
What the team gives back
Official AI Compute Partner designation, engine-cover or sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, driver and engineering access for TensorWave's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Compute Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the MI355X build-out. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in compute credits. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of the team's compute environment, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, engineering content.

The askA 25-minute call with Darrick Horton before the United States GP to size an Official AI Compute Partner entry at Haas, part-paid in compute credits, with a Las Vegas GP announcement window and full activation from 2027.

Primary decision-maker

Darrick Horton
Co-Founder & CEO, TensorWave · verified
Horton co-founded TensorWave in Las Vegas in 2023 and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Piotr Tomasik, Co-Founder, President and COO, and Jeff Tatarchuk, Co-Founder and Chief Growth Officer. No CMO or CFO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Las Vegas home race.
“Darrick, CoreWeave took its seat at Aston Martin the year it listed; the AMD story has no seat, and the American team's compute lane is open. Las Vegas is your home race. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers in kind?”
Bottom line
A $350M round at $1.55B on 10 June, a live 8,192-GPU cluster and 2 GW of secured capacity put TensorWave at peak brand-investment authority; the compute lane at the American team is open and its home race in Las Vegas sits inside the window.

Honeywell Aerospace

Aerospace · Avionics, Propulsion & Electrification · Phoenix, Arizona · Nasdaq: HONA (regular-way from 29 Jun 2026; HONAV when-issued from 15 Jun)

Honeywell Aerospace, the $17.4B-revenue avionics, engines and electrification supplier, becomes a standalone Nasdaq company on 29 June 2026: Honeywell's board set the 15 June record date on 5 June, and the separation gives one of aviation's biggest suppliers its own balance sheet, ticker and brand budget for the first time.

The case

Honeywell announced on 5 June that its board has set 15 June 2026 as the record date for the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace, with distribution on 29 June on a one-for-two basis; the shares trade when-issued as HONAV from around 15 June and regular-way on Nasdaq as HONA from 29 June. The business reported 2025 net sales of $17.4B, up 12% organically, led by commercial aftermarket and defence. Headquartered in Phoenix, it is led by Jim Currier as President and CEO with Josh Jepsen as CFO, chaired by former Eaton chief Craig Arnold.

Aerospace is already on the grid: Boeing sits on the Alpine, Atlas Air on the Aston Martin, and Bombardier, a Honeywell customer, has left the Aston Martin roster. The engines-and-avionics tier has never taken a seat. That leaves a supplier-grade engineering story, from megawatt electric machines to thermal management, without a grid home just as Formula 1's new hybrid era begins and a British team starts its Honda power-unit years.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 5 June 2026 Honeywell's board set 15 June as the record date for the spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace and confirmed distribution at 12:01 a.m. New York time on 29 June, one Honeywell Aerospace share for every two Honeywell shares. When-issued trading as HONAV starts on or about 15 June; regular-way trading on Nasdaq as HONA on 29 June. The Form 10 was filed on 3 March.
A brand that must stand on its own
Until 29 June the aerospace business has been a segment of a conglomerate; from that day it has its own investors, its own annual report and its own marketing budget. Spin-offs spend their first hundred days establishing an identity with investors, customers and recruits, and that is the budget a team partnership would come from.
Scale, honestly
The business reported 2025 net sales of $17.4B, up 12% organically, led by commercial aftermarket and defence and space. Capacity is not the question; appetite is. No Honeywell Formula 1 sponsorship is on record and no chief marketing officer is named, which is why the score stops at 71 despite a hard listing date inside the window.
Calendar window
Regular-way trading begins the day after the Austrian GP on 28 June; the British GP on 5 July is the first race weekend as an independent company, at the home of the recommended team. The United States GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP follow in the autumn near the Phoenix headquarters and the US investor base.

Why Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Aston Martin Aramco carries Aramco as title partner, Honda supplying the power unit from 2026, Atlas Air in the cargo-aviation lane, and Arm, CoreWeave, NetApp, Cognizant and ServiceNow on technology. Bombardier, a business-jet maker and Honeywell customer, has departed, so no aerospace-engineering brand is on the car: Official Aerospace Technology Partner is a clean category.
The only aerospace-shaped roster
Boeing sits on the Alpine, which closes that car to a supplier that sells to Boeing and its rivals alike. No other team carries an aerospace or aviation story on the livery; Aston Martin already has one through Atlas Air and its former business-jet partnership, so the audience and the hospitality format exist.
The hybrid-era engineering story
Formula 1's 2026 rules lean harder on the electrical side of the power unit. Honeywell's 1-megawatt aerospace generator ran at 1.02 MVA and 900 kW continuously at about 97% efficiency and roughly 8 kW/kg, and doubles as a motor. The regulated power unit is Honda's, but thermal management, test rigs and electrical engineering exchange with the Silverstone campus are open ground.
UK and US at once
A Phoenix-headquartered, Nasdaq-listed company with a British team gives the US rounds a home-market story and the British GP a first-weekend stage; Honeywell Aerospace's UK sites and European airline customers give the Silverstone hospitality a customer list.

Value To Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Brand launch (Mode B)
A new listed company's identity told through precision engineering on a global broadcast in its first hundred days: the Honeywell Aerospace name on the car from the British GP, the first race weekend after the 29 June listing, with the US rounds in Austin and Las Vegas timed to the first results as an independent company.
Engineering exchange, outside the regulated unit
Thermal-management and electrical-machine know-how from the 1-megawatt generator programme applied to test rigs, cooling and energy-store integration at the AMR Technology Campus, with the homologated power unit left to Honda; a joint engineering series for the team's channels.
Commercial lift for the team
Airline, defence, business-aviation and institutional-investor guests at the British GP and the US rounds, the audience Aston Martin's Aramco and technology partners already court, plus a reference story for the team's own aerospace-grade supply chain.
What the team gives back
Official Aerospace Technology Partner designation, sidepod placement, British GP and US-round hospitality, driver and engineering access, and a first-year brand-launch activation timed to the 29 June listing.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Aerospace Technology Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, the company's first three years as a listed business. Estimated $5-8M a year. Scope: sidepod placement, the engineering exchange above, hospitality at the British GP and the US rounds for airline, defence and investor guests.

The askA 25-minute call with Jim Currier before the 15 June record date to ask who owns brand at the new company, test appetite for a first-race-weekend announcement at the British GP, and size an Official Aerospace Technology Partner entry against Aston Martin's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

James Currier
President & CEO, Honeywell Aerospace · verified
Currier, 60, has run Honeywell's aerospace business since August 2023 and led it into the spin-off. Path: Josh Jepsen, CFO since February 2026 (ex-Deere), and business-unit presidents Bob Buddecke, Dave Marinick and Rich DeGraff. No chief marketing officer is named in the spin-off filings.

Opening angle

Lead with the first race weekend as an independent company.
“Jim, Honeywell Aerospace trades on its own from 29 June and the British GP is its first race weekend as a listed company. Aston Martin's aerospace lane is open and the hybrid era needs your electrification story. 25 minutes before the record date?”
Bottom line
A $17.4B business listing on its own on 29 June, an open aerospace-engineering lane at Aston Martin and a British GP a week later give Honeywell Aerospace a clean brand-launch play. It scores 71: no marketing owner is named, the halo is B2B, and the power-unit rules limit what can run on the car.

Risks & counters

NO MARKETING OWNER
No chief marketing officer is named in the Form 10 or the spin-off releases; no obvious sponsor sits below the CEO. Counter: Go straight to Currier with a spin-off brand-launch framing and ask who owns brand.
SUPPLIER, NOT SPONSOR
No Honeywell Formula 1 sponsorship is on record, and the power unit is Honda's and homologated, so product cannot go on the car. Counter: Anchor on Boeing and Atlas Air as precedents and keep the workstream outside the regulated unit.

The case

On 12 May 2026 Celonis launched the Celonis Context Model, a real-time digital twin of a company's operations built from process data, and signed a definitive agreement to acquire Ikigai Labs, whose forecasting and simulation software rests on patents licensed from MIT; MIT becomes a Celonis shareholder and Ikigai co-founder Devavrat Shah joins as Chief Scientist, Enterprise AI. Celonis last priced at about $13B in an August 2022 extension led by Qatar Investment Authority, after a $1B Series D at $11B in June 2021; it has raised roughly $2.4B in total. Revenue is not disclosed.

Formula E's technology lanes are held by integrators, not software: TCS titles the Jaguar, Tech Mahindra sits on the Mahindra, Sand Technologies on the Envision and TWG AI on the Andretti. No process-intelligence or operations-software brand is on the grid. Porsche AG already runs Celonis across supply chain and production, and Porsche is doubling its Formula E presence to two works teams for the first GEN4 season.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 12 May 2026 Celonis launched the Celonis Context Model, a real-time digital twin of a company's operations built from process data, and signed a definitive agreement to acquire Ikigai Labs, an AI decision-intelligence company whose planning, simulation and forecasting software rests on patents licensed from MIT. MIT becomes a Celonis shareholder and Ikigai co-founder Devavrat Shah, an MIT professor, joins as Chief Scientist, Enterprise AI.
A repositioning that needs a stage
The launch recasts Celonis from process-mining vendor to the context layer beneath enterprise AI agents, a message aimed at chief executives and boards rather than process engineers. Product repositioning of that kind is exactly what a motorsport platform amplifies: a live operations twin at a race team is the demonstration the pitch needs.
Capital position, honestly

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 201 · 07 JUN 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 201 · HOT · F1

Quantinuum

Quantum Computing · Trapped-Ion Systems · Broomfield, Colorado (European HQ Cambridge, UK) · Nasdaq: QNT (IPO 4 Jun 2026; ~$15B reported)

Quantinuum, the Honeywell-controlled trapped-ion quantum computer maker formed from Honeywell Quantum Solutions and Cambridge Quantum, priced an upsized IPO at $60 a share and began trading on Nasdaq as QNT on 4 June 2026, raising $1.68B in one of the largest quantum-computing listings to date.

The case

Quantinuum sold 28 million Class A shares at $60, above the $53-55 range, raising $1.68B; J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley led the books and the shares opened on Nasdaq on 4 June, closing flat on debut. Reports put the valuation at roughly $15B, up from the $10B pre-money at which Honeywell led a $600M raise in September 2025. The S-1 shows the scale of the bet: 2025 revenue of $30.9M, bookings of $79.3M and a net loss of $192.6M, with Honeywell keeping about 48% of the voting power.

Quantum has no seat on the grid, but its rivals do: IBM sits on the Ferrari, Google Cloud on the McLaren, Microsoft on the Mercedes and the Alpine, Oracle on the Red Bull. Each parent runs a quantum programme that would block a Quantinuum deal. That leaves a shortlist, and one roster that already reads as a compute stack, from Arm processors to CoreWeave's AI cloud, with the quantum layer missing.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Quantinuum priced an upsized IPO of 28 million Class A shares at $60, above the $53-55 range, and began trading on Nasdaq as QNT on 4 June 2026, raising $1.68B with J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley leading the books. The stock closed flat on its first day. It is the first traditional listing of a full-stack quantum company.
Valuation and backing
Reports put the valuation at roughly $15B, up from the $10B pre-money valuation of the $600M raise Honeywell led in September 2025. Honeywell keeps about 48% of the voting power and its chairman and CEO, Vimal Kapur, chairs the Quantinuum board: a first sports partnership would be read as a Honeywell-sanctioned brand move.
The first two quarters as a public company
The S-1 discloses 2025 revenue of $30.9M, bookings of $79.3M and a net loss of $192.6M. A company priced on its roadmap rather than its revenue has to keep investors, customers and recruits engaged through every quarter, and the period straight after listing is when the brand budget is set.
Calendar window
The British GP on 5 July, Aston Martin's home race, sits four weeks from the row date; the United States GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP follow in the autumn near the company's Colorado base and its US investors. Teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed over the summer launches in full for 2027.

Why Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The compute-stack roster
Aston Martin Aramco carries Arm on processors and edge compute, CoreWeave as Official AI Cloud Computing Partner, NetApp on data infrastructure, Cognizant and ServiceNow on the enterprise layer and Cognition for AI software engineering. Quantum is the missing layer, and no quantum company sits on any other car either: Official Quantum Computing Partner is a clean category.
Every rival is locked elsewhere
IBM is on the Ferrari, Google Cloud on the McLaren, Microsoft on the Mercedes and the Alpine, Oracle on the Red Bull. Each parent runs a quantum programme, so those four cars are closed to Quantinuum. Aston Martin has no such conflict.
UK and US at once
Quantinuum's European headquarters is in Cambridge with offices in London and Oxford, close to the Silverstone campus; its corporate headquarters is in Broomfield, Colorado. A British-based team with a Nasdaq-listed American partner tells the same story from both sides of the Atlantic.
A team that will use the product
Aston Martin has moved its engineering compute to the cloud with CoreWeave and built a data pipeline with NetApp; a research programme on Helios sits naturally on top of that stack, run by engineers who already treat compute as a competitive lever.
