Exploratory workstream (Mode A)
Two research programmes on Helios: combinatorial optimisation for race-strategy scenarios and freight scheduling, benchmarked against the classical solvers the team uses today, and InQuanto chemistry simulation of battery and fuel materials relevant to the hybrid power unit. Results are research-grade and published jointly; no operational claim is made.
Commercial lift for the team
A newly listed deep-tech company brings a guest list of institutional investors, government and enterprise buyers, and a scientific audience to the British GP and the US rounds that Aston Martin's technology partners want to meet.
Content and ecosystem
The quantum layer completing a visible compute stack is a story the team can tell on camera: joint papers, engineering content with the CoreWeave and Arm programmes, and a reference customer for Quantinuum's enterprise sales.
What the team gives back
Official Quantum Computing Partner designation, engine-cover or sidepod placement, British GP and US-round hospitality, driver and engineering access, and a research programme the team's engineers own.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Quantum Computing Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the company's first three years as a listed business and the Sol system due in 2027. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in compute access on Helios. Scope: engine-cover or sidepod placement, a joint research programme, British GP and US-round hospitality, engineering content.

The askA 25-minute call with Raj Hazra before the British GP to agree a research scope on Helios, a Silverstone or Austin announcement window, and the size of an Official Quantum Computing Partner entry against Aston Martin's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Rajeeb Hazra
President & CEO, Quantinuum · verified
Hazra leads Quantinuum after 25 years at Intel and a compute-and-networking role at Micron, and fronted the IPO. Path: Nitesh Sharan, CFO since April 2026 (ex-SoundHound AI), and chairman Vimal Kapur, Honeywell's chairman and CEO. No chief marketing officer is confirmed.

Opening angle

Lead with the compute-stack gap.
“Raj, Aston Martin's roster runs from Arm to CoreWeave and stops short of quantum; no team on the grid has that layer. You have just listed and the British GP is four weeks out. 25 minutes to see how the seat would work?”
Bottom line
A $1.68B IPO at roughly $15B, Honeywell's backing and a grid where every quantum rival is locked to another team give Quantinuum a clean lane at Aston Martin, whose roster already reads as a compute stack. Revenue of $30.9M against a $192.6M loss is what holds the score back.

Intelligence Brief / N° 202 · HOT · F1

Supabase

Developer Platform · Open-Source Postgres Backend · San Francisco (remote-first; founded 2020) · Private ($10.5B post-money; $500M Series F, Jun 2026)

Supabase, the open-source Postgres backend that more than 9 million developers build on, closed a $500M Series F led by GIC at a $10.5B post-money valuation on 4 June 2026, doubling the $5B it set eight months earlier and taking total funding past $1B.

The case

Supabase announced on 4 June a $500M Series F led by GIC, with Accel, Y Combinator, Craft, Felicis, Peak XV and Coatue returning, a second investment from Stripe and a first from Salesforce Ventures. The post-money valuation is $10.5B, up from $5B at the October 2025 Series E and $2B at the April 2025 Series D; total capital raised now exceeds $1B. The company reports more than 250,000 customers and over 9 million developers, and says database launches grew 600% in the past year, with over 60% created by AI coding tools.

The grid has already priced developer infrastructure: Atlassian holds the Williams title, Oracle sits on the Red Bull, Google Cloud and Dell on the McLaren. What none of them owns is the open-source Postgres layer beneath the AI-coding boom. Supabase says Claude Code has been the largest single creator of new databases on its platform this year, and Claude already races on the Williams. That is a warm path, not a cold call.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 4 June 2026 Supabase announced a $500M Series F led by GIC at a $10.5B post-money valuation, with Accel, Y Combinator, Craft, Felicis, Peak XV and Coatue returning, Stripe investing for a second time and Salesforce Ventures joining. Total capital raised now exceeds $1B. The company announced it on its own blog; CNBC and TechCrunch confirmed the figures.
Valuation doubled in eight months
The Series E in October 2025 priced the company at $5B; the Series D in April 2025 at $2B. A company re-priced from $2B to $10.5B inside fourteen months has a story to tell enterprise buyers and, eventually, public markets, and now has the budget to tell it.
The AI-coding tailwind
Supabase says database launches on its platform grew 600% in the past year and that over 60% of new databases are created by AI tools, with Claude Code the largest contributor since the start of 2026. That is the same Claude that races on the Williams: the partnership story writes itself.
Calendar window
The British GP on 5 July is Williams' home race and sits five weeks from the announcement; the United States GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP follow in the autumn, close to Supabase's US customer base. Teams settle their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed over the summer can launch in full for 2027.

Why Atlassian Williams Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, VAST for data infrastructure, Keeper for identity security, Airia and Brillio on the technology side and Claude as Official Thinking Partner. No database, backend or developer-platform brand is on the car: Official Developer Platform Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The warm path
Supabase's own funding announcement names Claude Code as the biggest creator of new Supabase databases this year. Claude has been on the Williams since the February livery reveal, working with the team's engineers and strategists. The introduction can run through a relationship Williams already has, and the activation can pair the coding agent with the database it builds on.
A roster that speaks to developers
Atlassian sells to the same software teams Supabase does. A Williams sponsorship puts Supabase next to Jira, Bitbucket and Claude on the one car in Formula 1 that already reads as a developer stack, rather than as a lone logo on a consumer-brand livery.
Story and market fit
A remote-first company with founders from outside Silicon Valley and a global developer community fits a British team with a global fan base and US ambitions. The British GP gives a home stage; Austin and Las Vegas give the US one.

Value To Atlassian Williams Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Supabase provides the Postgres database, authentication, storage and realtime layer for the applications Williams ships around the car: fan and ticketing apps, partner and hospitality portals, and the internal dashboards and tools engineers and strategists build with Claude. Multigres, released in preview with the round, gives those systems horizontal scale on race weekends when traffic spikes.
Commercial lift for the team
A platform used by more than 9 million developers brings a developer audience Williams' existing partners want to reach, plus a guest list of founders, investors and enterprise engineering leaders for the British GP and the US rounds.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced engineering content with the Claude programme: how a race team builds and ships software in a week, the coding agent and the database on one car, and a factory reference customer for Supabase's enterprise sales.
What the team gives back
Official Developer Platform Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, British GP and US-round hospitality, driver and engineering access for Supabase's channels, and a developer-community activation at Silverstone.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Developer Platform Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the next raise or a listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in platform credits. Scope: livery placement, developer activations at the British GP and the US rounds, content with the Claude programme, first refusal on a database category in 2030.

The askA 25-minute call with Paul Copplestone before the British GP to walk through the Claude Code connection, agree a Silverstone or Austin announcement window, and size an Official Developer Platform Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Paul Copplestone
Co-Founder & CEO, Supabase · verified
Copplestone co-founded Supabase in 2020 with CTO Ant Wilson and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Rory Wilding, COO and Chief Commercial Officer, and Scott Buxton, CFO. No chief marketing officer is listed; marketing is developer-led.

Opening angle

Lead with the Claude Code number.
“Paul, Claude Code is the biggest creator of Supabase databases this year, and Claude already races on the Williams. The developer-platform lane there is open and the British GP is five weeks out. 25 minutes to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $500M raise at $10.5B, more than 9 million developers, and Claude Code as the top creator of Supabase databases put Supabase at peak brand-investment capacity with a warm route onto the one car Claude already races on. The developer-platform lane at Williams is open and the British GP sits inside the window.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 205 · 03 JUN 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 205 · HOT · F1

AlphaSense

AI Market Intelligence · Financial & Corporate Research Platform · New York · Private ($7.5B; $350M round, Jun 2026)

AlphaSense, the New York AI market-intelligence platform used by 90% of the S&P 100, closed a $350M round on 3 June 2026 at a $7.5B valuation, led by Vitruvian, Accenture Ventures and J.P. Morgan Asset Management, on annual recurring revenue above $600M and reported IPO intent.

The case

AlphaSense announced the $350M round on 3 June 2026: led by Vitruvian Partners, Accenture Ventures and J.P. Morgan Asset Management, with Goldman Sachs Alternatives, CapitalG and Viking returning, taking total funding past $1B. The $7.5B valuation nearly doubles the $4B set by the $650M round of 2024. Annual recurring revenue passed $600M in the first quarter, up from $500M in October 2025. More than 7,000 enterprises use the platform, including 90% of the S&P 100 and every top global investment bank. Jack Kokko told the press an IPO is a possibility.

The product is the research desk for the people who run the world's capital: analysts, bankers, corporate strategists and the boards they brief. Those are the guests every F1 team's commercial partners want in the suite, and no team carries a market-intelligence or research platform. The round arrives with Accenture as both investor and channel partner, giving AlphaSense a reason to be seen by chief executives, not just analysts, over the next twelve months.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
AlphaSense announced on 3 June 2026 that it had closed a $350M round at a $7.5B valuation, led by Vitruvian Partners, Accenture Ventures and J.P. Morgan Asset Management, with D. E. Shaw Ventures and Pinegrove Opportunity Partners joining and Goldman Sachs Alternatives, CapitalG and Viking Global Investors returning. Total funding now exceeds $1B. Sophie Bower-Straziota of Vitruvian joins the board.
Revenue, not just valuation
Annual recurring revenue passed $600M in the first quarter of 2026, up from $500M in October 2025, and the valuation nearly doubled from the $4B set by the $650M round of 2024. This is a company with the revenue to fund a multi-year programme from operating budget, not from the raise.
A listing story being told
Jack Kokko told the press an IPO is a possibility. That is reported, not committed, but a company preparing to be known by public-market investors and chief executives, rather than only by the analysts who already use it, is exactly when a brand platform earns its budget. The Accenture partnership adds an enterprise channel that wants the brand seen in boardrooms.
Calendar window
The British GP at Silverstone on 5 July sits inside the six-to-ten-week window; Belgium and Hungary follow before the summer break, when McLaren settles its 2027 roster. A deal agreed in July can launch at Austin or Las Vegas, where AlphaSense's US banking and corporate customers are, and run in full from 2027.

Why Mclaren Mastercard F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
No team on the grid carries a market-intelligence or financial-research platform. McLaren's roster has Goldman Sachs, CNBC, Deloitte, Workday, Alteryx and Dell, all adjacent, none competing: Official Market Intelligence Partner is a clean category next to the most B2B-fluent partner programme in the paddock.
The warm path
Goldman Sachs Alternatives is an existing AlphaSense investor and Goldman Sachs is a McLaren partner. The introduction runs through a partner McLaren already trusts, and every top global investment bank is an AlphaSense customer, so the guests AlphaSense would host are the ones McLaren's finance partners already recognise.
Beside Gemini, not against it
Gemini is McLaren's Primary Partner for AI and is used across racing operations. AlphaSense is not an AI assistant; it is the research layer for markets, filings and expert calls. The category has to be written as market and financial research, with exclusivity, so the two sit side by side rather than overlap.
Why not the others
Aston Martin carries the Financial Times, Public, Coinbase and Pepperstone, a crowded financial-information roster; Mercedes has Nasdaq and UBS at the highest price on the grid; Williams' BNY, Barclays, Nuveen and Stephens would make AlphaSense one more finance logo rather than the intelligence layer. McLaren gives it the stage its customers already attend.

Value To Mclaren Mastercard F1 Team — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Commercial workstream (Mode B)
McLaren's commercial and strategy teams sell to public companies and renew with them. AlphaSense puts partners' and prospects' earnings calls, broker research, regulatory filings and expert-call transcripts in one search, so partner prospecting, renewal risk and the financial health of rival teams' sponsors are tracked with the tools an investment bank uses.
Hospitality that matches the customer list
AlphaSense's buyers are analysts, bankers and corporate strategists at more than 7,000 enterprises, including 90% of the S&P 100. Silverstone, Monza, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality puts those decision-makers in McLaren's suite, the audience the team's B2B partners already pay to reach.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced content on how a race team reads its market, natural alongside CNBC on the roster; co-hosted investor events at the US rounds; a McLaren reference story for AlphaSense's enterprise sales and for the Accenture channel.
What the team gives back
Official Market Intelligence Partner designation with category exclusivity, car placement at US and European rounds, platform seats for McLaren's commercial and strategy staff, driver and leadership access for customer programmes.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Market Intelligence Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning a probable listing window. Estimated $4-6M a year, hospitality-weighted. Scope: category exclusivity for market and financial research, car placement at US and European rounds, platform seats for McLaren's commercial staff, co-hosted investor events at Austin and Las Vegas.

The askA 25-minute call with Heather Zynczak before the British GP to confirm the listing intent on the record, agree a category definition that sits beside Gemini, and size an Official Market Intelligence Partner entry against McLaren's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Heather Zynczak
Chief Marketing Officer, AlphaSense · verified
Zynczak has been CMO since April 2024 and has scaled two software brands: Domo from launch to $100M revenue and Pluralsight through its IPO, after Oracle and SAP. Path: Jack Kokko, Founder and CEO, signs; Kiva Kolstein, President and Chief Revenue Officer; Samantha Greenberg, CFO since April 2026.

Opening angle

Lead with the customer list and the open lane.
“Heather, every top investment bank runs on AlphaSense and entertains at McLaren, where Goldman already sits and nobody owns market intelligence. A listing story needs a stage. 25 minutes before Silverstone to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $350M round at $7.5B on 3 June, ARR above $600M, a customer list that already fills McLaren's suites and an open market-intelligence lane put AlphaSense at peak brand-investment authority with a warm route through Goldman Sachs. A MODE B workstream and an unconfirmed IPO hold the score at 73.

Glean

Enterprise AI · Work AI Platform · Palo Alto, California · Private ($7.2B, Series F Jun 2025)

Glean, the Palo Alto 'Work AI' platform, crossed $300M in annual recurring revenue on 28 May 2026, tripling in fifteen months, on the $7.2B valuation set by its $150M Series F. It has never entered motorsport, and Formula E's Work AI lane is open as the Gen4 era approaches.

The case

CEO Arvind Jain announced on 28 May that ARR has passed $300M, five months after $200M and roughly three times the level of fifteen months earlier. The company raised $150M at $7.2B in June 2025 in a Series F led by Wellington Management, taking total funding to about $768M, and bought document-intelligence start-up Aryn on 11 March 2026. There has been no new round in 2026: this is a demand inflection, not a capital one, and the score says so. The buyers Glean must now win are enterprise CIOs, Formula E's paddock audience.

The enterprise-AI archetype is already on the grid. TWG AI is Official Artificial Intelligence partner of Andretti's programme; Sand Technologies backs Envision; Google Cloud is the championship's cloud partner. None of them sells a Work AI platform to end users, so a Glean-class brand would arrive first in its category. Mahindra Racing, committed as a manufacturer to the Gen4 era through 2030, pairs an Indian engineering parent with Glean's biggest office beyond America.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 28 May 2026 CEO Arvind Jain announced that Glean had passed $300M in annual recurring revenue, five months after $200M and roughly three times the level of fifteen months earlier; TechCrunch reported it the same day. The figure is company-stated, not audited, and the brief says so.
Why this is the moment
The last capital event is a year old: the $150M Series F at $7.2B closed in June 2025. What has changed since is demand. A company that has tripled revenue in fifteen months moves from proving the product to building the brand that keeps winning enterprise accounts against Microsoft, Google and the model labs, and that is when a global platform earns its place in the budget.
The Gen4 clock
Formula E's Gen4 era begins with Season 13 in December 2026 and Mahindra Racing has committed as a manufacturer through 2030. Teams settle their Season 13 partner rosters over the summer, so a decision taken before the London E-Prix finale on 15-16 August can be announced with the new car.
What holds the score back
No raise, no listing and no hard deadline: urgency is scored 11 of 20 and timing 14. The case is strong on capacity and fit, not on a forcing event, and the brief does not pretend otherwise.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

Why Mahindra Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Mahindra Racing carries Mahindra & Mahindra as parent and title and Tech Mahindra as its engineering and IT-services partner, and nothing else in enterprise software. Official Work AI Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price, with exclusivity scoped to the Work AI platform so it sits beside Tech Mahindra rather than against it.
A parent that is the customer
Glean sells to large, multi-business enterprises whose knowledge is scattered across systems. The Mahindra Group is exactly that, and Glean's largest base outside the US is its Bengaluru centre of more than 450 people. A team deployment that extends into group functions is a reference account, not just a logo.
A manufacturer committed to 2030
Mahindra Racing's Gen4 commitment as a manufacturer, announced 26 November 2025, runs to at least 2030. A three-season term from Season 13 sits entirely inside it, which removes the exit risk that undermines multi-year deals with customer teams.
Why not the others
TWG AI is Andretti's Official Artificial Intelligence partner, Sand Technologies backs Envision on AI and TCS, an IT-services group with its own AI practice, holds Jaguar's title. The remaining teams are open but carry neither the enterprise-software adjacency nor the India and US story that makes Mahindra the natural first deployment.

Value To Mahindra Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
A racing team runs on documents: technical regulations and homologation files, supplier and freight records, simulation and test reports, sponsor and hospitality contracts. Glean connects those sources, respects who is allowed to see what, and gives engineers, operations and commercial staff one assistant and a set of agents that answer from the team's own knowledge. The team gets hours back every week; the parent group can extend the same deployment to chosen functions.
Commercial lift for the team
Glean's buyers are CIOs and heads of IT at large enterprises, the audience Formula E's paddock is built to host. A partner that brings that guest list to London, Berlin and the new Austin and Miami rounds strengthens every other B2B conversation the team is having.
Content and ecosystem
A working deployment is a story: how a Formula E team finds what it knows before a race weekend, told through the engineers who use it. That content serves Glean's enterprise sales and Mahindra's technology positioning at the same time, and gives the Mahindra Group a visible AI programme with a global stage.
What the team gives back
Official Work AI Partner designation, car and garage branding, category exclusivity for the Work AI platform, hospitality at the London finale and at the Season 13 rounds, driver and engineering access, and a reference account inside one of India's largest industrial groups.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Work AI Partner. THREE YEARS, Season 13 to Season 15 (2026-27 to 2028-29), inside the Gen4 commitment. Estimated $2-3M a year, part-payable in seats. Scope: Work AI platform exclusivity, car and garage branding, a working team deployment, London and Bengaluru hospitality, engineering content.

The askA 25-minute call with Matt Kixmoeller before the London E-Prix to size an Official Work AI Partner entry against Mahindra Racing's Season 13 roster, agree a team deployment scoped with Tech Mahindra, and set an announcement window with the Gen4 car.

Primary decision-maker

Matt "Kix" Kixmoeller
Chief Marketing Officer, Glean · verified
Kixmoeller runs Glean's marketing after leading marketing at Ghost Autonomy and marketing, product and strategy at Pure Storage, a Mercedes F1 technical partner since 2016. Path: Arvind Jain, co-founder and CEO; Amar Maletira, COO, ex-CEO of Rackspace. No CFO confirmed.

Opening angle

Lead with the category and the clock.
“Kix, you watched Pure Storage put its name on a Mercedes. Glean just crossed $300M ARR and Formula E's Work AI lane is open, with Mahindra committed to 2030. 25 minutes before the London E-Prix?”
Bottom line
$300M ARR crossed on 28 May, a $7.2B valuation and about $768M raised put Glean at the moment enterprise brands start spending on credibility. Formula E's Work AI lane is open, Mahindra is committed through 2030, and Season 13 rosters close over the summer.

The case

Corgi announced on 28 May a $106M Series B1 led by TCV at a $2.6B valuation, three weeks after the same investor led its $160M Series B at $1.3B on 6 May. Insurance is on the grid, but thinly. Orion180, a Florida homeowners insurer, has been on the Haas car since October 2024; Aon is at Ferrari as a broker. Cadillac, the grid's new American entrant, carries none of it, and the executive who runs the team also runs an insurance group.

Trigger
On 28 May 2026 Corgi announced a $106M Series B1 led by TCV at a $2.6B valuation, three weeks after the same investor led a $160M Series B at $1.3B on 6 May. Total funding is $378M. Corgi came out of stealth in January 2026 with $108M and has since doubled its valuation twice. Companies that re-price this fast spend the following quarter telling the story to customers, recruits and the next round of investors, and Corgi already invests in brand: a mascot, a named office cafe, a consumer-grade identity in a category that has none.
Sports named as a vertical
The 28 May release names trucking, small business and sports as the next verticals. A Formula 1 partnership is the fastest way to make the sports line credible to leagues, clubs and venues, and to put Corgi in front of the sports-industry buyers who sit in the paddock.

The British GP at Silverstone on 3-5 July falls inside the six-to-ten-week window; the United States GP in Austin on 23-25 October and the Las Vegas GP on 19-21 November are the US stages left in 2026. Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed over the summer can be announced in Austin and run in full from 2027.

Official Insurance Partner designation, commercial-insurance exclusivity, sidepod or halo placement, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, driver and engineering access for Corgi's channels, and a case study Corgi can take to every league and club it pitches.

Entry as Official Insurance Partner of the Cadillac F1 Team. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, with an option to start at Austin in 2026. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in underwritten cover. Scope: commercial-insurance exclusivity, sidepod or halo placement, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for founder customers, a content series on insuring a start-up team.

Nico Laqua
Co-Founder & CEO, Corgi · verified

Bottom line
Two rounds in three weeks, a $2.6B valuation and a named push into sports put Corgi at the moment a brand gets built in public. Cadillac's inaugural roster carries no insurer, its chief executive runs one, and the British GP and Austin sit inside the window.

Exa

AI Search Infrastructure · Search API for AI Agents · San Francisco (founded 2021, Y Combinator) · Private ($2.2B; $250M Series C, May 2026)

Exa, the search engine built for AI agents, announced a $250M Series C led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $2.2B valuation on 20 May 2026, more than tripling the $700M Benchmark set in September. It powers search for Cursor, Cognition and HubSpot and ships as a native Claude connector.

The case

On 20 May Exa announced a $250M Series C led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $2.2B valuation, confirmed by Bloomberg the same day. It follows an $85M Series B led by Benchmark at $700M in September 2025 and a $22M Series A led by Lightspeed in July 2024. Exa says more than 5,000 companies and 400,000 developers use its search API, Cursor, Cognition and HubSpot among them. The money funds next-generation models, infrastructure for hundreds of thousands of searches a second, and a go-to-market build-out under Marcus Holm, joining as CRO from LaunchDarkly.

AI brands have moved onto the grid quickly: Claude races on the Williams, Cognition joined Aston Martin Aramco, Meta AI sits at Mercedes and TWG AI at Cadillac. Exa is the search layer beneath those agents, and the companies it positions against are already on cars, Google Cloud at McLaren and Microsoft at Mercedes and Alpine. A challenger with a $250M war chest and a new revenue chief has a story to tell against them.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 20 May 2026 Exa announced a $250M Series C led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $2.2B valuation, on its own blog and confirmed by Bloomberg the same day. The valuation has more than tripled since the $85M Series B at $700M led by Benchmark in September 2025.
A go-to-market build-out
The round came with a commercial hire: Marcus Holm, President of LaunchDarkly, joins as Chief Revenue Officer to build the global go-to-market organisation across sales, solutions and marketing. A company assembling its first real marketing function after a raise is the moment a first sports partnership gets decided.
The category is moving onto the grid
In the last year Claude joined Williams, Cognition joined Aston Martin Aramco, Meta AI joined Mercedes and TWG AI launched with Cadillac. AI brands are using F1 to reach engineers, buyers and capital markets at once; Exa sells into exactly those AI companies and has not yet chosen a stage.
Calendar window
Monaco GP (5-7 June), the Spanish GP in Barcelona (12-14 June), the Austrian GP (26-28 June) and the British GP (3-5 July) all fall inside the 6-10 week window. A deal agreed before Silverstone can be announced at the British GP and activated in full for 2027, when teams close their partner rosters in the autumn.

Why Atlassian Williams Racing — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, VAST for the data platform, Keeper for identity security, Airia and Brillio on the technology tier, and Claude as Official Thinking Partner. No search, retrieval or knowledge partner sits on the car: Official AI Search Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
The warm path
Exa is a native Claude connector and publishes an open-source MCP server; Claude has worked alongside Williams' engineers, strategists and operations teams since the February 2026 livery reveal. The introduction runs through a partner Williams already trusts, and the product plugs into a workflow the team already uses.
A team that will use the product
Williams' revival is data-led. Live web retrieval for the team's agents is consumed in the factory and on the pit wall, which separates a technology partner from a logo. The workstream is lighter than compute or data, and the brief scores it honestly at 14 out of 20.
Audience fit
Exa sells to developers and AI companies; Williams' partner roster is the most software-native on the grid, and its hospitality already gathers CIOs, CTOs and founders. The British GP, the team's home race, is the natural stage for a developer-facing brand with a San Francisco base.

Value To Atlassian Williams Racing — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Exa's search API and Websets give Williams' Claude-based agents live retrieval from the open web: FIA regulation and technical-directive monitoring, supplier and parts discovery, tracking of rivals' publicly reported upgrades, media monitoring, and sponsor-prospect research for the commercial team. Delivered as API capacity, it costs the team nothing inside the cost cap.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner that sells to AI-native companies brings founders, engineering leaders and venture investors to the British GP and Las Vegas suites, the audience Williams' technology partners want alongside them.
Content and ecosystem
Co-produced engineering content with the Claude programme (how the team's agents search, verify and decide), a Williams reference case for Exa's enterprise sales, and developer activations across Exa's 400,000-developer community and Williams' digital channels.
What the team gives back
Official AI Search Partner designation, sidepod or halo placement, naming of the team's research-agent stack, British GP hospitality, and driver and engineering access for Exa's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official AI Search Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the go-to-market build-out and any listing window. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in API credits for the team's agents. Scope: sidepod or halo placement, naming of the team's research-agent stack, British GP hospitality, developer content with the Claude programme.

The askA 25-minute call with Will Bryk before the Monaco GP to confirm the go-to-market budget with Marcus Holm, agree a 90-day pilot inside the Claude workflow at Williams, and size an Official AI Search Partner entry against the team's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Will Bryk
Co-Founder & CEO, Exa · verified
Bryk co-founded Exa in 2021 with Jeff Wang, a Harvard classmate, and CTO Dan McArdle, and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Marcus Holm, incoming CRO, owns go-to-market; Jeff Wang oversees finance. No CMO, CFO or COO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the Claude connection.
“Will, Exa is already a Claude connector and Claude already races on the Williams. Cognition took its seat at Aston Martin in its breakout year; the search lane at Williams is open. 25 minutes before Monaco to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $250M round at $2.2B, a new revenue chief with a go-to-market mandate, and a native connection to the Claude programme already on the Williams give Exa the budget, the motive and a warm path. The search lane at Williams is open, and Monaco and the British GP sit inside the window.

Value To Cadillac F1 Team — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Audience and commerce (Mode B)
300,000 business customers as a marketing channel and a guest list: founder hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, a Cadillac offer inside the Mercury product for the team's US fan base of business owners, and a Mercury Bank launch activation at the US rounds.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner whose customers are one in three US startups brings founders, venture investors and bankers to the team's hospitality, the audience a first-year American team needs to sell its remaining 2027 inventory.
Paddock supplier banking
Banking, corporate cards and treasury for the team's US entity and its American supplier base: a real, if modest, operational use that makes the partnership more than a logo.
What the team gives back
Official Banking Partner designation, sidepod or rear-wing placement, driver access for Mercury's founder community, and co-branded content with the team's engineering and commercial leadership.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Banking Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, spanning the bank launch and a probable listing window. Estimated $4-6M a year. Scope: sidepod or rear-wing placement, founder hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, a Mercury Bank launch activation at the US rounds, co-branded content with the team's leadership.

The askA 25-minute call with Immad Akhund before the Monaco GP to confirm the bank-launch timetable, test the TWG Global category question with the team, and size an Official Banking Partner entry against Cadillac's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Immad Akhund
Co-Founder & CEO, Mercury · verified
Akhund founded Mercury in 2017 with Max Tagher (CTO) and Jason Zhang (COO) and fronts every raise and the charter; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Rachel Moncton Oatway, VP Marketing (ex-ClassPass), who reports to him, and Dan Kang, CFO since May 2025. No CMO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the bank launch.
“Immad, Mercury is about to become a bank in its own name, and Cadillac is the first American team in a decade with no bank on the car. Revolut and Airwallex have already taken theirs. 25 minutes before Monaco to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $200M round at $5.2B, $650M-plus of profitable revenue, and a bank charter that turns Mercury into a bank in its own name give it the budget, the motive and a launch to time a partnership to. Cadillac is the American team with no bank on the car, and Monaco and the British GP sit inside the window.

briefs.page_html:
Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 218 · 19 MAY 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 218 · HOT · F1

Armada

Edge AI Infrastructure · Modular, Satellite-Connected Data Centres · San Francisco (founded late 2022) · Private ($2B pre-money; $230M Series B, May 2026)

Armada, the San Francisco builder of ruggedised, satellite-connected data centres that run on oil fields, mines and Navy sites, closed an oversubscribed $230M Series B at a $2B pre-money valuation on 19 May 2026 and will build them at a new Arizona factory with Johnson Controls from this summer.

75
Opportunity / 100
Timing window
HOT
Series
F1
Recommended team
TGR Haas F1 Team
Action horizon
6-10 WKS

The case

On 19 May 2026 Armada announced a $230M oversubscribed Series B at a $2B pre-money valuation, co-led by Overmatch, BlackRock and 8090 Industries, taking total funding to nearly $500M. Johnson Controls invested alongside an agreement to build Galleon Forge One, an up-to-400,000 sq ft Arizona factory with more than 500 jobs, in continuous production from summer 2026. The company says customer bookings grew 540% from FY25 to FY26. Its Galleon and Leviathan units are self-contained, Starlink-connected data centres for places with no grid or fibre: oil fields, mines, ships and bases.

The grid has already bought the data-centre archetype: Core Scientific joined Cadillac as official data-centre partner in March 2026, CoreWeave sits at Aston Martin, Hewlett Packard Enterprise at Mercedes. None of them sells compute that travels. A Formula 1 garage is a temporary remote site rebuilt 24 times a year, which is the problem Armada was founded to solve, and Microsoft's M12 and Johnson Controls are investor names a team can put on a car.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 19 May 2026 Armada announced a $230M oversubscribed Series B at a $2B pre-money valuation, co-led by Overmatch, BlackRock and 8090 Industries, taking total funding to nearly $500M. The figures come from the company's own release and were carried by CNBC the same day.
A factory, not just a round
Johnson Controls invested alongside an agreement to build Galleon Forge One, an up-to-400,000 sq ft Arizona factory with more than 500 jobs, in continuous production from summer 2026, initially building the megawatt-scale Leviathan. A company that has just committed to American manufacturing has a story it needs to tell to customers, policymakers and future public-market investors, and a race in Austin is where that audience gathers.
Demand is the proof point
The company reports 540% customer bookings growth from FY25 to FY26 and a 2,000% year-on-year rise in Q1 FY27 bookings; these are company figures, unaudited, and the brief treats them as such. Customers named in its own releases span oil and gas, mining, telecom, hospitality and government, including the U.S. Navy, Alaska's Department of Transportation, Targa Resources and Atlas Energy.
Calendar window
The Miami GP has just run; the United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American rounds left in 2026, and teams settle their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed over the summer can be announced at Austin and activated in full for 2027.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

$230M
$230M oversubscribed Series B at a $2B pre-money valuation, announced 19 May 2026 in a company release and…
540%
The company says customer bookings grew 540% from FY25 to FY26.

Why Tgr Haas F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
The Haas roster is connectivity and services: Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner, Haas Automation, MoneyGram, CommScope as Official Connectivity Partner (Feb 2025), Ruckus Networks as Official Networking Partner (Jan 2026), Mphasis as Official Digital Partner, UChicago Medicine and Infobip. No compute, cloud or data-centre partner is listed, so Official Edge Computing Partner is a clean category at the most accessible price on the grid.
Complementary, not a clash
CommScope and Ruckus run the wired and wireless network in the garage, pit wall and hospitality. Armada's Galleon is the compute and the satellite backhaul that sit behind that network. The clash-check is a category definition, not a rival product, and it should be cleared with Haas before the first call.
Two American industrial brands
Haas is the American-owned privateer of the grid, founded by a machine-tool manufacturer. Armada is building an Arizona factory with Johnson Controls to make AI infrastructure in the United States. The shared story, American industry that builds hard things, is one the team can tell in Austin and Las Vegas without stretching.
A team that will use the product

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 220 · 15 MAY 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 220 · HOT · F1

Anduril Industries

Defence Technology · Autonomous Systems / Lattice Software · Costa Mesa, California (founded 2017) · Private ($61B; $5B Series H, May 2026)

Anduril, the Costa Mesa defence-technology company that already sponsors NASCAR and Hendrick Motorsports, announced a $5B Series H at a $61B valuation on 13 May 2026, doubling its price in a year, weeks before its first NASCAR title race and the start of production at its $1B Ohio factory.

The case

On 13 May 2026 Anduril announced a $5B Series H led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz at a $61B valuation, double the $30.5B set in June 2025, taking total funding past $11B over eight rounds. The demand behind it is public: the US Army awarded a ten-year enterprise contract with a $20B ceiling on 13 March 2026, and Arsenal-1, a $1B factory in Columbus, Ohio, targets production from July. Anduril has bought motorsport already: Official Defense Partner of NASCAR, title sponsor of June's San Diego weekend at Naval Base Coronado, and Hendrick's William Byron through 2028.

That NASCAR programme is the tell. A company that put a Cup Series event on a naval base to recruit engineers and tell a rebuild-the-arsenal story has a template Formula 1 can scale: three US rounds, a global engineering audience and a listing expected in 2027. General Motors is the bridge. GM Defense signed a teaming agreement with Anduril in October 2023 on autonomy and electrification, and Cadillac is GM's works team.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 13 May 2026 Anduril announced a $5B Series H led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz at a $61B valuation, double the $30.5B set by the $2.5B round of June 2025; total funding is now more than $11B over eight rounds. The company announced the round itself and Bloomberg, TechCrunch and GovConWire carried it the same day. Revenue is not disclosed and the brief uses no revenue figure.
The demand behind the price
The US Army awarded Anduril a ten-year enterprise contract with a $20B ceiling on 13 March 2026, consolidating more than 120 procurement actions into one framework built around the Lattice software. The ceiling is a maximum, not an obligated amount, and the brief says so. Arsenal-1, the $1B hyperscale factory in Columbus, Ohio, targets production from July 2026.
Motorsport is already in the budget
Anduril is Official Defense Partner of NASCAR and presenting sponsor of the NASCAR San Diego weekend; the Anduril 250 'Race the Base' Cup Series street race ran at Naval Base Coronado on 21 June 2026. It is also a primary sponsor of Hendrick Motorsports' William Byron for two Cup races a season from 2026 through 2028. The question for Anduril is not whether to buy motorsport but whether to scale it to a global engineering audience.
Calendar window
The Miami GP has just run; the United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the US rounds left in 2026, and teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A listing is expected by analysts in 2027 or later; a partnership agreed over the summer can be announced at Austin and run through the listing window.

Why Cadillac F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The warm path
GM Defense, a General Motors subsidiary, signed a teaming agreement with Anduril in October 2023 on autonomy, battery electrification and new propulsion, and the two showed Infantry Squad Vehicles fitted with Anduril systems at AUSA that year. Cadillac F1 Team is General Motors' works entry. The introduction can run through a relationship both sides already value.
The open lane
Cadillac's debut roster is deliberately small: TWG AI as primary and exclusive AI partner, Core Scientific for data-centre infrastructure, IFS for enterprise software, Tenneco as technical partner, Jim Beam, Tommy Hilfiger and Claro. No aerospace, defence or autonomy partner is on it, and the team has said it is not seeking a title sponsor in year one, so a top-tier team partner is the largest seat on offer.
American identity, US stages
A Costa Mesa company that used a naval base for its first NASCAR event gets an American works team, an Indiana headquarters, and Miami, Austin and Las Vegas as home rounds. The 'rebuild the arsenal' story and Cadillac's American-engineering debut are the same story told twice.
Price of entry
A first-season team prices its partner tier below the established grid, and its inventory is not yet crowded. For a brand that spends on two Cup races a season with Hendrick, the step up to a three-year F1 seat is proportionate to a $5B raise.

Value To Cadillac F1 Team — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Halo with concrete mechanics (Mode B)
TWG AI holds Cadillac's exclusive AI lane, so the brief does not claim a Lattice-on-the-pit-wall workstream. What Anduril brings is a brand that recruits engineers: co-produced content across Arsenal-1 and the Indiana headquarters, engineering-talent programmes with the team, and a manufacturing story that runs from a hyperscale factory to a race car built in the same country.
Commercial lift for the team
Anduril's guest list is Pentagon, Congressional, allied-government and prime-contractor audiences, plus the venture and public-market investors who priced the $61B round. Hospitality at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas puts that audience in Cadillac's suite alongside its other B2B partners.
Programmes that already exist
The Hendrick agreement carries warfighter and military-family programmes; the same mechanics translate to the US rounds, with GM Defense as a natural co-sponsor. Content from the Coronado event gives the team a template rather than a blank page.
What the team gives back
Official Defence Technology Partner designation, engine-cover or rear-wing placement, US-round hospitality, driver and engineering access for recruitment content, and a joint GM Defense and Cadillac engineering story for Anduril's channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Defence Technology Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, bridging the Hendrick term and a probable listing. Estimated $8-12M a year, the top of Cadillac's partner tier. Scope: engine-cover or rear-wing placement, US-round hospitality, recruitment and manufacturing content, a joint GM Defense and Cadillac engineering story.

The askA 25-minute call with Jeff Miller before the United States GP to test the F1 step-up against the NASCAR programme, confirm the category definition with TWG AI, and size an Official Defence Technology Partner entry against Cadillac's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Jeff Miller
Chief Marketing Officer, Anduril Industries · verified
Anduril's first marketing chief, hired in May 2024 from Cruise, where he was VP of marketing, after Snapchat, PepsiCo and Ogilvy; he built the NASCAR and Hendrick programmes. Path: Matthew Steckman, President and Chief Business Officer; Matt Grimm, Co-Founder and COO; Brian Schimpf, CEO.

Opening angle

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 223 · 11 MAY 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 223 · HOT · F1

Helsing

Defence Technology · AI Software / Autonomous Systems · Munich · Private ($18B reported; $1.2B round in close, May 2026)

Helsing, Munich's defence-AI company, was reported on 11 May 2026 to be closing a $1.2B round led by Dragoneer at an $18B valuation, eleven weeks after the Bundestag approved its first HX-2 strike-drone contract for the Bundeswehr. Germany's most valuable startup, by that print, is entering its build phase.

The case

TechCrunch reported on 11 May that Helsing was in the final close of a $1.2B round led by Dragoneer and co-led by Lightspeed at an $18B valuation, up from the ~€12B set by its €600M Series D under Daniel Ek's Prima Materia in June 2025. Order flow has arrived to match the capital: on 25 February the Bundestag budget committee approved a €269M initial HX-2 contract with a framework of up to €1.46B over seven years, inside a 4,300-drone first tranche. The round later closed at $1.8B on 13 July.

Defence is not new to the paddock: Boeing sits on Alpine's roster and BAE Systems shares fast-jet technology with Williams. What is new is a European defence company with venture capital at this scale and a hiring problem, competing with the primes and the hyperscalers for the same engineers. Formula 1 is Europe's most-watched engineering shop floor, and no defence-technology company has a seat in it.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
TechCrunch reported on 11 May 2026 that Helsing was closing a $1.2B round led by Dragoneer and co-led by Lightspeed at an $18B valuation. At the row date this was press-reported, not company-announced; on 13 July CNBC and Defense News reported the round closed at $1.8B at the same $18B valuation, Europe's largest defence-startup round.
Contract before capital
On 25 February 2026 the Bundestag budget committee approved an initial €269M HX-2 loitering-munition contract with Helsing, with framework options up to €1.46B over seven years, inside a 4,300-drone first tranche. The company had a sovereign customer's order book before it had the new money, which is the sequence a brand budget follows.
Valuation step-up
The €600M Series D of June 2025, led by Daniel Ek's Prima Materia with General Catalyst, Accel, Plural and Saab, priced Helsing at about €12B. The 2026 round moved that to $18B in under a year. A company re-priced that fast has recruiting, political and customer audiences to speak to, and the budget to do it.
Calendar window
From the 11 May row date the European rounds run Monaco, Barcelona, Austria, the British GP, Belgium, Hungary, Zandvoort and Monza, where Helsing's customers and recruits sit. Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a conversation opened in May can be signed before the US GP and Las Vegas.

Why Audi Revolut F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Audi's roster carries Revolut as title partner, Extreme Networks, NinjaOne, ElevenLabs and JigSpace on the technology side, bp/Castrol, adidas and a run of consumer brands. There is no defence, aerospace or security-technology partner, and none anywhere on the grid: the category is clean and ownable at a team-partner price.
The German story
Audi's power units come from Neuburg an der Donau in Bavaria, with chassis in Hinwil and a technology centre in Bicester; 2026 is its first season as a full works entry. Helsing is Munich's flagship deep-tech company. Two German engineering programmes in a build phase at the same time give both boards a home narrative.
A partner that will use the relationship
The talent programme is the workstream: Helsing and Audi's three sites compete for the same software, autonomy and hardware engineers, and a joint graduate intake, secondments and shared recruiting content are things both organisations would run regardless of the car.
Why not the AI lanes elsewhere
Helsing is an AI company, and the AI lanes at Williams (Claude), Aston Martin (Cognition), Cadillac (TWG AI), McLaren (Gemini, Groq) and Mercedes (Meta AI, G42) are taken. Audi has no broad AI partner, only ElevenLabs for voice, so the defence-technology designation does not collide with an incumbent.

Value To Audi Revolut F1 Team — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

Talent (Mode B, concrete)
A joint engineering-talent programme across Neuburg, Hinwil and Bicester: graduate intake, engineer secondments in both directions, and a recruitment content series shot in the factories. Helsing gets Formula 1's pull with European engineers; Audi gets a partner whose hiring brand is as strong as its own.
Access
Paddock hospitality at the European rounds for ministry, armed-forces and NATO-market delegations, the audience Helsing sells to and one that Audi's existing hospitality programme does not otherwise reach.
Narrative
A made-in-Europe engineering story on a German car in its first season, framed around software, autonomy and sovereignty rather than consumer advertising, with content Audi can use in its own Vorsprung durch Technik positioning.
What the team gives back
Official Defence Technology Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, factory and garage access for recruitment content, and hospitality allocations at the European rounds and the US GP.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Defence Technology Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the HX-2 production ramp and a likely listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year. Scope: sidepod or engine-cover placement, a joint engineering-talent programme across Neuburg, Hinwil and Bicester, European-round hospitality for government customers, and a recruitment content series.

The askA 25-minute call with Torsten Reil, with Johannes Boie on the line, to put the round on the record, test the appetite of Audi's board for a defence-technology partner, and size a talent-led Official Defence Technology Partner entry against Audi's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Torsten Reil
Co-Founder & Co-CEO, Helsing · verified
Reil co-founded Helsing in 2021 and shares the CEO role with Gundbert Scherf; he previously founded NaturalMotion, the Oxford games studio behind CSR Racing, sold to Zynga for $527M in 2014. Path: Johannes Boie, Chief Marketing Officer and Communications; Anita Szarek, CFO; Niklas Köhler, President.

Opening angle

Lead with the talent war, not the logo.
“Torsten, you are hiring the same engineers Audi needs for Neuburg and Bicester, and no defence company has a seat on the grid. Audi's first season is being written now. 25 minutes to see how a Bavarian pairing would work?”
Bottom line
An $18B valuation, a Bundestag-approved €269M HX-2 contract with a €1.46B framework, and a hiring race against the primes give Helsing budget and motive at the same moment. Audi's debut roster has no defence or security partner, and the Bavarian pairing is the opening.

Intelligence Brief · Confidential
N° 224 · 07 MAY 2026
Intelligence Brief / N° 224 · HOT · F1

PayPal

Payments · Digital Wallets / Checkout · San Jose, California · NASDAQ: PYPL

PayPal named Antonio Lucio Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer on 29 April 2026, inside a reorganisation into three businesses under new CEO Enrique Lores, effective 2 June. Both men ran HP when it became Ferrari's title partner in 2024. A $33.2B-revenue payments brand has a Formula 1-literate top team.

The case

On 29 April PayPal announced a reorganisation into three operating units, Checkout Solutions & PayPal, Consumer Financial Services & Venmo, and Payment Services & Crypto, effective 2 June, with Antonio Lucio joining from HP as Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer and Diego Scotti departing. It is the first structural move by Enrique Lores, President and CEO since 1 March after six years running HP. The base is large: 2025 revenue of $33.2B, total payment volume of $1.79T and net income of $5.2B, reported on 3 February.

The pair have done this before. HP announced its multi-year title partnership with Ferrari on 24 April 2024 with Lores as CEO and Lucio as chief marketing and corporate affairs officer; the HP livery debuted at the Miami GP weeks later. PayPal already buys sports, a Phoenix Suns jersey patch since 2018 and the PayPal Park naming rights in San Jose, yet has nothing in Formula 1 while Visa, Mastercard and American Express do.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 29 April 2026 PayPal announced a strategic reorganisation into three operating units, Checkout Solutions & PayPal under Frank Keller, Consumer Financial Services & Venmo under Alexis Sowa (interim) and Payment Services & Crypto under Jeff Pomeroy (interim), effective 2 June. Antonio Lucio joins from HP as Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer and Anshu Bhardwaj becomes Chief AI Transformation & Simplification Officer; Diego Scotti and Michelle Gill leave.
A new CEO's first move
Enrique Lores became President and CEO on 1 March 2026 after six years running HP; the reorganisation is his first structural decision, taken inside sixty days, with a stated aim of getting closer to the consumer and simplifying how the company works. Brand rebuilds follow structures like this, and the executive who will run it arrives on 2 June.
The base
PayPal reported 2025 net revenue of $33.2B, up 4%, total payment volume of $1.79T, up 7%, and net income of $5.2B on 3 February 2026. It already spends on sport at scale: a Phoenix Suns jersey patch since 2018, extended through the 2026 NBA season, and the PayPal Park naming rights in San Jose.
Calendar window
From the 7 May row date the European rounds run from Monaco through Monza; the US GP and Las Vegas fall in the last quarter of the calendar. Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a conversation opened in May lands as Lucio takes the seat and can be announced at a US round.

Proof points — every figure checked against its source (see Sources)

$33.2B
Public: NASDAQ PYPL; 2025 revenue $33.2B (+4%), total payment volume $1.79T (+7%), net income $5.2B (result…

Why Scuderia Ferrari Hp — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Ferrari's roster carries HP as title partner and UniCredit, BingX, Vantage and AON on the finance side; there is no payments, wallet or checkout partner. Official Payments Partner is a clean category at the team with the largest global following.
The warm path
HP announced its multi-year Ferrari title partnership on 24 April 2024 with Enrique Lores as CEO and Antonio Lucio as Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer; the livery debuted at the Miami GP that May. The two executives now running PayPal have negotiated with Maranello's commercial team, sat in its hospitality and seen its fan-commerce numbers. That is a leadership tie of the warmest class.
A team that will use the product
Ferrari sells to fans directly: store, tickets, hospitality, esports. PayPal's checkout, Pay Later and Venmo are used in the transaction, not just shown on the car, which separates a payments partner from a logo.
Why not the US-first alternative
Cadillac's debut roster has no finance partner and PayPal is a San Jose company, so the American entry was weighed. It was not chosen: it has no relationship path, no comparable fan-commerce volume in year one, and the Ferrari tie is the asset the desk can activate now. Cadillac stays the fallback if Ferrari's board declines a payments partner.

Value To Scuderia Ferrari Hp — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
PayPal and Venmo as the checkout and wallet layer across Ferrari's online store, ticketing and hospitality bookings, with Pay Later offered on high-ticket merchandise and Venmo activated for the US fan base around the US GP and Las Vegas. Conversion and basket data shared under contract so the team can see what the partnership moves.
Commercial lift for the team
A partner with hundreds of millions of consumer accounts and a merchant network brings a US audience of small businesses, developers and enterprise clients to hospitality at the US rounds, alongside the HP programme's technology guests.
Content and ecosystem
A checkout-to-pit-wall story: how a race weekend's fan transactions run on PayPal, co-produced with Ferrari's digital team; Venmo social-payment moments around Miami and Las Vegas; Ferrari as a named enterprise reference for PayPal's merchant business.
What the team gives back
Official Payments Partner designation, rear-wing endplate or halo placement, integration rights across store and ticketing, US-round hospitality, and driver and garage access for PayPal and Venmo channels.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Payments Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, matching Lucio's brand-rebuild horizon. Estimated $8-12M a year, part in kind via checkout integration. Scope: rear-wing endplate or halo placement, checkout and wallet integration across store and ticketing, US-round hospitality, and a co-branded Pay Later and Venmo campaign around the US rounds.

The askA 25-minute call with Antonio Lucio in his first fortnight (2 June onward), opened through Enrique Lores or Frank Keller in May, to test appetite for a Ferrari payments partnership, agree a US-round announcement window, and size an Official Payments Partner entry against Ferrari's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Antonio Lucio
Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer, PayPal (from 2 June 2026) · verified
Lucio joins PayPal on 2 June from HP, where he was EVP and Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer when HP signed Ferrari; earlier CMO of Facebook. Path: Enrique Lores, President & CEO; Jamie Miller, Chief Financial and Operating Officer; Frank Keller, President, Checkout Solutions & PayPal.

Opening angle

Lead with the Ferrari relationship they already own.
“Antonio, you and Enrique put HP on the Ferrari; the payments lane on that same car is open, and Visa and Mastercard are already on the grid. 25 minutes before your 2 June start to see how PayPal takes it?”
Bottom line
A new CEO and CMO who signed Ferrari's title deal from HP, a reorganisation effective 2 June, $33.2B of revenue and a sports-sponsorship habit at NBA and MLS scale put PayPal at peak brand-investment authority. Ferrari's payments lane is open; Visa, Mastercard and American Express already race.

Intelligence Brief / N° 225 · HOT · F1

Hightouch

Marketing Technology · Customer Data Platform / AI Decisioning · San Francisco · Private ($2.75B; $150M Series D, Apr 2026)

San Francisco marketing-data company Hightouch announced a $150M Series D at a $2.75B valuation on 29 April 2026, led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives' growth arm and Bain Capital Ventures, more than doubling its price in fourteen months. Its buyers are chief marketing officers, the audience paddock hospitality was built for.

The case

Hightouch announced on 29 April that it had raised $150M in a Series D led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Bain Capital Ventures at a $2.75B valuation, with Iconiq, Sapphire Ventures, Amplify, Y Combinator and TD7, The Trade Desk's venture arm, participating; total funding is about $322M. Hightouch says revenue has grown more than 100% in each of the past two years, and names Domino's, PetSmart, DraftKings, Ramp and Whoop among customers. Its Series C, $80M at $1.2B led by Sapphire, closed in February 2025.

The product is a marketing data layer that reads a company's warehouse and pushes audiences to advertising, email and CRM tools, with AI agents deciding what each customer sees next. It is bought by marketing leaders, which makes the paddock a sales floor, not a billboard. Gartner named Hightouch a Leader in its 2025 Magic Quadrant for customer data platforms in January, and no team on the grid carries a partner in the category.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
Hightouch announced on 29 April 2026 a $150M Series D led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Bain Capital Ventures at a $2.75B valuation, with Iconiq, Sapphire Ventures, Amplify Partners, Y Combinator and TD7, The Trade Desk's venture arm, participating. Total funding is about $322M across six rounds. The release is the company's own, so the figures are announced, not reported.
Price more than doubled
The Series C of February 2025, $80M led by Sapphire Ventures, valued Hightouch at $1.2B. Fourteen months later the Series D priced it at $2.75B. Hightouch says revenue has grown more than 100% in each of the past two years; no revenue figure is public and none is used here.
Category leadership is being bought
Gartner named Hightouch a Leader in the 2025 Magic Quadrant for Customer Data Platforms (announced 29 January 2026). The company is investing to hold that position against Salesforce, Adobe and the warehouse vendors, and its buyers, chief marketing officers, are the people a Formula 1 partnership puts in a room.
Calendar window
From the 5 May row date the European rounds run from Monaco to Monza; the US GP and Las Vegas fall in the last quarter of the calendar. Teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter, so a conversation opened in May can be announced at a US round and activated in full for 2027.

Why Mclaren Mastercard F1 Team — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
McLaren's technology roster is the longest in the sponsor table: Google Cloud, Dell, Cisco, Splunk, Alteryx, Smartsheet, Medallia, Dropbox, Workday, Freshworks, Okta, Groq, Gemini and Rubrik. Salesforce, whose platform ran McLaren's fan-relationship programme, has departed. Nothing on the roster activates fan data into media, email and the store: Official Marketing Data Partner is a clean designation.
A stack to plug into
Hightouch reads a company's cloud data warehouse rather than copying the data into its own system; Google Cloud joined McLaren's roster this season, giving the programme a warehouse-side partner already in place.
A team that will use the product
McLaren's commercial machine is the most visible on the grid: a global fan base, a large store and a hospitality programme that is itself a marketing operation. Fan-data activation is consumed by the team's digital and commercial staff every week, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
The buyer audience
Hightouch sells to chief marketing officers. McLaren's partners are largely enterprise brands whose CMOs attend the races; a seat at the Paddock Club at the US GP and Las Vegas is a sales floor for Hightouch as much as a brand placement.

Value To Mclaren Mastercard F1 Team — Mode A · tech in the car / championship

Operational workstream (Mode A)
Audiences built from ticketing, store, app and content behaviour in McLaren's warehouse, pushed to paid media, email and the McLaren store, with AI decisioning choosing the next offer for each fan and measuring lift. The team funds no new data platform; Hightouch supplies the activation layer and the services to run it.
Commercial lift for the team
A measured increase in fan revenue per head across store, tickets and hospitality, reported quarterly, and a partner whose guest list is chief marketing officers, the audience McLaren's other B2B partners want in the suite.
Content and ecosystem
A co-authored annual fan-data report on how a Formula 1 team markets to its fans, McLaren as a named reference customer for Hightouch's enterprise sales, and engineering-to-marketing content that fits the team's technology positioning.
What the team gives back
Official Marketing Data Partner designation, mirror or engine-cover placement, integration rights across McLaren's fan-data estate, US-round hospitality, and driver access for Hightouch's customer events.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Marketing Data Partner. THREE YEARS, 2027-2029, covering the next raise and a probable listing window. Estimated $2-4M a year, part in kind via platform licence and services. Scope: mirror or engine-cover placement, a fan-data activation programme with McLaren's digital team, CMO hospitality at the US rounds, and a co-authored annual fan-data report.

The askA 25-minute call with Kashish Gupta and Tejas Manohar before Monaco to test appetite, agree how a fan-data activation programme would be measured, and size an Official Marketing Data Partner entry against McLaren's 2027 roster.

Primary decision-maker

Kashish Gupta
Co-Founder & Co-CEO, Hightouch · verified
Gupta co-founded Hightouch in 2018 and shares the CEO role with Tejas Manohar; a Wharton graduate and former Bessemer investor, he fronts the raises. Path: Tejas Manohar, Co-Founder & Co-CEO; Cherry Miao, CFO; Brian Kotlyar, VP Marketing & Growth. No chief marketing officer is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the buyer, not the badge.
“Kashish, your buyers are CMOs, and every one of them passes through a Formula 1 paddock. McLaren's fan-data lane opened when Salesforce left, and Google Cloud just arrived. 25 minutes before Monaco to see the numbers?”
Bottom line
A $150M Series D at $2.75B, revenue more than doubling for two years and a customer list that includes Whoop and DraftKings put Hightouch at peak brand-investment authority. McLaren's fan-data lane opened when Salesforce departed, and the buyers Hightouch needs are already in the paddock.

Glydways

Autonomous Transit · Personal Rapid Transit Networks · South San Francisco, California · Private (~$700M reported; $170M Series C, Apr 2026)

Glydways, the South San Francisco builder of on-demand autonomous transit networks, closed an oversubscribed $170M Series C co-led by Suzuki Motor Corporation, ACS Group and Khosla Ventures on 14 April 2026, as its first three public systems, in the UAE, greater New York and South Metro Atlanta, move toward passengers this year.

The case

On 14 April 2026 Glydways announced a $170M Series C co-led by Suzuki Motor Corporation, ACS Group and Khosla Ventures, with Mitsui Chemicals, Gates Frontier and new investor Obayashi Corporation; total funding exceeds $250M, and Bloomberg reported the round at almost $700M with talks for $250M more at $1B or above. The money is for going public in the literal sense: the South Metro Atlanta system broke ground in February and opens in December 2026, Dubai's RTA signed for a 2.8km pilot route, and Abu Dhabi's investment office is assessing a deployment. THE FIRST PASSENGERS RIDE THIS YEAR.

No autonomous-transit or mobility-network brand sits anywhere on the Formula E grid; the only autonomous-vehicle partner in either series is Zoox, at Williams in Formula 1. Formula E's works teams belong to carmakers, which matters when Suzuki co-led the round: Nissan, Porsche, Jaguar, Citroën, Cupra, DS and Mahindra each carry a rival badge. That leaves the independents, and one of them is American, with Miami and Austin on its next season's calendar.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 14 April 2026 Glydways announced an oversubscribed $170M Series C co-led by Suzuki Motor Corporation, ACS Group and Khosla Ventures, with Mitsui Chemicals and Gates Frontier returning and Obayashi Corporation new. Total funding now exceeds $250M. Bloomberg reported the round valued the company at almost $700M and that talks are under way for $250M more at $1B or above; those valuation figures are press-reported, not company-stated.
The first public passengers
The South Metro Atlanta demonstration pilot, built with ACS Infra, broke ground in February 2026 and is scheduled to open to the public in December 2026: a dedicated 0.5-mile guideway from the ATL SkyTrain at the Georgia International Convention Center to the Gateway Center Arena, the first Glydways system to run as public transportation anywhere. A company whose product the public has never ridden becomes, this year, one the public judges.
Two Gulf agreements
Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority signed with Glydways at the World Governments Summit in February 2026 to study initial routes, with a planned 2.8km pilot from National Paints Metro Station to Bluewaters Island. The Abu Dhabi Investment Office signed an interim agreement in November 2025 to assess a deployment in the capital. Gulf transport authorities are also Formula E's founding audience: Jeddah opens Season 13.
Calendar window
The Tokyo E-Prix on 25-26 July is the home race for three of Glydways' investors, Suzuki, Obayashi and Mitsui Chemicals, and falls inside the action horizon. Formula E's Season 13 rosters are agreed over the summer; the GEN4 era opens in Jeddah in December, and the Austin E-Prix on 6 February and Miami on 20 February 2027 are the US rounds closest to Glydways' Atlanta and New York pilots.

Why Andretti Formula E — the open lane, the audience, the platform

The open lane
Andretti's roster is Andretti Global, TWG Motorsports, TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo, with Porsche powertrain to the end of Season 12 and Nissan from Season 13. There is no mobility, transit or autonomy partner on it, and no such brand anywhere on the Formula E grid.
No carmaker clash
Suzuki co-led the round, and eight of the grid's teams are carmaker works entries or carry a carmaker's badge: Nissan, Porsche, Jaguar, Citroën, Cupra, DS, Mahindra and Lola Yamaha ABT. Andretti is an independent; a Suzuki-backed company can sit on its car without embarrassing anyone.
The American team with the American rounds
Andretti is the American entry in Formula E. Season 13 brings an Austin E-Prix on 6 February and Miami on 20 February 2027, the two rounds nearest Glydways' first public riders in Atlanta and its greater New York pilot, and Miami already ran in Season 12.
Why not the others
Envision Racing is the other independent and its sustainability identity fits, but it is UK-based with a Chinese parent and offers no US home story. Jaguar TCS Racing's autonomy-adjacent parent is a rival carmaker to an investor. The works teams are ruled out on the carmaker clash above.

Value To Andretti Formula E — Mode B · tech serves the team operation

The audience is the product (Mode B)
Glydways sells to city and regional governments. Formula E races on city streets by agreement with those same governments, and its paddock is where transport authorities, mayors and investment offices are hosted. A partnership buys Glydways the room: Tokyo for its Japanese investors, Jeddah for the Gulf agreements, Miami and Austin for the US pilots.
A working demonstration on the concourse
A branded Glydways pod on the E-Prix fan concourse, or a short on-demand shuttle between fan zones where the circuit allows, shows the product moving people rather than a logo on a car. Formula E's own pitch to host cities is driverless, electric, on-demand transit; Glydways is that pitch made physical.
Content the team cannot make alone
The Atlanta line's first public rides in December 2026, the Dubai and Abu Dhabi studies and the GEN4 launch give Andretti a season-long story about how cities will move, with drivers riding the pods and city officials on camera.
What the team gives back
Official Mobility Partner designation, livery and driver-suit placement, a pod demonstration at the US rounds, hospitality for city officials at Tokyo, Jeddah, Miami and Austin, and driver access for Glydways' public-launch communications.

Deal architecture

Entry as Official Mobility Partner. THREE YEARS, Seasons 13-15, tracking public operations from 2027. Estimated $1-2M a year, scaled to a Series C business. Scope: livery and driver-suit placement, a pod demonstration at Miami and Austin, city-official hospitality at Tokyo and Jeddah, and joint content around the Atlanta opening.

The askA 25-minute call with Gokul Hemmady and Chris Riley before the Tokyo E-Prix to test the city-official hospitality model, agree a Season 13 entry against Andretti's roster, and set the Atlanta opening as the first activation.

Primary decision-maker

Gokul Hemmady
CEO, Glydways · verified
Hemmady joined Glydways in 2019 as President and CFO and now runs it as CEO; a first sports partnership is his sign-off. Path: Chris Riley, Chief Commercial Officer, ex-Ogilvy Singapore chairman, owns partnerships and corporate reputation; Mark Seeger, Founder and Chief Strategy Officer. No CMO is listed.

Opening angle

Lead with the cities, not the cars.
“Gokul, Formula E races on the streets of the cities you sell to, and no transit brand is on its grid. Andretti is the American team, with Miami and Austin next season. 25 minutes on how the pod meets the paddock?”
Bottom line
A $170M Series C, first public passengers in Atlanta by December and live agreements in Dubai and Abu Dhabi make 2026 the year Glydways needs a public face. Formula E races in the cities it sells to, no transit brand is on the grid, and Andretti is the American team with Miami and Austin next season.

Defence Technology · Autonomous Maritime Vessels / Shipbuilding · Austin, Texas · Private ($9.25B; $1.75B Series D, Mar 2026)

Saronic, the Austin-based builder of autonomous naval vessels, closed a $1.75B Series D led by Kleiner Perkins at a $9.25B post-money valuation on 31 March 2026, more than doubling its price in a year, with the capital pointed at shipyards: a $300M Louisiana expansion and Port Alpha, then choosing its site.

The case

On 31 March 2026 Saronic announced a $1.75B Series D led by Kleiner Perkins at a $9.25B post-money valuation, with Advent International, Bessemer Venture Partners, DFJ Growth and BAM Elevate joining 8VC, Caffeinated Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Elad Gil and Franklin Templeton; a $600M Series C had valued it at $4B in 2025. In December the US Navy awarded a $392M production contract for its 24-foot Corsair, prototype to production in under 12 months. Franklin, Louisiana is adding 300,000 square feet and 1,500 jobs; Port Alpha targets 20-plus vessels a year by 2027. AMERICAN SHIPBUILDING, REBUILT FROM TEXAS.

No defence, maritime-autonomy or shipbuilding brand sits on the Formula 1 grid; the nearest adjacencies are Boeing at Alpine and Zoox at Williams, and neither conflicts. The question is not a category clash but which team's identity a US Navy supplier can stand behind. Two teams are American: one a privateer built around machine tools, the other a General Motors works entry in its first season with a manufacturing campus rising in Indiana.

Why now — the clock this signal is on

Trigger
On 31 March 2026 Saronic announced a $1.75B Series D led by Kleiner Perkins at a $9.25B post-money valuation, with Advent International, Bessemer Venture Partners, DFJ Growth and BAM Elevate joining 8VC, Caffeinated Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Elad Gil and Franklin Templeton. A $600M Series C had valued the company at $4B in 2025, so the price more than doubled in about a year.
Production, not prototypes
In December 2025 the US Navy awarded Saronic a $392M production contract for the 24-foot Corsair, announced at the Reagan National Defense Forum, with the Navy Secretary citing prototype to production in under 12 months. The same month Saronic announced a $300M expansion of its Franklin, Louisiana shipyard, adding more than 300,000 square feet and 1,500 jobs, where the 180-foot Marauder is built.
Port Alpha
The Series D capital is earmarked for shipbuilding capacity: Port Alpha, a planned Texas shipyard expected to build more than 20 autonomous surface vessels a year by 2027 and create 10,000 direct jobs over a decade. On this row's date the site was still being selected; Saronic announced Brownsville, Texas, on 16 July 2026. A company choosing where to put 10,000 jobs is in a season of governors, senators and public ceremonies, which is also the audience a US Grand Prix suite holds.
Calendar window
The Miami GP ran on 3 May 2026, two days before this row. The United States GP in Austin in late October is Saronic's home race, and Cadillac settles its 2027 partner roster between the summer break and Austin. A deal agreed by July can be announced at home.

Saronic brings Navy leadership, members of Congress, state officials and defence-industrial executives to the Austin, Miami and Las Vegas suites, an American power audience Cadillac's first-season hospitality is built to host.
